  priority_date date [note: 'The legally established date that determines the seniority of this water right relative to other rights on the same water source. Under prior appropriation doctrine, earlier priority dates have superior claim during shortage conditions. Critical for western-state water allocation compliance.']
  record_created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this water right record was first created in the system. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and Silver layer ingestion tracking in the Databricks Lakehouse.']
  record_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this water right record was most recently modified. Supports change detection, incremental processing, and audit trail requirements in the Databricks Lakehouse Silver layer.']
  right_type varchar [note: 'Legal classification of the water right doctrine under which the entitlement is held. Surface rights derive from surface water bodies; groundwater rights pertain to aquifer extraction; riparian rights attach to land adjacent to a water body; appropriative rights follow prior appropriation doctrine (first-in-time, first-in-right) common in western US states; prescriptive rights arise from long-term use. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: surface|groundwater|riparian|appropriative|prescriptive|adjudicated — promote to reference product if additional types are needed]']
  season_end_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which authorized water diversion or use must cease each year under seasonal restrictions of the permit. Null if the right has no seasonal restriction.']
  season_start_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which authorized water diversion or use may begin each year under seasonal restrictions of the permit. Null if the right has no seasonal restriction.']
  source_water_body varchar [note: 'Name of the surface water body (river, stream, canal, reservoir, lake) or groundwater basin from which water is authorized to be diverted or extracted. Required for source identification in regulatory filings and environmental monitoring.']
  source_water_body_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the water source type. Distinguishes surface water sources (river, stream, canal, reservoir, lake, spring) from groundwater sources (aquifer) for regulatory categorization and environmental impact assessment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: river|stream|canal|reservoir|lake|spring|aquifer — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  transfer_date date [note: 'The date on which ownership or appurtenance of this water right was most recently transferred to the current holder. Null if no transfer has occurred. Supports transfer history tracking and chain-of-title documentation.']
  water_district varchar [note: 'Name of the irrigation district, water conservation district, or water management area within which this water right is administered. Relevant for district-level allocation, assessment fees, and delivery scheduling.']
  water_right_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the water right. Existence Justification: In agricultural operations, a farm unit actively approves and manages multiple vendors for input supply (seed, fertilizer, agrochemicals, fuel), and a single vendor supplies inputs to multiple farm units across a region or enterprise. This is not an analytical correlation — procurement teams explicitly create, maintain, and expire farm-unit-level vendor approvals with farm-specific pricing agreements, approved input categories, and validity periods. The relationship is operationally managed as a \'Vendor Approval\' or \'Supply Agreement\' record that procurement and farm managers actively govern.'

Belongs to the relationship — the same account may be a tenant on one field and a custom operator on another.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the operational role relationship between a field and a customer account. It captures who operates a given field, in what capacity, and for what period — supporting FSA farm records, crop insurance operator declarations, lease management, and custom farming billing. Each record links one field to one account with a specific operator role and effective date range. A field may have multiple simultaneous records (e.g., one landowner + one tenant + one custom operator), and one account may have many such records across its entire field portfolio.. Existence Justification: In agricultural operations, a single field can be simultaneously operated by multiple accounts in different capacities — a landowner account holds title, a cash-rent tenant account farms the ground, and a custom operator account may perform specific operations (e.g., harvesting). Conversely, one account (e.g., a large farming operation or custom operator) manages many fields across multiple farm units. The business actively tracks these operator relationships for FSA farm records, crop insurance eligibility, and operational billing — this is not a derived correlation but an actively managed operational record.'
}

Table land.field_input_restriction {
  field_input_restriction_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the field_input_restriction association']
  field_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the agricultural field or paddock on which the input restriction applies']
  input_product_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the agricultural input product that is restricted on the associated field']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date from which this field-input restriction is considered active and operationally enforced. Typically aligned with the start of an organic certification period, conservation contract enrollment date, or regulatory advisory issuance date.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'The date on which this restriction lapses or is no longer applicable. May be null for indefinite restrictions. Examples: expiry of organic certification, end of FSA conservation contract term, or lifting of a groundwater advisory.']
  is_active boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this restriction is currently in force. Derived from effective_date and expiry_date but maintained as an explicit operational flag to support fast compliance queries during application planning and spray record generation.']
  regulatory_basis varchar [note: 'The regulatory or policy authority underpinning this restriction. Drives compliance reporting and audit trail. Aligned with USDA NOP, EPA FIFRA, and FSA program requirements.']
  restriction_reason varchar [note: 'Human-readable explanation of why this input product is restricted on this field. Examples: \'Organic certification prohibits synthetic inputs\', \'Groundwater advisory — sandy soil over aquifer recharge zone\', \'FSA conservation contract CRP enrollment\', \'GMO-restricted field boundary\'.']
  restriction_type varchar [note: 'Classification of how the input product is restricted on this field. \'prohibited\' means no application permitted; \'rate_limited\' means application is allowed below a maximum rate; \'buffer_zone_only\' means application is excluded within a defined distance of a waterway or boundary; \'timing_restricted\' means application is only permitted outside certain windows (e.g., pre-planting only); \'conditional\' means restriction applies only under specific conditions.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the regulatory and operational restriction Contract between a field and an agricultural input product. It captures the specific restriction governing whether and how a given input product may be applied to a given field, driven by organic certification, groundwater advisories, conservation program enrollment, GMO restrictions, or other regulatory requirements. Each record links one field to one input_product and carries the restriction type, regulatory basis, effective period, and reason — data that exists only in the context of this specific field-product pairing.. Existence Justification: In agricultural operations, a field can have multiple input product restrictions simultaneously (e.g., an organic-certified field restricts all synthetic pesticides, while a field near a waterway restricts specific herbicides, and a conservation-enrolled field restricts certain soil amendments). Conversely, a single input product (e.g., a restricted-use herbicide) is restricted on many different fields across the farm for different regulatory reasons. The business actively manages these restrictions — creating, updating, and expiring them — as a compliance and operational control mechanism with its own regulatory basis, effective dates, and restriction type.'
}

Existence Justification: In agricultural operations, a single field genuinely holds multiple simultaneous certifications (e.g., USDA Organic + GlobalG.A.P. + Rainforest Alliance applied to the same paddock at the same time), and a single certification (e.g., a farm-level USDA Organic certificate) covers multiple fields within that farm unit. This is not an analytical derivation; it is an operational record that auditors, certification bodies, and farm managers create, update, and query directly.'

  depreciation_method varchar [note: 'Accounting method used to calculate periodic depreciation of the asset. Straight-line spreads cost evenly; declining balance accelerates early depreciation; units of production ties depreciation to actual usage hours. Configured in SAP S/4HANA FI/AM.']

  operational_status varchar [note: 'Current operational readiness status of the asset indicating whether it is available for field deployment. Business justification: Telematics readings are streamed continuously from equipment during field operations. telematics_reading has asset_id, field_id, and vra_prescription_id but no FK to the specific field_operation conte']
  field_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the agricultural field or land parcel where the equipment was operating at the time of the reading. Supports field coverage monitoring and VRA audit trails.']

Direct FK to input_product enables automated label compliance monitoring — comparing actual application rate against m']

  load_weight_kg decimal(10,2) [note: 'Weight of the load carried by the equipment (e.g., grain in combine hopper, fertilizer in applicator) in kilograms at the time of the reading. Supports yield estimation, logistics planning, and axle load compliance.']
  longitude double [note: 'RTK-corrected WGS84 longitude coordinate of the equipment at the time of the reading, in decimal degrees. Supports fleet position tracking, field coverage monitoring, geofence evaluation, and theft detection.']
  ndvi_reading decimal(5,4) [note: 'Normalized Difference Vegetation Index value captured by the onboard crop sensor at the time of the reading, ranging from -1.0 to 1.0. Supports variable rate application (VRA) decisions, crop health monitoring, and precision agriculture analytics.']
  operational_status varchar [note: 'Current operational state of the equipment at the time of the reading. Drives OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) calculation by classifying time into productive, transport, idle, and parked categories. EVENT_PAYLOAD_OR_VALUE per EVENT_LOG role minimum.']
  pto_engaged boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the Power Take-Off (PTO) shaft was engaged at the time of the reading. PTO engagement signals active implement operation (e.g., mower, spreader, pump) and is used for productive-time classification in OEE calculations.']
  pto_rpm varchar [note: 'Power Take-Off shaft speed in revolutions per minute at the time of the reading when PTO is engaged. Used to verify correct implement operating speed and diagnose PTO-related faults.']
  reading_quality_flag varchar [note: 'Data quality classification for this telemetry record assigned during Silver layer ingestion. \'Valid\' records are used in analytics; \'suspect\' records require review; \'invalid\' records are excluded from reporting. Supports data governance and AI/ML feature engineering.']
  reading_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise UTC timestamp when the telemetry event was recorded by the equipment\'s onboard controller. EVENT_TIMESTAMP per EVENT_LOG role minimum. Distinct from ingestion audit timestamps.']
  rtk_correction_status varchar [note: 'Quality indicator for the GPS/RTK positional correction applied at the time of the reading. \'Fixed\' indicates sub-inch accuracy; \'float\' and \'dgps\' indicate degraded precision. Critical for VRA prescription audit trails and auto-steer accuracy validation.']
  signal_strength_dbm decimal(6,2) [note: 'Cellular or satellite communication signal strength in decibel-milliwatts (dBm) at the time of the reading. Supports data quality assessment, connectivity gap analysis, and telematics infrastructure planning.']
  transmission_delay_ms varchar [note: 'Latency in milliseconds between the equipment recording the telemetry event and the data being received by the cloud platform. Supports data quality scoring and near-real-time fleet dashboard reliability assessment.']

  Note: 'High-frequency telemetry records streamed from John Deere Operations Center, Trimble, and other IoT-enabled agricultural equipment. Captures machine hours, engine RPM, fuel consumption rate, ground speed, PTO engagement, hydraulic pressure, GPS coordinates (RTK-corrected latitude/longitude), heading, NDVI sensor readings, implement depth/width, load weight, fault codes (DTC), operational status (field working/transport/idle/parked), geofence zone, RTK correction status, field boundary match flag, data source identifier, and timestamp. SSOT for all equipment telemetry including fleet position tracking — latest-reading queries provide current fleet position for dispatch dashboards, field coverage monitoring, theft detection, and operator hours-of-service compliance (replacing standalone fleet_position). Supports OEE calculation, predictive maintenance triggers, precision agriculture VRA audit trails, and fleet dispatch. One record per telemetry event per asset.'
}

  is_warranty_claim boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this fault has been submitted or is eligible for a manufacturer warranty claim.   last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to the fault record in the source system. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED field for change tracking, incremental data pipeline processing, and audit trail compliance in the Databricks silver layer.']
  maintenance_team varchar [note: 'Name or code of the maintenance team or work center responsible for resolving this fault, as assigned in SAP PM. Examples: internal_fleet_team, dealer_service, oem_field_technician. Supports workload balancing and maintenance team performance KPI reporting.']
  odometer_km_at_fault decimal(10,1) [note: 'Total cumulative distance in kilometers recorded on the equipment odometer at the time of fault, as reported by telematics. Applicable to mobile equipment (tractors, combines, sprayers). Used alongside engine hours for condition-based maintenance scheduling and warranty claims.']
  recurrence_count varchar [note: 'Number of times this same fault (same DTC code or fault category on the same asset) has recurred within the current operating season. A value greater than 1 indicates a recurring fault pattern requiring escalated RCM investigation. Supports chronic failure identification and maintenance strategy optimization.']
  resolution_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the fault was confirmed as resolved and the equipment returned to full operational service. Distinct from downtime_end_timestamp (which marks when equipment restarted) — resolution_timestamp marks formal closure confirmation in SAP PM. Used for mean time to repair (MTTR) calculations.']
  root_cause_code varchar [note: 'Standardized root cause classification code assigned after fault investigation, aligned with SAP PM cause catalog and ISO 14224 failure taxonomy. Examples: wear_and_tear, improper_maintenance, manufacturing_defect, operator_misuse, environmental_damage, age_related_failure. Used for RCM analysis and preventive maintenance optimization. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: wear_and_tear|improper_maintenance|manufacturing_defect|operator_misuse|environmental_damage|age_related_failure|unknown — promote to reference product]']
  root_cause_description varchar [note: 'Free-text narrative describing the identified root cause of the fault following investigation. Complements root_cause_code with detailed findings from the technician or maintenance engineer. Supports knowledge base development and recurring fault prevention.']
  severity_level varchar [note: 'Severity classification of the fault indicating operational impact and urgency of corrective action. Critical = immediate equipment stoppage; High = significant performance degradation; Medium = reduced efficiency; Low = minor issue, can continue operating. Drives maintenance prioritization and OEE availability calculations.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Identifies the operational system of record from which this fault record originated. SAP_PM = SAP S/4HANA Plant Maintenance notification; JD_OPS_CENTER = John Deere Operations Center telematics alert; TRIMBLE = Trimble Ag Software field report; MANUAL = manually entered; CLIMATE_FIELDVIEW = Climate FieldView event. Supports data lineage and silver layer reconciliation.']
  yield_impact_bu decimal(12,2) [note: 'Estimated yield loss in bushels (BU) attributable to the equipment downtime caused by this fault. Calculated based on acres lost and expected yield per acre (YPM). Supports crop loss reporting, insurance claims, and financial impact assessment. BU (Bushel) is the standard grain yield unit per USDA WASDE reporting.']

  Note: 'Record of equipment faults, breakdowns, and diagnostic trouble codes (DTC) detected via telematics or reported by operators. Captures fault code, fault description, severity level, detection source (telematics/operator/inspection), asset affected, field/location at time of fault, downtime start/end, estimated production impact (acres lost, yield impact), root cause classification, and corrective action taken. Feeds into OEE availability calculations and reliability-centered maintenance (RCM) analysis.'
}

  growing_season_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the growing season or crop year during which this OEE record was captured. Enables seasonal fleet performance trending and year-over-year OEE benchmarking aligned with crop planning cycles.']

Contract performance reporting uses OEE availability and throughput data to validate whether equipment ']

Linking oee_record to the concurrent weathe']
  acceptable_output_quantity decimal(14,4) [note: 'Quantity of output meeting quality standards during the measurement period. Used as the numerator for quality rate calculation. For harvesting equipment, represents grain meeting grade standards; for sprayers, represents correctly applied area.']
  actual_operating_time_min varchar [note: 'Total minutes the asset was actively operating (engine running and performing work) during the measurement period, as recorded by John Deere Operations Center telematics. Equals planned production time minus unplanned downtime.']

  availability_rate decimal(5,4) [note: 'Ratio of actual operating time to planned production time, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.9250 = 92.50%). Calculated as (Planned Production Time - Unplanned Downtime) / Planned Production Time. One of the three OEE component rates.']
  breakdown_count varchar [note: 'Number of unplanned equipment breakdowns (failures requiring corrective maintenance work orders) that occurred during the measurement period. Drives unplanned downtime and is a key input to MTBF calculation.']

  data_source varchar [note: 'Operational system of record from which the OEE measurement data was sourced. Supports data lineage tracking and audit trail for Silver Layer ingestion. Primary source is John Deere Operations Center telematics; secondary sources include SAP S/4HANA PM and manual entry.']
  engine_hours decimal(8,2) [note: 'Total engine operating hours accumulated by the asset during the measurement period, as reported by John Deere Operations Center telematics. Used for preventive maintenance scheduling and asset lifecycle tracking per ISO 55000.']
  fuel_consumption_gallons decimal(10,3) [note: 'Total fuel consumed by the asset during the measurement period in US gallons, as reported by John Deere Operations Center telematics. Used for OPEX cost allocation, fuel efficiency benchmarking, and environmental reporting.']
  gps_tracking_enabled boolean [note: 'Indicates whether GPS/RTK precision positioning was active on the asset during this measurement period. When true, telematics data (acres covered, field boundaries) is sourced from John Deere Operations Center GPS telemetry; when false, data may be manually entered.']
  idle_time_min varchar [note: 'Total minutes the asset engine was running but not performing productive work (idling) during the measurement period. Captured via John Deere Operations Center telematics. Contributes to performance loss analysis and fuel waste identification.']
  measurement_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which this OEE measurement was recorded. Used for daily and shift-level fleet performance trending and CAPEX justification reporting.']
  measurement_end_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time when the OEE measurement period ended (shift or day end). Combined with start timestamp to derive total measurement window duration.']
  measurement_period_type varchar [note: 'Granularity of the OEE measurement period: shift-level (per operational shift), daily (24-hour calendar day), or weekly (7-day rolling). Determines aggregation level for KPI reporting.']
  measurement_start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time when the OEE measurement period began (shift or day start). Used for granular telematics alignment with John Deere Operations Center data.']
  minor_stoppage_count varchar [note: 'Number of brief, unplanned stoppages (typically under 10 minutes each) that did not trigger a formal work order but contributed to performance rate loss during the measurement period. Sourced from John Deere Operations Center telematics event data.']
  oee_benchmark_target decimal(5,4) [note: 'The benchmark OEE target percentage (as a decimal) defined for the asset category (e.g., 0.8500 = 85% for combines). Sourced from asset category reference data. Used to assess performance gap and trigger CAPEX replacement reviews.']
  oee_percentage decimal(5,4) [note: 'Composite OEE score expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.7906 = 79.06%), calculated as Availability Rate × Performance Rate × Quality Rate. Primary KPI for fleet performance management and CAPEX justification for equipment replacement per ISO 55000.']
  oee_variance decimal(5,4) [note: 'Difference between actual OEE percentage and the benchmark target (oee_percentage minus oee_benchmark_target), expressed as a signed decimal. Negative values indicate underperformance; used to prioritize maintenance interventions and CAPEX reviews.']
  operation_type varchar [note: 'Type of agricultural operation the equipment was performing during the measurement period. Enables OEE benchmarking by operation type (e.g., combine OEE during harvesting vs. transport). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: planting|spraying|harvesting|tillage|irrigation|fertilization|transport|other — promote to reference product]']
  output_unit varchar [note: 'Unit of measure for total and acceptable output quantity fields. Aligned with asset type and crop/operation context. Examples: acres for field coverage, bushels (BU) or metric tons (MT) for harvested grain, gallons for applied inputs.']
  performance_rate decimal(5,4) [note: 'Ratio of actual throughput to theoretical maximum throughput during operating time, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.8800 = 88.00%). Captures speed losses and minor stoppages. One of the three OEE component rates.']
  planned_downtime_min varchar [note: 'Total minutes of scheduled downtime during the measurement period for preventive maintenance (PM), calibration, operator breaks, or planned changeovers. Excluded from planned production time per OEE methodology.']
  planned_production_time_min varchar [note: 'Total scheduled operating time in minutes for the asset during the measurement period, excluding planned maintenance windows and scheduled breaks. Denominator for availability rate calculation per OEE methodology.']
  quality_rate decimal(5,4) [note: 'Ratio of acceptable output (meeting quality standards) to total output produced during the measurement period, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.9700 = 97.00%). Captures quality losses such as crop damage or mis-application. One of the three OEE component rates.']
  record_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known business identifier for this OEE measurement record, formatted as OEE-YYYY-MM-DD-XXXXXX. Used for cross-system referencing between SAP S/4HANA PM and John Deere Operations Center.']
  record_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the OEE record: draft (data being collected), confirmed (data validated by system), approved (reviewed by fleet manager), voided (record invalidated due to data quality issues).']
  theoretical_throughput_rate decimal(10,4) [note: 'The ideal or nameplate throughput rate of the asset under optimal conditions (e.g., acres per hour for a combine, gallons per minute for a sprayer). Used as the denominator for performance rate calculation.']
  throughput_unit varchar [note: 'Unit of measure for throughput rate fields (theoretical and actual), aligned with the asset type and operation. Examples: acres_per_hour for planters/combines, gallons_per_min for sprayers, bushels_per_hour for grain handling equipment.']
  total_acres_covered decimal(10,2) [note: 'Total land area covered by the equipment during the measurement period, in acres, as recorded by GPS/RTK telematics from John Deere Operations Center. Key operational metric for field coverage efficiency and fuel cost allocation.']
  total_output_quantity decimal(14,4) [note: 'Total quantity of output produced by the asset during the measurement period (e.g., total acres covered, total bushels harvested, total gallons applied). Includes both acceptable and rejected/defective output.']
  unplanned_downtime_min varchar [note: 'Total minutes of unplanned equipment downtime during the measurement period due to breakdowns, failures, or unexpected stoppages. Key input to availability rate and MTBF/MTTR analysis per ISO 55000.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this OEE record was last modified in the Silver Layer data product. Used to detect late-arriving telematics data corrections from John Deere Operations Center and track record revision history.']
  work_center_code varchar [note: 'Reference to the SAP S/4HANA work center or operational unit (farm site, field zone, processing facility) where the equipment was deployed during this OEE measurement period.']

  Note: 'Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) measurement records calculated per asset per operational shift or day. Captures availability rate (planned vs. actual uptime), performance rate (actual vs. theoretical throughput), quality rate (acceptable output vs. total output), composite OEE percentage, planned production time, unplanned downtime minutes, planned downtime minutes, total acres covered, and benchmark OEE target from asset category. Supports fleet performance management, CAPEX justification for equipment replacement, and operational efficiency KPI reporting aligned with ISO 55000.'
}

  component_code varchar [note: 'OEM-defined code identifying the specific component, assembly, or sub-system that is the subject of the warranty claim (e.g., engine, transmission, hydraulic pump, GPS/RTK receiver, VRA controller).']
  component_description varchar [note: 'Human-readable description of the component, part, or assembly being claimed under warranty. Complements the component_code for reporting and communication with dealers and OEMs.']
  cost_center_code varchar [note: 'SAP cost center code to which the warranty claim costs and recoveries are allocated for financial reporting and CAPEX/OPEX management. Supports cost center-level warranty cost recovery analysis.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when the warranty claim record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code applicable to all monetary amounts on this warranty claim (claimed_repair_cost, approved_repair_cost, reimbursement_amount). Supports multi-currency operations for international equipment procurement.']
  dispute_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the warranty claim has been formally disputed with the OEM or dealer following an initial rejection or partial approval. True when a dispute has been raised; False otherwise.']
  dispute_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes documenting the basis for disputing a rejected or partially approved warranty claim, including supporting evidence references and escalation actions taken with the OEM or dealer.']
  downtime_hours decimal(8,1) [note: 'Total number of hours the equipment asset was out of service due to the failure covered by this warranty claim. Used for Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) impact analysis and operational loss quantification.']
  failure_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which the equipment failure or defect was first observed or reported in the field. Used to determine warranty coverage eligibility relative to purchase date and warranty period.']
  failure_description varchar [note: 'Detailed narrative description of the equipment failure, defect symptoms, and observed conditions at the time of failure. Supports OEM adjudication and root cause analysis.']
  failure_hours decimal(10,1) [note: 'Total engine/operational hours recorded on the asset at the time of failure. Critical for warranty eligibility determination based on hour-based warranty thresholds and for OEM reliability analysis.']
  labor_cost_claimed decimal(14,2) [note: 'The labor cost component of the total claimed repair cost submitted to the OEM or dealer. Enables granular cost breakdown analysis for warranty cost recovery and labor rate benchmarking.']
  oem_case_reference varchar [note: 'The case or claim reference number assigned by the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) or authorized dealer upon receipt of the warranty claim submission. Used for tracking claim status with the OEM.']
  parts_cost_claimed decimal(14,2) [note: 'The parts and materials cost component of the total claimed repair cost submitted to the OEM or dealer. Supports parts cost recovery tracking and procurement reliability analysis by component.']
  payment_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which the OEM or dealer issued the reimbursement payment for the approved warranty claim. Used for accounts receivable reconciliation and warranty cost recovery tracking.']
  reimbursement_amount decimal(14,2) [note: 'The actual monetary amount received from the OEM or dealer as reimbursement for the approved warranty claim. Populated upon payment confirmation. Used for CAPEX/OPEX cost recovery reconciliation.']
  rejection_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which the OEM or dealer formally rejected the warranty claim. Populated only when claim_status is \'rejected\'. Used for dispute tracking and procurement reliability analysis.']
  rejection_reason varchar [note: 'Reason code provided by the OEM or dealer for rejecting the warranty claim. Informs dispute resolution and procurement decisions on equipment reliability. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: out_of_warranty|operator_misuse|improper_maintenance|cosmetic_damage|no_defect_found|documentation_incomplete|other — promote to reference product if additional reasons are required]']
  repair_completed_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which the warranty repair was completed and the asset was returned to service. Used to calculate total repair cycle time and asset availability metrics.']
  serial_number_component varchar [note: 'Serial number of the specific failed component or part, where available. Supports traceability for batch/lot defect analysis and OEM recall investigations.']
  submission_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which the warranty claim was formally submitted to the dealer or OEM manufacturer. Used to calculate claim processing lead times and warranty filing compliance.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when the warranty claim record was most recently modified. Supports change tracking, audit trail requirements, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks Silver Layer.']
  warranty_expiry_date date [note: 'The date on which the applicable warranty coverage for the asset or component expires. Used to validate warranty eligibility at the time of claim submission and for proactive warranty utilization planning.']
  warranty_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the warranty coverage type under which the claim is filed. Determines applicable coverage terms, reimbursement rates, and OEM adjudication rules. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: standard|extended|powertrain|precision_ag_hardware|emissions — promote to reference product if additional types are required]']

  Note: 'Records of warranty claims submitted to equipment manufacturers or dealers for defective parts, premature failures, or manufacturing defects. Captures claim number, asset reference, part/component claimed, failure description, failure date, hours at failure, dealer/manufacturer claim submission date, claim status (submitted/approved/rejected/paid), approved repair cost, reimbursement amount received, and OEM case reference. Supports warranty cost recovery tracking and informs procurement decisions on equipment reliability.'
}

  Note: 'This association product represents the Contract between an agricultural equipment asset and a customer account in custom hire operations. It captures the formal service engagement whereby a specific piece of equipment is contracted to a specific customer account for a defined period and scope of work. Each record links one asset to one account and carries the contractual terms (acreage, rate, service type) and operational performance data that exist only in the context of this specific asset-customer engagement.. Existence Justification: In agricultural custom hire operations, a single piece of equipment (e.g., a combine harvester) is contracted out to multiple customer accounts across a season, and a single customer account may contract multiple assets (combine, grain cart, tractor, sprayer) for their farming operations. The business actively manages these service contracts with specific terms including contracted acreage, hourly rates, service type, and performance tracking — this is a recognized operational concept called a \'Custom Hire Contract\' or \'Equipment Service Agreement\' that humans create, update, and close throughout the crop season.'

Table equipment.parts_issue {
  parts_issue_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the parts_issue association']
  parts_inventory_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking this parts issue line to the specific spare part or consumable record in the MRO inventory master.']
  work_order_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking this parts issue line to the parent maintenance work order that consumed the part.']
  issue_date date [note: 'Calendar date on which the part was physically drawn from the warehouse and issued to the work order. Belongs to the issue event, not to the work order header (which has planned/actual start dates) or the inventory master.']
  line_number varchar [note: 'Sequential line number of this parts issue record within the work order, matching the SAP PM component line or Maximo material usage line number. Enables ordering and referencing of individual parts lines on a work order.']
  parts_cost decimal(14,2) [note: 'Total monetary cost of spare parts and materials consumed against the work order, aggregated from embedded parts consumption line items. Supports OPEX cost tracking and inventory replenishment analysis. Maps to SAP MM goods issue cost (DMBTR) settled to the work order. [Moved from work_order: The work_order.parts_cost is a derived aggregate (sum of all parts issue line costs) and should be computed from parts_issue records rather than stored redundantly on the work order header. If retained on work_order for performance, it should be treated as a calculated/denormalized field, not a source-of-truth attribute. The authoritative per-part cost data lives in the parts_issue association.]']
  quantity_issued decimal [note: 'Actual quantity of the part issued from inventory to the work order, expressed in the part\'s base unit of measure. Belongs to the issue event, not to the work order header or the inventory master.']
  reservation_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of this material reservation/issue line: planned (on work order plan, not yet reserved), reserved (stock reserved but not yet drawn), issued (physically drawn from warehouse), partially_issued (partial quantity drawn), returned (unused quantity returned to stock), cancelled (line removed from work order). Drives inventory availability calculations and OPEX accruals.']
  return_quantity decimal [note: 'Quantity of the part returned to inventory after work order completion (unused material). Drives inventory replenishment recalculation and OPEX cost adjustment.']
  unit_cost_at_issue decimal [note: 'Unit cost of the part at the time of issue, captured from the inventory valuation at issue date. Differs from the current unit_cost on parts_inventory due to price fluctuations; belongs to this issue event for accurate historical OPEX costing.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Parts Issue (Material Reservation) event between work_order and parts_inventory. It captures each line-item-level consumption of a spare part or consumable against a specific maintenance work order, as recorded in the CMMS (SAP PM goods issue / IBM Maximo material usage). Each record links one work_order to one parts_inventory item and carries the quantity issued, unit cost at time of issue, issue date, reservation status, and return quantity — data that exists only in the context of this specific work-order-to-part consumption event. Serves as the SSOT for actual material consumption supporting OPEX cost tracking, inventory replenishment triggers, and maintenance cost analysis by asset and crop enterprise.. Existence Justification: In agricultural CMMS operations, a single work order consumes multiple spare parts from inventory (e.g., a combine harvester repair may require an air filter, hydraulic seal, and drive belt simultaneously), and each part number is consumed across many different work orders over time. This is a textbook operational M:N: the \'parts issue\' or \'material reservation\' is a well-established CMMS business concept actively created, updated, and closed by maintenance planners and technicians. The relationship carries its own data — quantity issued, unit cost at time of issue, issue date, reservation status, and return quantity — none of which belong solely to the work order header or the parts inventory master.'
}

Table equipment.maintenance_plan_bom {
  maintenance_plan_bom_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the maintenance_plan_bom association']

  estimated_cost decimal [note: 'Estimated cost of the required quantity of this part for one cycle of the maintenance plan, expressed in the plan\'s currency. Calculated as required_quantity × unit_cost at plan authoring time. Contributes to the maintenance_plan.estimated_parts_cost rollup but is tracked at line-item level here.']
  estimated_parts_cost decimal(12,2) [note: 'Estimated total cost of parts and materials required to complete one cycle of this maintenance plan, in the base currency. Used for OPEX budgeting and procurement planning in SAP MM. [Moved from maintenance_plan: This is a rolled-up aggregate of all part line costs in the BOM. The authoritative line-item costs now live in the association (estimated_cost per plan-part combination). The rollup can be derived by summing association records, making the denormalized field on maintenance_plan redundant. If retained on maintenance_plan, it should be treated as a computed/cached field, not a source of truth.]']
  is_mandatory boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this part is mandatory for plan execution (true) or optional/conditional based on inspection findings (false). A mandatory part must be staged before the work order can be released; an optional part is staged on-demand.']
  line_number varchar [note: 'Sequential line number of this part within the maintenance plan BOM, used for display ordering and reference in work order printouts and CMMS integrations. Assigned by the maintenance planner at BOM authoring time.']
  part_role varchar [note: 'The functional role of this part within the maintenance plan. Belongs to the association, not to the part master.']
  required_quantity decimal [note: 'The quantity of this part required to complete one full cycle of the maintenance plan. Belongs to the plan-part combination, not to the plan or part alone — the same part may be required in different quantities across different plans.']
  substitution_allowed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether an approved substitute part may be used in place of this specified part if the primary part is out of stock. When true, the work order execution team may source an approved alternate without plan deviation.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Bill of Materials (BOM) contract between a preventive maintenance plan and a parts inventory item. It captures the planned parts list for each PM plan cycle, specifying which parts are required, in what quantity, in what role, and at what estimated cost. Each record links one maintenance_plan to one parts_inventory item with attributes that exist only in the context of this plan-part combination. Actively managed by maintenance planners in CMMS systems to ensure parts availability before work order execution and to drive automated procurement replenishment ahead of planting and harvest seasons.. Existence Justification: In agricultural equipment maintenance management, a preventive maintenance (PM) plan defines a Bill of Materials (BOM) specifying exactly which parts and consumables are required for each service interval — one plan requires many parts, and one part (e.g., an oil filter or hydraulic fluid) appears across many plans. This is a well-recognized operational concept in CMMS systems called a \'PM BOM\' or \'maintenance plan parts list\', actively created and managed by maintenance planners. The relationship carries its own data (required quantity, part role, mandatory flag, estimated cost, consumption UOM) that belongs to neither the plan nor the part inventory record alone.'
}

  compatible_formulation_types varchar [note: 'The specific formulation type codes (per industry-standard classification) that this asset is rated to handle for the linked input product, based on tank material compatibility, nozzle suitability, and equipment design.   Note: 'This association product represents the formal compatibility certification between an agricultural equipment asset and an agricultural input product. Each record links one asset to one input_product with attributes that exist only in the context of this compatibility relationship — such as the approved application rate range achievable by that specific asset for that specific input, and whether a formal certification is required and on file.. Existence Justification: In agricultural operations, specific equipment assets (sprayers, spreaders, planters) are certified or rated for compatibility with specific input products based on material compatibility, nozzle specifications, EPA label requirements, and equipment capabilities. A single sprayer asset can be approved for many herbicide/fungicide formulations, and a single input product can be applied by many different equipment assets across a farm fleet. This compatibility relationship is actively managed by agronomists and equipment managers as a formal certification or approval record — it is not derivable from transactional application data alone.'

  Note: 'SSOT for TMS-generated transportation orders authorizing and managing the full lifecycle of agricultural commodity movements — from order creation through carrier booking, load planning, and dispatch execution. Single authoritative record for carrier dispatch authorization, freight capacity commitment, booking management, and load execution planning within the supply domain. Subsumes freight booking and load plan data — no separate products exist for these concepts.'

  freight_rate decimal(14,4) [note: 'Contracted or spot freight rate applied to this booking, expressed as a monetary amount per unit of measure (e.g., per MT, per mile, per load). Commercially sensitive pricing data.']
  incoterm_code varchar [note: 'International Commercial Terms (Incoterms) code defining the transfer of risk, cost responsibility, and delivery obligations between shipper and consignee. FOB and CIF are common in agricultural commodity trade. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EXW|FCA|CPT|CIP|DAP|DPU|DDP|FAS|FOB|CFR|CIF — 11 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  is_food_grade boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this booking requires food-grade transport equipment and handling procedures compliant with FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule. Critical for edible agricultural commodities.']
  is_hazmat boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the shipment contains hazardous materials (e.g., agricultural chemicals, pesticides, fertilizers) requiring special handling, placarding, and regulatory documentation under DOT HazMat regulations.']
  lot_number varchar [note: 'Lot Number (LOT) identifying the specific production batch of agricultural commodity being transported. Enables end-to-end traceability from farm to table and supports recall management.']
  mode_of_transport varchar [note: 'Primary transportation mode used for this freight booking. Determines applicable regulatory requirements, documentation (BOL vs AWB), and rate structures.']
  pickup_appointment_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Confirmed date and time of the scheduled pickup appointment at the origin location. Used for dock scheduling and carrier arrival coordination.']
  quantity_uom varchar [note: 'Unit of measure for the booked quantity. Agricultural-specific units include Bushel (BU), Hundredweight (CWT), and Metric Ton (MT) for bulk commodities. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: KG|MT|BU|CWT|PAL|EA|CS — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  rate_basis varchar [note: 'Unit basis on which the freight rate is applied. Determines how total freight charges are calculated from the rate and booked quantity or distance.']
  rfid_tag_code varchar [note: 'Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) tag identifier associated with the shipment for real-time traceability tracking throughout the supply chain. Supports lot-level traceability per FSMA Traceability Rule.']
  service_level varchar [note: 'Service tier contracted for this booking, defining transit time commitments and priority handling. Spot bookings are ad-hoc market-rate engagements outside contracted lanes.']
  special_instructions varchar [note: 'Free-text field for carrier-specific handling instructions, including loading sequence requirements, fragile cargo notes, PHI (Pre-Harvest Interval) compliance notes, or customer-specific delivery requirements.']
  temperature_max_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Maximum allowable temperature in degrees Celsius for cold chain compliance during transport. Paired with minimum temperature to define the acceptable cold chain range for perishable goods.']
  temperature_min_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Minimum allowable temperature in degrees Celsius for cold chain compliance during transport. Mandatory for perishable agricultural products under FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule.']
  total_freight_amount decimal(14,2) [note: 'Net total freight cost for this booking, calculated as base freight amount plus all accessorial charges. Used for COGS allocation, OPEX reporting, and carrier invoice reconciliation.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Audit timestamp recording when this freight booking record was most recently modified.']

  Note: 'Records the confirmed booking of freight capacity with a carrier or 3PL for a specific transport order. Captures booking confirmation number, carrier assignment, booked capacity (weight/volume), equipment type (reefer, dry van, flatbed, hopper), pickup appointment date/time, delivery appointment date/time, freight rate applied, accessorial charges, booking status, and cancellation terms. Bridges transport order to actual carrier execution and BOL issuance.'
}

This enables food safety teams to quaran']

Linking cold_chain_reading directly to corrective_action enables excursion-triggered CAPA workflows, carrier accounta']
  facility_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the storage facility or warehouse where this reading was captured, if the sensor is stationary (e.g., cold room, blast freezer). Null for in-transit readings. Links to facility master for location-based compliance reporting.']
  food_safety_plan_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to compliance.food_safety_plan.   observation_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to weather.observation. Business justification: FSMA cold-chain excursion root cause analysis: a food safety auditor investigating a temperature excursion on a produce shipment correlates the cold-chain sensor reading with the nearest weather stati']
  shipment_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the parent shipment record for which this cold chain reading was captured. Links telemetry to the shipment lifecycle and BOL/AWB traceability.']

Drives escalation routing and corrective action urgency. \'none\' = within spec; \'low\' = minor deviation; \'medium\' = moderate deviation; \'high\' = significant breach; \'critical\' = product safety risk.']
  battery_level_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Remaining battery charge percentage of the IoT sensor device at the time of reading. Enables proactive device maintenance and prevents data gaps due to device power failure during critical cold chain legs.']

Mandatory for HACCP CCP records when corrective_action_taken is True.']
  corrective_action_taken boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a corrective action was initiated in response to the excursion detected at this reading (True = corrective action recorded). Required for HACCP CCP corrective action documentation and GFSI audit evidence.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this cold chain reading record was first ingested into the Databricks silver layer. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and late-arriving data detection.']
  custody_transfer_party varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the party receiving custody at a chain-of-custody transfer event. Populated only when chain_of_custody_event is True. Supports FSMA traceability lot (LOT) tracking and food safety incident root cause investigation.']
  data_quality_flag varchar [note: 'Quality assessment of this reading: \'valid\' = passed all validation checks; \'suspect\' = reading is outside expected sensor range or statistical outlier; \'invalid\' = sensor malfunction confirmed; \'missing\' = gap-filled placeholder; \'interpolated\' = estimated from adjacent readings.']
  excursion_deviation_c decimal(6,2) [note: 'Magnitude of temperature deviation from the nearest threshold boundary in degrees Celsius at the time of this reading. Positive value indicates above max threshold; negative indicates below min threshold. Supports severity scoring and product safety risk assessment.']
  excursion_duration_minutes varchar [note: 'Cumulative duration in minutes that the temperature has been outside the required range at the time of this reading. Used for HACCP corrective action decision-making and product disposition assessment.']
  excursion_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this reading breached the commodity-specific temperature threshold (True = excursion detected). Primary trigger for HACCP corrective action workflows and GFSI audit evidence generation.']
  fsma_traceability_lot_code varchar [note: 'FSMA-compliant traceability lot code (TLC) assigned to the commodity lot being monitored in this reading. Enables rapid lot-level traceability for food safety incident response per FSMA Section 204 requirements.']
  gps_latitude decimal(9,6) [note: 'WGS-84 decimal latitude coordinate of the sensor/vehicle at the time of reading. Enables geospatial mapping of excursion events and route compliance verification.']
  gps_longitude decimal(9,6) [note: 'WGS-84 decimal longitude coordinate of the sensor/vehicle at the time of reading. Used in conjunction with latitude for geospatial excursion root cause analysis.']
  haccp_ccp_reference varchar [note: 'Reference code identifying the specific HACCP Critical Control Point (CCP) plan entry that governs the temperature limits for this reading. Links telemetry data to the formal HACCP plan for audit evidence and regulatory inspection.']
  humidity_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Observed relative humidity percentage inside the transport unit or storage compartment at the time of reading. Critical for fresh produce, cut flowers, and dairy commodities where moisture control prevents spoilage.']
  product_disposition varchar [note: 'Disposition decision for the commodity lot based on cold chain excursion assessment at this reading point: \'accepted\' = within spec; \'quarantine_hold\' = held pending QA review; \'rejected\' = product condemned; \'pending_review\' = awaiting QA decision. Populated for excursion events.']
  reading_interval_seconds varchar [note: 'Configured polling interval in seconds at which the sensor device is programmed to capture readings. Used to validate data completeness and detect gaps in the telemetry stream.']
  reading_source varchar [note: 'Origin system or method by which this reading was captured: \'iot_sensor\' = direct IoT device telemetry; \'rfid_logger\' = RFID data logger; \'manual_entry\' = operator-entered; \'tms_integration\' = received via TMS feed; \'wms_integration\' = received via WMS integration.']
  reading_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Exact date and time (UTC) when the sensor captured this temperature and humidity observation. Primary event timestamp for cold chain telemetry sequencing and excursion duration calculation.']
  reading_type varchar [note: 'Discriminator indicating how this reading was generated: \'periodic\' = scheduled interval reading; \'event_triggered\' = sensor threshold breach; \'manual\' = operator-entered; \'chain_of_custody\' = recorded at custody transfer point; \'alarm\' = device alarm state.']
  required_temp_max_c decimal(6,2) [note: 'Commodity-specific maximum allowable temperature in degrees Celsius for this shipment leg. Defines the upper bound of the HACCP CCP temperature range. Exceedance triggers the excursion_flag.']
  required_temp_min_c decimal(6,2) [note: 'Commodity-specific minimum allowable temperature in degrees Celsius for this shipment leg. Defines the lower bound of the HACCP critical control point (CCP) temperature range against which excursions are evaluated.']
  rfid_tag_code varchar [note: 'RFID tag identifier attached to the pallet, container, or shipment unit being monitored. Enables automated chain-of-custody tracking and links physical asset movement to cold chain telemetry.']
  sensor_calibration_due_date date [note: 'Date by which the sensor device is due for its next calibration verification. Readings captured after this date may be flagged as non-compliant for HACCP and GFSI audit purposes.']
  sensor_device_code varchar [note: 'Unique identifier of the IoT temperature/humidity sensor or RFID-enabled data logger device that captured this reading. Used for device traceability and calibration audit trails.']
  temperature_c decimal(6,2) [note: 'Observed ambient temperature in degrees Celsius at the time of reading. Primary cold chain measurement used for HACCP critical control point (CCP) monitoring and excursion detection.']
  temperature_f decimal(6,2) [note: 'Observed ambient temperature in degrees Fahrenheit at the time of reading. Provided alongside Celsius to support US-market carrier and customer reporting requirements without unit conversion.']
  temperature_zone varchar [note: 'Categorical temperature zone designation for the transport compartment or storage area. Classifies the cold chain environment type: frozen (<-18°C), chilled (0–8°C), ambient (15–25°C), controlled_ambient (8–15°C), ultra_low (<-40°C for specialty biologics/vaccines).']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to this cold chain reading record in the silver layer. Tracks corrections, quality flag updates, and disposition changes for audit trail purposes.']

  Note: 'SSOT for continuous temperature and humidity monitoring data across cold chain shipments of perishable agricultural commodities (fresh produce, dairy, meat, seafood, cut flowers). Records shipment reference, IoT sensor/RFID device ID, timestamp, temperature (°C/°F), humidity (%), GPS coordinates, excursion flag (breach of commodity-specific temperature threshold), alert severity, corrective action taken, and chain-of-custody transfer events. Critical for HACCP compliance, GFSI certification audit evidence, and food safety incident root cause investigation. Single authoritative record for cold chain telemetry within the supply domain.'
}

  disposition_date date [note: 'The date on which the final disposition of this lot was recorded (sold, consumed, destroyed, etc.). Used for lot lifecycle closure reporting and regulatory record retention.']
  final_disposition varchar [note: 'The ultimate disposition of this lot upon closure of the traceability record. \'sold\' = delivered to customer; \'consumed\' = used in internal processing; \'destroyed\' = disposed due to quality failure or recall; \'donated\' = donated to food bank or relief; \'returned\' = returned to supplier; \'pending\' = disposition not yet determined.']
  fsma_tlc varchar [note: 'The FSMA Section 204-compliant Traceability Lot Code (TLC) assigned to this lot at the first point of land-based receiving or transformation. Required for FDA food traceability rule compliance and one-up/one-back recall response.']
  fsma_tlc_source varchar [note: 'Identifies the point in the supply chain where the FSMA Traceability Lot Code (TLC) was first assigned. Required by FDA food traceability rule to establish the Critical Tracking Event (CTE) origin.']
  harvest_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which this lot was harvested from the originating field. Critical for Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) compliance calculations and shelf-life determination. Sourced from Climate FieldView or John Deere Operations Center harvest records.']
  lot_event_type varchar [note: 'Classifies the nature of the lot creation or transformation event. \'original\' = first-time lot creation at harvest; \'split\' = divided from a parent lot; \'merge\' = combined from multiple parent lots; \'repack\' = repackaged without commodity change; \'reclassify\' = grade or classification change.']
  lot_number varchar [note: 'The externally-known, human-readable lot identifier assigned at origin (farm or first point of aggregation). Serves as the primary business identifier for traceability across the supply chain. Aligns with SAP S/4HANA MM batch number and FSMA Traceability Lot Code (TLC).']
  lot_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the lot within the supply chain traceability record. Drives operational workflows, recall response, and final disposition reporting. \'on_hold\' indicates quarantine or quality hold pending investigation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: active|in_transit|in_storage|processing|on_hold|sold|consumed|destroyed — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  moisture_content_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'The moisture content of the commodity in this lot expressed as a percentage. Critical for storage safety (mold/mycotoxin prevention), weight adjustment calculations, and grade determination. Measured at intake and updated after drying operations.']
  mrl_test_date date [note: 'The date on which MRL testing was performed on a representative sample from this lot. Used to determine test currency and whether re-testing is required for extended storage periods.']
  origin_country_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the country where this lot was produced or harvested. Required for Country of Origin Labeling (COOL) compliance and import/export documentation.']
  phi_compliant boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the required Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) was observed between the last pesticide application and the harvest date for this lot. True = PHI compliance confirmed; False = PHI violation detected. Mandatory for food safety and EPA compliance.']
  phi_days_observed varchar [note: 'The actual number of days elapsed between the last recorded pesticide application and the harvest date for this lot. Used to verify PHI compliance against the label-required interval.']
  quantity_bu decimal(18,4) [note: 'The current net quantity of commodity in this lot expressed in Bushels (BU), the standard US grain trade unit. Maintained alongside MT for domestic market reporting and USDA WASDE alignment.']
  quantity_mt decimal(18,4) [note: 'The current net quantity of commodity in this lot expressed in Metric Tons (MT). Updated at each custody transfer or split/merge event. Principal quantitative measure for the lot.']
  recall_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this lot is currently subject to an active recall or withdrawal action. True = lot implicated in recall; False = no active recall. Triggers immediate operational holds and one-up/one-back notification workflows.']
  recall_reference varchar [note: 'The official FDA or USDA recall reference number associated with this lot if recall_flag is True. Enables cross-referencing with regulatory recall databases and internal recall management records.']
  requires_cold_chain boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this lot requires continuous cold chain management throughout storage and transportation. True = cold chain mandatory; False = ambient storage acceptable. Drives carrier selection and facility assignment.']
  rfid_tag_code varchar [note: 'The current active RFID tag EPC (Electronic Product Code) associated with this lot for automated identification and tracking through the supply chain. Supports real-time location tracking in Manhattan Associates WMS.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'The operational system of record from which this lot traceability record originated. Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and Silver layer provenance tracking in the Databricks Lakehouse.']
  storage_temp_max_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'The maximum allowable storage temperature in degrees Celsius for this lot. Exceedance triggers a cold chain exception event and potential quality hold.']
  storage_temp_min_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'The minimum required storage temperature in degrees Celsius for this lot to maintain food safety and quality. Used for cold chain compliance monitoring and facility assignment validation.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this lot traceability record was most recently modified. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and change detection for downstream consumers.']

  Note: 'SSOT for end-to-end traceability of agricultural commodity lots (LOT) moving through the supply chain from farm origin through storage, processing, and delivery to final customer. Captures lot number, commodity type, originating field/farm, harvest date, GRN reference, current custody facility, chain-of-custody transfer events with timestamps, RFID tag history, split/merge lot events, COA linkage, MRL test results, PHI compliance status, and final disposition (sold, consumed, destroyed). Single authoritative record for lot-level supply chain traceability supporting FSMA Section 204 food traceability rule, GLOBALG.A.P. chain of custody, and one-up/one-back recall response.'
}

Table supply.freight_rate {
  freight_rate_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique system-generated identifier for a freight rate record. Primary key for the freight_rate data product within the supply domain.']
  carrier_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the carrier or third-party logistics (3PL) provider with whom this freight rate is contracted. Links to the carrier master record for carrier selection optimization and freight audit.']
  commodity_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to product.commodity. Business justification: Agricultural freight rates are commodity-specific — grain, produce, and livestock rates differ significantly based on handling requirements, temperature needs, and regulatory compliance costs. Linking']
  destination_location_facility_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the destination facility, food manufacturer, retailer distribution center, or port for the freight lane covered by this rate. Defines the endpoint of the origin-destination (O-D) lane.']
  gl_account_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Freight rates are used to pre-accrue freight costs to GL accounts during rate-based accrual processes. Agriculture logistics finance teams use rate cards to generate freight expense accruals by GL acc']
  primary_freight_facility_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the origin facility, farm, elevator, or distribution center for the freight lane covered by this rate. Defines the starting point of the origin-destination (O-D) lane for carrier selection and route optimization.']
  service_contract_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the parent freight contract or rate agreement under which this rate schedule is established. Supports contract lifecycle management and volume commitment tracking.']
  base_rate decimal(18,4) [note: 'The contracted base freight rate amount, expressed in the unit defined by rate_type (e.g., USD per mile, USD per CWT, USD per MT, USD per BU, or flat USD amount). This is the principal monetary fact for the rate record, excluding fuel surcharge and accessorial charges. Used as the foundation for freight cost estimation and carrier invoice audit.']
  commitment_discount_pct decimal(6,4) [note: 'Percentage discount applied to the base rate when the contracted volume commitment tier is met or exceeded. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.05 = 5% discount). Incentivizes volume commitment with carriers and 3PLs for agricultural commodity lanes.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this freight rate record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and SOX financial reporting controls. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the freight rate is denominated (e.g., USD for US Dollar, CAD for Canadian Dollar, EUR for Euro). Required for multi-currency freight cost estimation and financial reporting under GAAP/IFRS.']
  destination_country_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the destination of the freight lane. Required for export documentation, customs compliance, and international freight rate applicability.']
  destination_zip_code varchar [note: 'ZIP code of the destination point for the freight lane. Used for lane-level rate matching in TMS when a specific facility ID is not available. Supports zone-based and mileage-based rate calculations.']
  detention_rate_per_hour decimal(10,4) [note: 'Accessorial charge rate applied per hour when a carrier\'s equipment is detained beyond the contracted free time at origin or destination. A key component of the accessorial rate schedule for agricultural commodity shipments where loading/unloading delays are common.']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date from which this freight rate becomes binding and applicable for freight cost estimation and carrier selection. Aligns with contract start date in carrier agreements. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.']
  equipment_type varchar [note: 'Type of transportation equipment required for this rate. Refrigerated (reefer) equipment is required for cold chain management of perishable agricultural commodities. Hopper trailers are used for bulk grain. Tankers for liquid commodities. Critical for cold chain compliance under FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'Date after which this freight rate is no longer valid for new shipment cost estimation. Null indicates an open-ended rate with no defined expiration. Retained post-expiry for freight audit variance analysis. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.']
  free_time_hours decimal(6,2) [note: 'Number of hours of free loading/unloading time included in the base rate before detention charges begin to accrue. Standard free time for agricultural commodity shipments is typically 2 hours. Critical for managing detention/demurrage cost exposure at grain elevators and processing facilities.']
  freight_terms varchar [note: 'Contractual freight payment terms defining who bears the freight cost and when title transfers. FOB (Free On Board) origin and destination are standard agricultural commodity trade terms. Prepaid = shipper pays; Collect = consignee pays; Third Party = billed to a third party. Aligns with SAP S/4HANA SD billing and SAP MM purchasing conditions.']
  fsma_compliant boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this freight rate is associated with a carrier that has been verified as compliant with the FSMA Sanitary Transportation of Human and Animal Food Rule (21 CFR Part 1, Subpart O). True = carrier has confirmed FSMA compliance for this lane and equipment type. Required for food safety audit and carrier qualification.']
  fuel_surcharge_formula varchar [note: 'Description or formula code defining how the fuel surcharge is calculated, typically indexed to the US Department of Energy (DOE) weekly diesel retail price index. Examples: \'DOE_TABLE_LOOKUP\', \'DOE_PERCENT_OF_BASE\', \'FIXED_CPM\' (cents per mile). Drives dynamic fuel surcharge computation in TMS freight cost estimation.']
  fuel_surcharge_rate decimal(10,4) [note: 'The current or baseline fuel surcharge rate expressed as a percentage of the base rate or as a fixed amount per mile (depending on fuel_surcharge_formula). Updated periodically based on DOE index triggers. Used in freight cost estimation and carrier invoice audit.']
  lane_distance_miles decimal(10,2) [note: 'Contracted or calculated mileage for the origin-destination freight lane. Used for per-mile rate calculations, fuel surcharge computation, and route optimization analysis. Typically derived from PC*MILER or equivalent mileage engine integrated with TMS.']
  lumper_rate decimal(10,4) [note: 'Accessorial charge for lumper (third-party unloading labor) services at destination facilities such as food manufacturer warehouses and retail distribution centers. Included in the accessorial rate schedule when the carrier is responsible for arranging unloading labor.']
  minimum_charge decimal(18,4) [note: 'The minimum freight charge applicable regardless of shipment weight, volume, or distance. Ensures carrier cost recovery for small or short-haul shipments. Applied during freight cost estimation when the calculated base rate falls below this threshold.']
  origin_country_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the origin of the freight lane. Required for cross-border agricultural commodity movements and Country of Origin Labeling (COOL) compliance.']
  origin_zip_code varchar [note: 'ZIP code of the origin point for the freight lane. Used for lane-level rate matching in TMS when a specific facility ID is not available. Supports zone-based and mileage-based rate calculations.']
  rate_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric identifier for the freight rate record, used in carrier negotiations, freight audit, and SAP S/4HANA condition record references. Enables cross-system traceability between TMS, ERP, and carrier portals.']
  rate_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the freight rate record. Active rates are available for freight cost estimation and carrier selection. Expired rates are retained for freight audit variance analysis against historical invoices. Pending rates are awaiting carrier confirmation. Suspended rates are temporarily unavailable.']
  rate_type varchar [note: 'Classification of how the freight rate is calculated and applied. Per mile applies to truckload movements; per CWT (Hundredweight) and per MT (Metric Ton) apply to weight-based commodity pricing; per BU (Bushel) applies to grain and oilseed movements; flat rate applies to fixed-price lane agreements. Drives freight cost estimation logic in TMS.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Operational system of record from which this freight rate record originated. SAP_S4HANA indicates the rate was created in SAP S/4HANA MM condition records; TMS indicates origin from the Transportation Management System; MANUAL indicates direct entry. Supports data lineage and freight audit traceability.']
  stop_off_charge decimal(10,4) [note: 'Accessorial charge applied for each additional stop beyond the primary origin-destination pair on a multi-stop shipment. Common in agricultural distribution routes serving multiple farm locations or delivery points. Part of the accessorial rate schedule.']
  temp_max_celsius decimal(6,2) [note: 'Maximum allowable temperature in degrees Celsius for cold chain shipments covered by this rate. Applicable to refrigerated equipment rates for perishable agricultural commodities. Enforces FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule cold chain requirements.']
  temp_min_celsius decimal(6,2) [note: 'Minimum required temperature in degrees Celsius for cold chain shipments covered by this rate. Applicable to refrigerated equipment rates for perishable agricultural commodities (produce, dairy, meat). Enforces FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule cold chain requirements.']
  transit_days varchar [note: 'Contracted standard transit time in calendar days for the origin-destination lane at this rate. Used for delivery scheduling, cold chain management planning, and carrier service level evaluation. Critical for perishable agricultural commodity shipments.']
  transport_mode varchar [note: 'Mode of transportation for which this freight rate applies. Truckload (TL) and less-than-truckload (LTL) are primary modes for domestic agricultural commodity movements; rail and intermodal for bulk grain; ocean for export; air for high-value perishables. Aligns with BOL and AWB documentation requirements.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this freight rate record was last modified. Supports change tracking, freight audit variance analysis, and Silver Layer incremental processing in the Databricks Lakehouse. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  volume_tier_max decimal(18,4) [note: 'Maximum contracted volume (in the unit defined by rate_type) applicable for this rate tier. Null indicates no upper bound. Defines the upper boundary of the volume commitment tier for tiered discount rate structures.']
  volume_tier_min decimal(18,4) [note: 'Minimum contracted volume commitment (in the unit defined by rate_type, e.g., CWT, MT, BU, or number of loads) required to qualify for this rate tier. Supports volume-based discount structures in carrier contracts. Used for commitment tracking and carrier performance management.']
  volume_uom varchar [note: 'Unit of measure for the volume tier commitment quantities (volume_tier_min, volume_tier_max). Aligns with the rate_type unit. CWT (Hundredweight), MT (Metric Ton), and BU (Bushel) are standard agricultural commodity units. Ensures consistent volume commitment tracking across carrier contracts.']

  Note: 'SSOT for freight rate schedules negotiated with carriers and 3PLs for agricultural commodity transportation. Stores rate type (per mile, per CWT, per MT, per BU, flat rate), origin-destination lane, commodity class (NMFC), equipment type, effective and expiry dates, base rate, fuel surcharge formula (DOE index-linked), accessorial rate schedule (including detention/demurrage, lumper, stop-off charges), minimum charge, currency, and contracted volume tier with commitment discount. Used for freight cost estimation, carrier selection optimization, and freight audit variance analysis against actual invoices. Single authoritative record for contracted freight pricing within the supply domain.'
}
