  fsma_compliance_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Composite score (0-100) measuring the carrier\'s adherence to FSMA Sanitary Transportation of Human and Animal Food rule requirements, including vehicle sanitation, temperature control documentation, and training records. Mandatory for food-grade agricultural shipments.']
  improvement_plan_active boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the carrier is currently operating under a formal Carrier Improvement Plan (CIP) due to performance deficiencies. True when a corrective action plan is in force; False otherwise.']
  lane_destination_country_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the destination end of the primary evaluated shipping lane. Used for cross-border compliance checks and lane performance analytics.']
  lane_origin_country_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the origin end of the primary evaluated shipping lane. Supports COOL (Country of Origin Labeling) compliance and lane-level performance segmentation.']
  on_time_delivery_count varchar [note: 'Number of shipments delivered within the contracted delivery window during the evaluation period. Raw numerator for on-time delivery rate calculation.']
  on_time_delivery_rate decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of shipments delivered within the contracted delivery window during the evaluation period. Calculated as (on_time_delivery_count / total_shipments) * 100. Primary KPI for carrier selection and 3PL contract renewals.']
  on_time_pickup_count varchar [note: 'Number of shipments where the carrier completed pickup within the contracted pickup window during the evaluation period. Raw numerator for on-time pickup rate calculation.']
  on_time_pickup_rate decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of shipments where the carrier completed pickup within the contracted pickup window during the evaluation period. Calculated as (on_time_pickup_count / total_shipments) * 100. Key carrier KPI for agricultural supply chain reliability.']
  performance_tier varchar [note: 'Overall performance classification assigned to the carrier based on composite KPI scores for the evaluation period. Drives carrier selection priority in TMS route planning and 3PL contract renewal decisions. Values: preferred (top-tier, priority allocation), approved (meets standards), probation (below threshold, improvement plan required), suspended (disqualified from new loads).']
  previous_performance_tier varchar [note: 'Performance tier assigned to the carrier in the immediately preceding evaluation period. Enables tier trend analysis and escalation/de-escalation tracking for carrier management decisions.']
  rejected_load_count varchar [note: 'Number of loads rejected by the carrier (carrier-caused refusals) or rejected at destination due to carrier-attributable non-conformances (e.g., temperature breach, contamination) during the evaluation period.']
  rfid_tracking_compliance_rate decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of shipments where the carrier maintained continuous RFID tag scan compliance at all required checkpoints during the evaluation period. Supports FSMA traceability lot (LOT) tracking requirements.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Operational system of record from which the carrier performance data was sourced (e.g., SAP S/4HANA TM, Manhattan Associates WMS). Supports data lineage and Silver Layer provenance tracking.']
  temp_excursion_count varchar [note: 'Number of cold chain shipments where the carrier recorded a temperature excursion outside the contracted min/max range during the evaluation period. Raw numerator for temperature excursion rate.']
  temp_excursion_rate decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of cold chain shipments with a temperature excursion during the evaluation period. Calculated as (temp_excursion_count / cold_chain_shipments) * 100. Critical KPI for perishable agricultural commodity carriers under FSMA cold chain rules.']
  total_freight_cost decimal(18,2) [note: 'Total freight charges invoiced by the carrier for all shipments executed during the evaluation period, in the reporting currency. Used for COGS allocation, carrier spend analysis, and contract benchmarking.']
  total_shipments varchar [note: 'Total number of shipments executed by the carrier within the evaluation period. Serves as the denominator for all rate-based KPI calculations and statistical significance assessment.']
  transit_time_variance_hours decimal(8,2) [note: 'Difference between avg_transit_time_hours and contracted_transit_time_hours. Positive values indicate the carrier is running late on average; negative values indicate early delivery. Key input for route optimization and carrier negotiations.']
  transport_mode varchar [note: 'Primary mode of transportation used by the carrier for the evaluated shipment lanes (e.g., truck for domestic grain hauls, ocean for export containers). Aligns with BOL and AWB classification in SAP S/4HANA SD.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to the carrier performance evaluation record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Supports incremental data processing and audit trail requirements.']

  Note: 'Tracks operational performance metrics for each carrier across agricultural shipment lanes. Records carrier ID, evaluation period, on-time pickup rate, on-time delivery rate, damage claim rate, temperature excursion rate (cold chain), FSMA compliance score, total shipments executed, rejected loads count, average transit time vs. contracted, and overall performance tier (preferred/approved/probation/suspended). Drives carrier selection decisions and 3PL contract renewals.'
}

  payment_terms varchar [note: 'Contracted payment terms applicable to this freight invoice as agreed with the carrier (e.g., Net 30, Net 15, 2/10 Net 30). Determines payment due date and any early payment discount eligibility.']

  carrier_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the approved freight carrier or 3PL provider in the supply domain carrier master.']
  delivery_location_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the authorized delivery and receiving location in the customer domain.']
  approval_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of this carrier-location approval record. Drives TMS eligibility checks during load tendering.']
  approved_commodity_types varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of commodity categories this carrier is authorized to deliver to this specific location under this approval. May be a subset of the carrier\'s overall commodity capabilities.']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date from which this carrier-location approval is active and the carrier is authorized to deliver to this location. Required for approval lifecycle management.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'Date on which this carrier-location approval expires and must be renewed. Null indicates an open-ended approval. Used to trigger re-qualification workflows.']
  preferred_carrier_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the preferred transportation carrier for deliveries to this location. Used by TMS for carrier selection and rate tendering. Corresponds to the carrier master in SAP TMS or Manhattan Associates TMS. [Moved from delivery_location: This attribute on delivery_location captures a single preferred carrier as a soft string reference. With the CarrierLocationApproval association in place, preferred carrier designation is properly modeled via the preferred_flag on the association record, which supports multiple approved carriers per location with one flagged as preferred. The string code on delivery_location is redundant and should be retired in favor of the FK-backed association.]']
  preferred_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this carrier is the preferred (primary) carrier for deliveries to this location. A location may have one preferred carrier among multiple approved carriers.']
  service_level varchar [note: 'The agreed service level for this carrier-location approval (e.g., STANDARD, EXPEDITED, DEDICATED, SPOT). Governs TMS routing priority and SLA commitments for this pairing.']
  temperature_zone_capability varchar [note: 'The agreed temperature zone or range (e.g., AMBIENT, REFRIGERATED, FROZEN, CONTROLLED_ROOM_TEMP) that this carrier is approved to maintain for deliveries to this location. Derived from the intersection of carrier cold chain capability and location temperature control requirements.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the formal approval contract between a freight carrier and an authorized delivery location in the agricultural supply chain. It captures which carriers are approved to serve which receiving facilities, under what service terms, commodity authorizations, and temperature zone agreements. Each record links one carrier to one delivery location and carries attributes that exist only in the context of this approval relationship — such as service level, approved commodity types, temperature zone capability, and approval validity dates. Managed by logistics compliance and transportation teams.. Existence Justification: In agricultural logistics, specific carriers must be formally approved to serve specific delivery locations based on facility-level requirements such as temperature capability, vehicle weight limits, FSMA certification, and dock compatibility. A carrier can be approved to serve many delivery locations, and a delivery location can accept many approved carriers — this approval relationship is actively managed by logistics and compliance teams, not derived from transactional data. The business explicitly tracks which carriers are authorized for which locations, under what service terms, and for which commodity types.'
}

Table supply.facility_commodity_capability {
  facility_commodity_capability_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the facility_commodity_capability association']
  commodity_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the agricultural commodity (corn, soybeans, wheat, etc.) for which this facility capability is defined.']
  facility_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the supply chain facility (grain elevator, cold storage, processing plant, etc.) that holds this commodity capability configuration.']
  allocated_capacity_mt decimal [note: 'The portion of the facility\'s total storage capacity (in Metric Tons) allocated to this specific commodity. Derived from the detection-phase attribute storage_capacity_mt scoped to the facility-commodity pairing — cannot reside on facility alone (varies per commodity) nor on commodity alone (varies per facility).']
  capability_status varchar [note: 'Current operational status of this facility\'s capability to handle the specified commodity. SUSPENDED may indicate a failed inspection or lapsed certification. Drives logistics routing eligibility checks.']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date from which this facility-commodity capability configuration became operationally active. Used for compliance audit trails and logistics planning history.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'The date on which this facility-commodity capability configuration expires or must be recertified. Null if the capability has no scheduled expiry.']
  handling_cert_code varchar [note: 'The handling certification code applicable to this facility for this specific commodity (e.g., USDA-AMS grain handler license for corn, FDA FSMA produce safety certification for fresh commodities). Certification requirements differ by commodity type and facility. Explicitly identified in detection-phase relationship data as commodity_specific_handling_cert.']
  max_moisture_content_pct decimal [note: 'The maximum allowable moisture content percentage enforced at this facility for this commodity at point of acceptance or storage. May differ from the commodity-level standard due to facility-specific equipment capabilities or regional grain trade practices. Explicitly identified in detection-phase relationship data.']
  organic_segregation_capable boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this facility is capable of physically segregating this commodity to maintain organic certification integrity under USDA NOP requirements. Capability varies by commodity (e.g., a facility may segregate organic soybeans but not organic corn due to bin configuration). Explicitly identified in detection-phase relationship data.']
  primary_commodity varchar [note: 'The principal agricultural commodity type handled or stored at this facility (e.g., corn, soybeans, wheat, cotton, perishable produce, livestock). Drives commodity-specific compliance requirements, temperature zone configuration, and fumigation protocols. [Moved from facility: This STRING field on facility is a denormalized label for the dominant commodity type. With the facility_commodity_capability association in place, the full commodity relationship is formally modeled with proper FK integrity. The \'primary_commodity\' label can be deprecated in favor of querying the association table, or retained as a human-readable convenience label only — but it should not serve as the authoritative commodity reference.]']
  temperature_zone_assigned varchar [note: 'The temperature zone configuration assigned at this facility for storing this commodity. A facility may have multiple temperature zones and different commodities are routed to different zones. Sourced from detection-phase attribute temperature_zone scoped to the facility-commodity pairing.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the operational capability configuration between a supply chain facility and an agricultural commodity. It captures the specific storage capacity allocation, temperature zone assignment, organic segregation capability, and handling certifications that exist only in the context of a particular facility handling a particular commodity. Each record defines what a facility can do for a specific commodity — enabling logistics planning, compliance verification, and capacity allocation decisions across the agricultural supply network.. Existence Justification: In agricultural operations, a single facility (e.g., a grain elevator) actively handles multiple commodities simultaneously — corn, soybeans, and wheat may all be stored in segregated bins with different capacity allocations, temperature requirements, and handling certifications. Conversely, a single commodity like Yellow Corn No. 2 is stored and processed across many facilities in the logistics network. The business actively manages this relationship through commodity-specific storage configurations, organic segregation capabilities, and handling certifications that are unique to each facility-commodity pairing — this is not derivable from transactional data alone.'
}

Table supply.route_stop {
  route_stop_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the route_stop association']
  delivery_location_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking this route stop record to the authorized customer delivery and receiving location in the customer domain.']
  route_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking this route stop record to the parent transportation route definition in the supply domain.']
  commodity_types_served varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of commodity categories delivered to this specific delivery location on this specific route. A route may carry multiple commodity classes but only deliver a subset to each stop. Cannot reside on route (varies per stop) or delivery_location (varies per route).']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date from which this route stop assignment is active and valid for TMS planning. Allows stop assignments to be scheduled in advance or phased in with new route configurations.']
  estimated_arrival_window_end varchar [note: 'Planned latest arrival time at this delivery location stop on this route, expressed in HH:MM (24-hour) format. Defines the delivery window communicated to the receiving facility. Belongs to the route-stop relationship.']
  estimated_arrival_window_start varchar [note: 'Planned earliest arrival time at this delivery location stop on this route, expressed in HH:MM (24-hour) format. Derived from route transit time and stop sequence. Belongs to the route-stop relationship, not to either entity alone.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'Date after which this route stop assignment is no longer valid. Null indicates the stop is indefinitely active. Supports seasonal route configurations and temporary stop suspensions.']
  frequency varchar [note: 'Service frequency indicating how often this route calls at this delivery location (e.g., DAILY, WEEKLY, BIWEEKLY, ON_DEMAND). Drives TMS scheduling and carrier capacity planning for this stop.']
  stop_sequence varchar [note: 'Ordinal position of this delivery location within the route\'s stop sequence. Determines the order in which the carrier visits each stop along the route. Cannot reside on route (varies per stop) or delivery_location (varies per route).']
  stop_status varchar [note: 'Current operational status of this route stop assignment. ACTIVE indicates the stop is in use for TMS planning; SUSPENDED indicates a temporary hold (e.g., facility closure, seasonal restriction); INACTIVE indicates the stop has been permanently removed from the route.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Route Stop — the operational assignment of a customer delivery location as a designated stop on a planned transportation route within the agricultural supply chain TMS. It captures the specific stop-level planning data that exists only in the context of a route-to-delivery-location relationship: stop sequence, arrival windows, commodity types served, and service frequency. Each record links one route to one delivery location and is actively created, updated, and deleted by TMS planners as route networks evolve seasonally or as customer delivery points are added or removed.. Existence Justification: In agricultural TMS operations, a single route corridor (e.g., Midwest Grain Corridor) genuinely serves multiple customer delivery locations along its path — grain elevators, food processing plants, and distribution hubs are all stops on the same route. Conversely, a delivery location such as a major grain elevator or food manufacturing plant dock is realistically served by multiple routes originating from different farm regions or origins. The business actively manages this as a \'Route Stop\' or \'Route-to-Location Assignment\' — a TMS planning concept with its own operational data including stop sequence, arrival windows, commodity types served, and service frequency.'
}

Table supply.contract_commodity_coverage {
  contract_commodity_coverage_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the contract_commodity_coverage association']
  commodity_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the specific agricultural commodity covered under the terms of this contract pairing.']
  service_contract_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the parent logistics service contract under which this commodity coverage is defined.']
  base_freight_rate decimal [note: 'Contracted base freight rate per unit of measure applicable to this specific commodity under this service contract. Rates differ by commodity due to density, handling requirements, and regulatory classification.']
  committed_volume_mt decimal [note: 'Minimum guaranteed volume in Metric Tons committed per contract period specifically for this commodity under this service contract. Varies by commodity within the same contract and cannot reside on service_contract (which may cover multiple commodities at different volumes).']
  commodity_types_covered varchar [note: 'Pipe-delimited list of agricultural commodity categories covered under this contract (e.g., grain|produce|livestock_feed|refrigerated_dairy). Drives FSMA traceability obligations, temperature zone requirements, and MRL compliance checks during shipment execution. [Moved from service_contract: This pipe-delimited STRING field on service_contract is a denormalized anti-pattern that attempts to store multiple commodity references in a single column. It must be decomposed into individual contract_commodity_coverage records, each with its own commodity_id FK and commodity-specific rate/volume/SLA attributes. Retaining this field would create data integrity issues and prevent commodity-level querying.]']
  coverage_status varchar [note: 'Current operational status of this commodity\'s coverage under the service contract. A commodity may be temporarily suspended from a contract (e.g., seasonal exclusion, regulatory hold) without terminating the overall contract.']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date on which this commodity\'s specific coverage terms became effective under the service contract. May differ from the parent contract effective_date if a commodity was added mid-term.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'Date on which this commodity\'s coverage under the service contract expires. Nullable if coverage runs for the full contract term. Allows commodity-level term management within a multi-commodity contract.']
  freight_rate_uom varchar [note: 'Unit of measure against which the base_freight_rate for this commodity is applied within this contract. May differ by commodity (e.g., grains priced per MT, produce per load).']
  temp_compliance_target_pct decimal [note: 'Contracted minimum percentage of shipments for this commodity that must remain within the required temperature range under this service contract. Varies by commodity — frozen produce has stricter targets than ambient grain.']
  transit_time_target_hours decimal [note: 'Contracted maximum transit time in hours from pickup to delivery for this specific commodity under this service contract. Perishable commodities (produce, dairy) carry tighter targets than dry grains.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Coverage Contract between service_contract and commodity. It captures the commodity-specific terms negotiated within a logistics service contract — including committed volumes, freight rates, and temperature/transit SLA targets that apply to a specific commodity under a specific carrier or 3PL agreement. Each record links one service_contract to one commodity with attributes that exist only in the context of this pairing and cannot reside on either parent entity alone.. Existence Justification: In agricultural logistics, a single service contract with a carrier or 3PL explicitly covers multiple commodity types (e.g., a contract covering corn, soybeans, and wheat simultaneously), each with distinct committed volumes, freight rates, and temperature compliance targets. Conversely, a single commodity like Yellow Corn No. 2 is covered by many different service contracts across different carriers, lanes, and contract periods. The business actively manages these commodity-specific terms within each contract — this is not an analytical derivation but an operational record that logistics and supply chain teams create and maintain.'
}

  is_organic_certified boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the material in this stock position holds USDA National Organic Program (NOP) certification. Drives segregation requirements, premium pricing, and organic supply chain compliance.']

  last_movement_date date [note: 'Date of the most recent inventory movement (goods receipt, goods issue, transfer, or adjustment) recorded against this stock position. Used for slow-moving and obsolete inventory identification.']
  manufacture_date date [note: 'Date the material in this stock position was manufactured, processed, or harvested. Used for FIFO/FEFO rotation, shelf-life calculation, and traceability under FSMA and GLOBALG.A.P. requirements.']
  phi_days varchar [note: 'Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) in days — the minimum number of days that must elapse between the last pesticide or chemical application and harvest for this lot. Ensures Maximum Residue Limit (MRL) compliance and food safety regulatory adherence.']
  price_variance_usd decimal(18,2) [note: 'Variance between the standard cost and actual purchase price for this stock position in USD. Captured at period-end for GAAP/IFRS inventory valuation adjustments and commodity price risk reporting.']
  qty_available decimal(18,4) [note: 'Available-to-promise (ATP) quantity calculated as on-hand quantity minus reserved quantity in the primary unit of measure. Represents the uncommitted inventory available for new sales orders or production requirements.']
  qty_blocked decimal(18,4) [note: 'Quantity of the material in blocked stock status (not available for use) in the primary unit of measure. Includes recalled, quarantined, or damaged inventory pending disposition decision.']
  qty_in_quality_inspection decimal(18,4) [note: 'Quantity of the material currently held in quality inspection stock pending QM release in the primary unit of measure. Supports HACCP, FSMA, and GLOBALG.A.P. quality hold management.']
  qty_on_hand decimal(18,4) [note: 'Total physical quantity of the material currently on hand at the storage location in the primary unit of measure (CWT, BU, or MT). Represents the gross inventory position before reservations or holds.']
  qty_reserved decimal(18,4) [note: 'Quantity of the material reserved against open sales orders, production orders, or transfer orders in the primary unit of measure. Reduces available-to-promise (ATP) quantity for new commitments.']
  qty_shrinkage decimal(18,4) [note: 'Cumulative quantity lost to shrinkage (moisture loss, spoilage, handling losses) recorded against this stock position in the primary unit of measure. Used for shrinkage analysis, COGS adjustment, and post-harvest handling performance reporting.']
  rotation_method varchar [note: 'Inventory rotation method applied to this stock position for picking and consumption sequencing. FIFO (First In First Out) and FEFO (First Expired First Out) are standard for agricultural commodities and perishables to minimize spoilage and ensure food safety compliance.']
  sap_accounting_doc_number varchar [note: 'SAP FI accounting document number (BELNR) generated for the inventory valuation posting associated with this stock position. Provides the audit trail reference for GAAP/IFRS financial reporting and SOX compliance.']
  sscc varchar [note: 'GS1 Serial Shipping Container Code (SSCC-18) assigned to the logistics unit (pallet, bin, container) holding this stock position. Enables RFID-based tracking and WMS integration for supply chain traceability.']
  stock_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the stock position record. Active indicates normal inventory; expired indicates stock past its shelf life or PHI; recalled indicates a regulatory or quality recall event; quarantined indicates hold pending investigation; disposed indicates stock written off.']
  stock_type varchar [note: 'SAP S/4HANA stock type classification indicating the usability of the inventory. Unrestricted stock is available for use; quality inspection stock is pending QM release; blocked stock is not available; in-transit stock is between locations; returns stock is pending disposition.']
  total_value_usd decimal(18,2) [note: 'Total book value of this stock position in US dollars (USD), calculated as on-hand quantity multiplied by unit price. Used for balance sheet inventory reporting, period-end valuation snapshots, and GAAP/IFRS financial reporting.']
  unit_price_usd decimal(18,4) [note: 'Inventory valuation price per primary unit of measure in US dollars (USD). For standard cost materials, this is the standard price; for moving average materials, this is the current moving average price. Used for period-end inventory valuation and COGS calculation.']
  uom_primary varchar [note: 'Primary unit of measure for quantity reporting on this stock position. Agricultural commodities use industry-standard units: CWT (Hundredweight), BU (Bushel), MT (Metric Ton). Seeds and chemicals may use KG, LB, BAG, or EA. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CWT|BU|MT|KG|LB|TON|EA|BAG — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to this stock position record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change data capture (CDC), data lineage, and audit trail compliance.']
  valuation_date date [note: 'Date as of which the inventory valuation snapshot was captured for this stock position. Used for period-end financial reporting, GAAP/IFRS inventory valuation, and commodity position reporting.']
  valuation_method varchar [note: 'Inventory valuation method applied to this stock position. Standard cost uses a predetermined price; moving average recalculates price with each goods movement; FIFO (First In First Out) values inventory based on oldest cost layers. Supports GAAP and IFRS inventory accounting.']
  wms_position_number varchar [note: 'Manhattan Associates WMS internal position or license plate number for this stock position. Used for WMS-to-SAP reconciliation, cycle count management, and real-time inventory visibility.']

  Note: 'Core master record of current inventory positions across all agricultural storage locations (grain bins, cold storage, warehouses, field stockpiles). Tracks on-hand, reserved, and available-to-promise quantities in CWT, BU, and MT by material, commodity lot, and location. Includes stock type (unrestricted, quality inspection, blocked), valuation class, unit price, total value, and valuation method (standard cost, moving average, FIFO). Supports period-end valuation snapshots capturing valuation date, quantity, unit price, total value in USD, price variance, and SAP accounting document reference for GAAP/IFRS inventory valuation, COGS calculation, and commodity position reporting. Serves as the SSOT for real-time stock levels, inventory valuation, and period-end financial inventory reporting. Supports GS1 GTIN and SSCC identifiers for global supply chain interoperability. Integrates with SAP S/4HANA MM and Manhattan Associates WMS.'
}

Table inventory.cycle_count {

Cycle counts are performed at the bin level in Manhattan Associates WMS. Adding bin_location_id FK links the count to the auth']

Required for period-close physical inventory reconciliation, SOX controls over inventory accuracy, and financial statement asse']

  adjustment_posted_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the confirmed inventory variance from this cycle count has been posted as an inventory adjustment in SAP MM (MI07 Post Differences). True = adjustment posted; False = pending posting. Triggers downstream inventory_adjustment record creation.']

  count_document_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known WMS-generated document number uniquely identifying the cycle count event. Corresponds to the Manhattan Associates WMS count document and SAP MM physical inventory document number used for audit trail and reconciliation.']

  count_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the cycle count event. Tracks workflow progression from open through completion and approval in the WMS and SAP MM inventory management process.']
  count_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the cycle count event indicating whether it was a regularly scheduled count, an ad-hoc count, a recount triggered by variance, an annual physical inventory, or a system-triggered count. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: scheduled|ad_hoc|recount|annual|triggered — promote to reference product if additional types are needed]']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the cycle count record was first created in the system (WMS or SAP MM). Provides the audit trail creation marker for data lineage and compliance reporting.']

  grn_number varchar [note: 'Goods Receipt Note (GRN) number associated with the lot being counted. Provides traceability back to the original goods receipt event in SAP MM for supply chain continuity.']
  gtin varchar [note: 'GS1 Global Trade Item Number (GTIN-14) for the material being counted. Enables barcode scanning integration with Manhattan Associates WMS and supports GS1 traceability standards.']
  material_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the material being counted by agricultural input or output category. Supports domain-specific inventory accuracy reporting across seed, chemical, fertilizer, harvested commodity, and feed stock categories.']
  original_count_document_number varchar [note: 'For recount records (recount_flag = True), the count document number of the original cycle count that triggered this recount. Enables audit trail linking between original count and recount events.']
  recount_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this cycle count record is a recount triggered by an unacceptable variance on a prior count. True = recount; False = original count. Links to the original count via original_count_document_number.']
  sap_physical_inventory_doc varchar [note: 'SAP S/4HANA MM physical inventory document number (MI01) corresponding to this cycle count event. Provides the cross-system reference key for reconciliation between Manhattan Associates WMS and SAP MM.']
  scheduled_count_date date [note: 'The originally planned date for the cycle count as defined in the WMS cycle count schedule. Compared against count_date to measure schedule adherence and operational compliance.']
  stock_type varchar [note: 'SAP MM stock type category of the inventory being counted. Determines whether the stock is available for use (unrestricted), under quality hold (quality_inspection), blocked, or restricted. Critical for QM integration.']
  system_qty decimal(18,4) [note: 'The inventory quantity recorded in the WMS/SAP system at the time the cycle count was initiated, before the physical count result is entered. Represents the book inventory position used as the baseline for variance calculation.']
  uom varchar [note: 'The unit of measure in which system_qty, count_qty, and variance_qty are expressed. Agricultural inventory uses CWT (Hundredweight), BU (Bushel), and MT (Metric Ton) for commodities; other units for inputs. Aligns with SAP MM base UOM. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CWT|BU|MT|LB|KG|EA|GAL|TON — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the cycle count record was last modified in the system. Tracks updates such as recount entries, variance approvals, and root cause code assignments for audit trail completeness.']
  variance_pct decimal(8,4) [note: 'The variance quantity expressed as a percentage of the system quantity ((variance_qty / system_qty) * 100). Key inventory accuracy KPI metric used to assess count quality and trigger recount thresholds.']
  variance_qty decimal(18,4) [note: 'The difference between the physical count quantity and the system quantity (count_qty minus system_qty). A positive value indicates a surplus; a negative value indicates a shortage. Used to trigger inventory adjustment records.']
  variance_root_cause_code varchar [note: 'Standardized root cause code assigned to explain the inventory variance (e.g., SHRINKAGE, MISCOUNT, MISPLACE, DAMAGE, THEFT, SYSTEM_ERROR, UNIT_CONVERSION). Used for root cause analysis and continuous improvement of inventory accuracy. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: SHRINKAGE|MISCOUNT|MISPLACE|DAMAGE|THEFT|SYSTEM_ERROR|UNIT_CONVERSION|EXPIRY — promote to reference product]']
  variance_root_cause_description varchar [note: 'Free-text narrative description providing additional detail on the root cause of the inventory variance. Supplements the variance_root_cause_code with counter observations and corrective action notes.']
  variance_value_usd decimal(18,2) [note: 'The financial value of the inventory variance in US dollars, calculated as variance_qty multiplied by the standard or moving average unit price. Used for financial impact assessment, P&L reporting, and COGS adjustment authorization.']

  Note: 'WMS-driven cycle count event record capturing scheduled and ad-hoc physical inventory counts at the storage location and bin level. Captures count document number, count date, counter assigned, location/bin counted, material with GS1 GTIN, system quantity vs. physical count quantity in CWT/BU/MT, variance quantity, variance percentage, recount flag, count status, and root cause code for variances. Integrates with Manhattan Associates WMS cycle count module and SAP MM inventory management. Supports inventory accuracy KPI tracking and triggers inventory_adjustment records for confirmed variances.'
}

Business justification: Inventory adjustments for spoilage, expired product disposal, and condemned grain generate regulated waste events requiring EPA waste manifests and GRI 306 reporting. Linking inventory_adjustment to w']
  adjusted_qty decimal(18,4) [note: 'Inventory quantity after the adjustment has been applied. Expressed in the primary unit of measure (CWT, BU, or MT). Represents the corrected on-hand balance.']
  adjustment_status varchar [note: 'Current workflow lifecycle state of the inventory adjustment record. Controls whether the adjustment has been approved, posted to the general ledger, or reversed.']
  adjustment_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the inventory adjustment event. Shrinkage covers moisture loss, drying shrink, handling loss, and storage deterioration. Cycle count variance corrects WMS discrepancies. Damage write-off records pest damage or physical loss. Quality downgrade reclassifies commodity grade. Reclassification moves stock between categories.']
  approval_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the inventory adjustment was formally approved by the authorized approver. Supports SOX audit trail and segregation of duties compliance.']
  approver_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the employee who approved the inventory adjustment. Retained as a denormalized audit field to preserve the historical record even if the employee record changes.']
  cause_code varchar [note: 'Standardized root cause code identifying the reason for the inventory discrepancy or shrinkage event (e.g., MOIST-LOSS, PEST-DMG, PROC-ERR, CYCLE-VAR). Sourced from SAP MM cause code configuration. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product with full cause code taxonomy]']
  corrective_action varchar [note: 'Description of the corrective action implemented to prevent recurrence of the inventory discrepancy or shrinkage event. Supports continuous improvement and GFSI/SQF audit requirements.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the inventory adjustment record was first created in the system. Audit field for data lineage and Silver layer ingestion tracking.']
  document_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known business identifier for the inventory adjustment document. Generated by SAP S/4HANA MM or Manhattan Associates WMS at time of posting. Used for audit trail and cross-system reconciliation.']
  grn_number varchar [note: 'Goods Receipt Note (GRN) reference number linking the adjusted inventory to its original inbound receipt document. Enables traceability from adjustment back to procurement receipt.']
  is_reversal boolean [note: 'Flag indicating whether this adjustment record is a reversal of a previously posted adjustment. True when the record cancels a prior adjustment document. Supports audit trail integrity.']
  movement_type varchar [note: 'SAP S/4HANA MM movement type code governing the inventory posting (e.g., 551 for scrapping, 701 for physical inventory difference, 344 for transfer posting). Determines the accounting impact and stock category affected.']
  original_qty decimal(18,4) [note: 'Inventory quantity recorded before the adjustment event was applied. Expressed in the primary unit of measure (CWT, BU, or MT). Baseline for variance calculation.']
  plant_code varchar [note: 'SAP S/4HANA plant code identifying the facility (farm, processing plant, warehouse) where the inventory adjustment occurred. Supports multi-site inventory management.']
  posting_date date [note: 'Accounting posting date on which the inventory adjustment was recorded in SAP S/4HANA FI/MM. Determines the fiscal period for COGS and inventory valuation impact. May differ from shrinkage_event_date.']
  reason_code varchar [note: 'Business reason code for the inventory adjustment as defined in SAP S/4HANA MM configuration (e.g., physical inventory difference, goods issue correction, quality rejection). Distinct from cause_code which identifies root cause; reason_code identifies the business justification category.']
  reason_description varchar [note: 'Free-text narrative description of the specific reason for the inventory adjustment. Provides context beyond the structured reason_code for audit trail and corrective action documentation.']
  reversed_document_number varchar [note: 'Adjustment document number of the original posting that this record reverses. Populated only when is_reversal is True. Enables bidirectional audit trail linkage between original and reversal documents.']
  shrinkage_event_date date [note: 'Calendar date on which the shrinkage event (moisture loss, pest damage, storage deterioration) physically occurred. May differ from the adjustment posting date. Critical for seasonal shrinkage trend analysis.']
  shrinkage_pct decimal(7,4) [note: 'Percentage of original inventory quantity lost due to the shrinkage event (variance_qty / original_qty * 100). Used for shrinkage trend analysis and benchmarking by storage type, commodity, and season.']
  shrinkage_type varchar [note: 'Specific category of shrinkage event when adjustment_type is shrinkage. Distinguishes moisture loss during drying, physical handling loss, storage deterioration over time, pest damage, or quality-driven downgrade. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: moisture_loss|drying_shrink|handling_loss|storage_deterioration|pest_damage|quality_downgrade|other — promote to reference product]']
  stock_type_after varchar [note: 'SAP stock category of the inventory after the adjustment has been applied. Used for reclassification adjustments to confirm the target stock category.']
  stock_type_before varchar [note: 'SAP stock category of the inventory before the adjustment was applied. Relevant for reclassification adjustments that move stock between unrestricted, quality inspection, blocked, or restricted categories.']
  unit_cost_usd decimal(18,6) [note: 'Standard or moving average cost per unit of measure at the time of the adjustment, in US Dollars. Used to calculate the financial value impact of the inventory adjustment for COGS accuracy.']
  uom_primary varchar [note: 'Primary unit of measure for all quantity fields (original_qty, adjusted_qty, variance_qty). Agricultural commodities are measured in Hundredweight (CWT), Bushels (BU), or Metric Tons (MT) per USDA standards.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the inventory adjustment record was last modified in the system. Supports incremental data pipeline processing and audit trail in the Databricks Silver layer.']
  value_impact_usd decimal(18,2) [note: 'Estimated financial impact of the inventory adjustment in US Dollars (variance_qty multiplied by unit_cost_usd). Represents the COGS charge or inventory write-down posted to the general ledger. Negative values indicate inventory value reduction.']
  variance_qty decimal(18,4) [note: 'Net quantity difference between original and adjusted quantities (original_qty minus adjusted_qty). Negative values indicate stock reduction (shrinkage/loss); positive values indicate stock increase (count correction). Expressed in primary UOM.']
  wms_task_number varchar [note: 'Manhattan Associates WMS task or cycle count task number associated with this inventory adjustment. Provides cross-system traceability between the WMS cycle count event and the SAP inventory posting.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of all inventory quantity and value adjustments including shrinkage events (moisture loss/drying shrink, handling loss, storage deterioration, pest damage, quality downgrade), cycle count variance corrections, damage write-offs, and reclassifications. Captures adjustment document number, adjustment type (shrinkage, variance, damage, downgrade, reclassification), material, lot, location, original quantity, adjusted quantity, variance quantity in CWT/BU/MT, shrinkage type and percentage, cause code, adjustment reason code, corrective action taken, approver, cost impact, estimated value impact, shrinkage event date, and SAP accounting document reference. Serves as the SSOT for all shrinkage tracking, shrinkage trend analysis and benchmarking by storage type, commodity, and season. Supports COGS accuracy for commodity accounting and provides complete audit trail for all inventory corrections.'
}

Table inventory.bin_location {
  bin_location_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each bin location record within the warehouse management system. Serves as the primary key for the bin_location data product in the Databricks Silver Layer.']
  plant_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the SAP plant (facility or production site) to which this bin location belongs. Aligns bin-level inventory tracking with SAP S/4HANA MM plant-level stock management.']
  storage_location_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the parent storage location (grain bin facility, cold storage building, warehouse, or field stockpile site) that contains this bin. Enables hierarchical slot management within Manhattan Associates WMS and SAP S/4HANA MM.']
  aisle_code varchar [note: 'Alphanumeric code identifying the aisle within the storage section where this bin is physically located. Used for optimizing pick paths and directing warehouse personnel to the correct physical location.']
  allowed_material_types varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of SAP material type codes permitted for storage in this bin (e.g., \'FERT,DUNG,ERSA\' for fertilizers, seeds, and spare parts). Enforces material segregation rules and prevents incompatible commodity co-mingling. Managed in SAP S/4HANA MM material type configuration.']
  bin_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the bin within its storage location. Used in WMS slot management, pick/put-away instructions, and RFID scanning operations. Corresponds to the WMS bin number in Manhattan Associates.']
  bin_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable descriptive name or label for the bin location (e.g., \'North Grain Bin Cell 3A\', \'Cold Bay 12\', \'Rack Position A-02-03\'). Used in operational reports and warehouse floor maps.']
  bin_status varchar [note: 'Current operational lifecycle status of the bin location within the WMS. Active bins are available for put-away and picking; blocked bins are temporarily unavailable; reserved bins are pre-allocated; under_maintenance bins are being serviced; decommissioned bins are permanently retired.']
  bin_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the physical bin structure. Determines storage rules, capacity constraints, and compatible material types. Grain bin cells hold harvested commodities; rack positions hold packaged goods; cold storage bays hold perishables; floor stacks hold palletized inventory; bulk piles hold loose commodities; chemical cabinets hold agrochemicals. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: grain_bin_cell|rack_position|cold_storage_bay|floor_stack|bulk_pile|chemical_cabinet — promote to reference product]']
  capacity_bu decimal(18,4) [note: 'Maximum storage capacity of the bin expressed in Bushels (BU), the standard unit of measure for grain commodities in US agricultural operations. Used for grain bin cell utilization planning and WASDE reporting alignment.']
  capacity_cwt decimal(18,4) [note: 'Maximum storage capacity of the bin expressed in Hundredweight (CWT), a standard unit used for livestock feed, fertilizer, and certain commodity pricing in US agricultural markets.']
  capacity_mt decimal(18,4) [note: 'Maximum storage capacity of the bin expressed in Metric Tons (MT). Used for international trade documentation, export compliance, and alignment with global commodity reporting standards (CIF/FOB contracts).']
  commissioning_date date [note: 'Date the bin location was officially commissioned and made available for use in the WMS. Marks the start of the bin\'s operational lifecycle and is used for asset age tracking, depreciation scheduling, and capacity planning.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the bin location record was first created in the system. Provides audit trail for data lineage and supports SOX financial reporting controls for inventory master data governance.']
  current_utilization_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Current fill level of the bin expressed as a percentage of its maximum capacity. Calculated from WMS inventory positions and updated on each stock movement. Drives replenishment triggers and bin assignment logic in Manhattan Associates WMS.']
  decommissioning_date date [note: 'Date the bin location was permanently decommissioned and removed from active WMS operations. Nullable for active bins. Used for capacity planning, asset retirement reporting, and historical inventory analysis.']
  height_cm decimal(10,2) [note: 'Physical height dimension of the bin location in centimeters. Determines compatibility with stacked pallets, tall containers, or bulk commodity storage. Used in conjunction with level_code for equipment selection (e.g., high-reach forklift requirements).']
  is_gmo_segregated boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this bin is designated for GMO-segregated commodity storage. When True, the bin is used exclusively for non-GMO or identity-preserved commodities, supporting COOL (Country of Origin Labeling) and non-GMO supply chain traceability requirements.']
  is_hazmat_compatible boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this bin is certified and equipped to store hazardous materials such as pesticides, herbicides, or fertilizers with hazmat classifications. When True, the bin meets EPA and OSHA storage requirements for agrochemicals. Prevents co-mingling of hazmat and food-grade commodities.']
  is_organic_segregated boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this bin is designated exclusively for USDA National Organic Program (NOP) certified organic commodities. When True, the bin must be physically segregated from non-organic storage to maintain organic certification integrity and prevent commingling.']
  last_cleaned_date date [note: 'Date the bin location was last cleaned and sanitized. Critical for food safety compliance, particularly for grain bins and cold storage bays. Supports HACCP sanitation monitoring, FSMA Preventive Controls, and GLOBALG.A.P. hygiene audit requirements.']
  last_cycle_count_date date [note: 'Date of the most recent WMS-driven cycle count performed on this bin location. Used to schedule future cycle counts, assess inventory accuracy compliance, and support FSMA traceability requirements. Sourced from Manhattan Associates WMS cycle count completion records.']
  last_inspected_date date [note: 'Date of the most recent physical inspection of the bin location for structural integrity, pest presence, moisture ingress, or contamination. Supports USDA APHIS pest management compliance and GFSI audit readiness.']
  length_cm decimal(10,2) [note: 'Physical length dimension of the bin location in centimeters. Used for slotting optimization, determining compatible pallet or container sizes, and space utilization analysis within the warehouse management system.']
  level_code varchar [note: 'Alphanumeric code identifying the vertical level or tier of the bin within a rack or storage structure. Used for height-based storage rules and equipment selection (e.g., forklift reach requirements).']
  max_temp_celsius decimal(5,2) [note: 'Maximum allowable storage temperature in degrees Celsius for this bin location. Exceeding this threshold triggers WMS alerts and may require stock relocation to prevent quality degradation or food safety violations.']
  max_weight_kg decimal(12,3) [note: 'Maximum allowable weight load for this bin location in kilograms. Critical for structural safety compliance, particularly for rack positions and floor stacks. Prevents overloading that could cause structural failure or OSHA safety violations.']
  min_temp_celsius decimal(5,2) [note: 'Minimum allowable storage temperature in degrees Celsius for this bin location. Used to enforce cold chain compliance and prevent commodity spoilage. Monitored via IoT sensors integrated with the WMS.']
  put_away_strategy varchar [note: 'WMS put-away strategy assigned to this bin, governing how incoming stock is directed to this location. Fixed bins always receive the same material; open bins accept any compatible material; bulk bins receive large-volume commodity transfers; addition bins consolidate partial pallets; next_empty bins are filled sequentially.']
  rfid_tag_number varchar [note: 'RFID tag identifier physically attached to the bin location for automated scanning and real-time inventory tracking. Enables touchless bin identification during put-away, picking, and cycle count operations in Manhattan Associates WMS.']
  rotation_method varchar [note: 'Inventory rotation method applied to stock stored in this bin. FIFO (First In First Out) and FEFO (First Expired First Out) are standard for food-grade commodities to minimize spoilage and ensure compliance with food safety regulations. LIFO and LEFO may apply to non-perishable inputs.']
  row_code varchar [note: 'Alphanumeric code identifying the row within the aisle for this bin. Combined with aisle_code and level_code to form the full physical coordinate of the bin within the warehouse.']
  sap_storage_bin varchar [note: 'The storage bin identifier as defined in SAP S/4HANA Warehouse Management (WM) module. Used for cross-system reconciliation between Manhattan Associates WMS and SAP S/4HANA MM inventory postings. Corresponds to the LGPLA field in SAP WM.']
  storage_section_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the logical storage section or zone within the storage location to which this bin belongs (e.g., \'SEC-A\', \'ZONE-COLD-1\'). Supports zone-based picking strategies and inventory segmentation in Manhattan Associates WMS.']
  temperature_zone varchar [note: 'Temperature-controlled zone classification for the bin. Determines which commodities (e.g., fresh produce, frozen goods, ambient grain) can be stored in this bin. Critical for cold chain compliance and food safety under FDA and FSMA requirements.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to the bin location record. Used for change data capture (CDC) in the Databricks Silver Layer pipeline and supports audit trail requirements for inventory master data governance.']
  width_cm decimal(10,2) [note: 'Physical width dimension of the bin location in centimeters. Used alongside length and height for slotting optimization and determining whether specific pallet configurations or container types can be accommodated.']
  wms_bin_number varchar [note: 'The bin identifier as recorded in Manhattan Associates WMS, used for system-to-system integration and reconciliation with SAP S/4HANA WM storage bin records. This is the operational system key used in WMS transactions.']

  Note: 'Granular WMS bin-level location master within a storage location, representing individual grain bin cells, rack positions, cold storage bays, or floor stack positions. Captures bin code, bin type, storage section, maximum capacity in BU/MT/CWT, current utilization, temperature zone, hazmat compatibility flag, RFID tag, and WMS bin status. Enables precise slot management and bin-level inventory tracking within Manhattan Associates WMS.'

  is_hazmat boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this material is classified as hazardous (e.g., pesticides, herbicides, fumigants). When true, EPA SDS requirements, REI (Restricted Entry Interval), and special storage/handling rules apply.']
  is_mrp_active boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this reorder policy is currently included in SAP MM MRP planning runs. When false, the policy exists as a configuration record but does not trigger automated purchase requisitions.']
  is_regulated_substance boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this material is subject to regulatory quantity limits, licensing, or reporting requirements (e.g., restricted-use pesticides under EPA, controlled fertilizers under APHIS). Triggers compliance workflow on purchase requisition.']
  is_seasonal boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this material experiences significant seasonal demand fluctuations (e.g., planting season seeds, harvest-time chemicals). When true, seasonal demand profiles are applied in MRP planning.']
  last_reviewed_date date [note: 'Date when this reorder policy was last reviewed and validated by the inventory planner or supply chain manager. Supports periodic policy governance and audit trail requirements.']
  lead_time_days varchar [note: 'Expected number of calendar days from purchase requisition creation to goods receipt at the storage location. Used by SAP MM MRP to calculate replenishment timing and avoid stockouts.']
  lot_size_procedure varchar [note: 'SAP MM MRP lot-sizing procedure that determines how replenishment quantities are calculated: fixed order quantity, lot-for-lot (exact requirement), EOQ, period-based, or min-max. Maps to SAP Lot Size field.']
  maximum_order_qty decimal(18,4) [note: 'Maximum quantity allowed per single purchase requisition to control procurement spend, storage capacity, and perishability risk. Expressed in primary UOM.']
  maximum_stock_qty decimal(18,4) [note: 'Upper bound on inventory quantity for this material at this storage location. Replenishment orders will not exceed this level. Prevents overstocking and storage capacity violations.']
  minimum_order_qty decimal(18,4) [note: 'Minimum quantity that must be ordered per purchase requisition, typically driven by supplier minimum order requirements or packaging constraints. Expressed in primary UOM.']
  minimum_remaining_shelf_life_days varchar [note: 'Minimum number of days of remaining shelf life required at time of goods receipt for the material to be accepted into stock. Rejects deliveries that do not meet this threshold per quality management policy.']
  mrp_type varchar [note: 'SAP MRP planning type that governs how replenishment is triggered: reorder point (ROP), time-phased planning, consumption-based, or manual. Directly maps to SAP MM MRP Type field (e.g., VB, VM, PD).']
  order_multiple_qty decimal(18,4) [note: 'Quantity increment by which replenishment orders must be rounded up (e.g., full pallet, full bin, full truckload). Ensures orders align with supplier packaging or transport unit constraints.']
  peak_season_end_month varchar [note: 'Calendar month (1–12) when peak seasonal demand ends for this material. Defines the seasonal window during which elevated reorder points and safety stock levels are applied.']
  peak_season_safety_stock_qty decimal(18,4) [note: 'Elevated safety stock quantity applied during the defined peak season window (e.g., planting or harvest period). Overrides the standard safety stock quantity during peak months.']
  peak_season_start_month varchar [note: 'Calendar month (1–12) when peak seasonal demand begins for this material. Used to adjust reorder points and safety stock levels ahead of high-demand periods such as planting or harvest seasons.']
  policy_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier for this reorder policy record, used in SAP MM MRP planning runs and cross-system references.']
  policy_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the reorder policy configuration. Only active policies are evaluated during SAP MM MRP planning runs.']
  procurement_type varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the material is procured externally (purchased from supplier), produced in-house, or both. Drives SAP MM MRP to generate purchase requisitions vs. planned orders.']
  purchasing_organization varchar [note: 'SAP purchasing organization responsible for negotiating and executing supply contracts for this material. Defines the legal and organizational entity that issues purchase orders.']
  reorder_point_qty decimal(18,4) [note: 'Stock level threshold at which a purchase requisition is automatically triggered in SAP MM MRP. Expressed in the primary unit of measure (CWT, BU, or MT). When on-hand quantity falls to or below this value, replenishment is initiated.']
  rotation_method varchar [note: 'Inventory rotation method applied to this material: FIFO (First In First Out), FEFO (First Expired First Out), LIFO (Last In First Out), or manual. FEFO is mandatory for perishable commodities and chemicals with expiration dates per FSMA and HACCP requirements.']
  safety_stock_qty decimal(18,4) [note: 'Minimum buffer stock quantity maintained to protect against demand variability and supply lead time uncertainty. Expressed in primary UOM. Corresponds to SAP MM Safety Stock field in MRP 2 view.']
  shelf_life_days varchar [note: 'Maximum number of days this material can be stored before it expires or degrades below acceptable quality standards. Used to enforce FEFO rotation and calculate expiration dates from goods receipt date.']
  storage_condition varchar [note: 'Required storage environment for this material. Drives assignment to compatible storage locations (e.g., cold storage for perishables, hazmat-certified bins for chemicals). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ambient|refrigerated|frozen|controlled_atmosphere|dry|hazmat — promote to reference product]']
  uom_primary varchar [note: 'Primary unit of measure in which all quantity thresholds (reorder point, safety stock, maximum stock, EOQ) are expressed. Supports CWT (hundredweight), BU (bushel), and MT (metric ton) per agricultural inventory standards. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CWT|BU|MT|LB|KG|GAL|L|EA — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this reorder policy record was last modified. Used for change detection in downstream MRP planning runs and data pipeline incremental loads.']

  Note: 'Master configuration record defining reorder and replenishment policies for inventory-managed materials including seeds, chemicals, fertilizers, and feed. Captures material, storage location, reorder point quantity, safety stock level in CWT/BU/MT, maximum stock level, economic order quantity (EOQ), lead time days, preferred supplier reference, and seasonal demand flag. Drives automated purchase requisition creation in SAP MM MRP.'
}

  phi_days_remaining varchar [note: 'Number of days remaining in the Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) at the time the hold was initiated. A positive value indicates the crop was harvested before the PHI elapsed, which may be the root cause of an MRL exceedance hold.']
  qty_on_hold_bu decimal(18,4) [note: 'Quantity of inventory placed under quarantine hold expressed in bushels (BU). Standard unit for grain commodities (corn, soybeans, wheat) in US agricultural trade and USDA WASDE reporting.']
  qty_on_hold_cwt decimal(18,4) [note: 'Quantity of inventory placed under quarantine hold expressed in hundredweight (CWT). Primary unit for grain and commodity inventory valuation and trading in US agricultural markets.']
  qty_on_hold_mt decimal(18,4) [note: 'Quantity of inventory placed under quarantine hold expressed in metric tons (MT). Required for international trade documentation, EU regulatory reporting, and Codex Alimentarius compliance.']
  regulatory_notification_date date [note: 'Date on which the regulatory authority (FDA, USDA, EPA, EU RASFF) was formally notified of the quarantine hold or food safety event. Required for FSMA compliance documentation and EU RASFF reporting timelines.']
  regulatory_notification_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this quarantine hold requires mandatory notification to a regulatory authority (FDA, USDA FSIS, EPA, EU RASFF). True when the hold involves a food safety risk, MRL exceedance, or mandatory recall trigger.']
  regulatory_reference_number varchar [note: 'Official reference number assigned by the regulatory authority (FDA recall number, USDA FSIS case number, EU RASFF notification number, EPA enforcement action number) for tracking the regulatory response to this hold.']
  sap_qm_inspection_lot varchar [note: 'SAP QM inspection lot number associated with this quarantine hold. Links the hold to the formal quality inspection process and usage decision workflow in SAP S/4HANA QM module.']
  sap_qm_usage_decision varchar [note: 'SAP QM usage decision code recorded at inspection lot closure. A=Accept (release to unrestricted stock), R=Reject (block/destroy), B=Return to vendor, S=Sort/rework. Drives automatic stock transfer posting in SAP MM.']
  uom_primary varchar [note: 'The primary unit of measure used for inventory valuation and SAP MM stock management for this quarantine hold record. Determines which quantity field is the authoritative measure for disposition and reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CWT|BU|MT|KG|LB|EA|CS — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to the quarantine hold record. Supports change tracking, audit trail requirements, and Databricks Silver Layer incremental processing.']
  wms_hold_tag_number varchar [note: 'Physical hold tag or WMS blocking record number assigned by Manhattan Associates WMS to identify and segregate the quarantined inventory in the warehouse or storage facility.']

  Note: 'Transactional record managing inventory holds and quarantine status for lots or stock positions pending quality inspection, regulatory review, or food safety investigation. Captures hold number, material, lot, location, quantity on hold in CWT/BU/MT, hold type (quality, regulatory, safety, recall, customer_complaint), hold reason, initiating event reference (COA failure, HACCP deviation, MRL exceedance per EPA/EU Regulation 396/2005), hold start date, expected release date, actual release date, disposition decision (release, rework, destroy, return), and approver. Distinct from the vendor-level qualification_status on the vendor master, as a vendor may be globally approved but conditionally approved for a specific material category.']
  contracted_price decimal [note: 'Negotiated contracted price per base unit of measure for this vendor-material combination. Cannot reside on material_master (price varies by vendor) nor on vendor (price varies by material). Expressed in the vendor\'s invoicing currency.']
  lead_time_days varchar [note: 'Vendor-specific lead time in calendar days from purchase order placement to expected delivery for this material. Relationship-specific — the same vendor may have different lead times for different materials.']
  min_order_qty decimal [note: 'Minimum order quantity (in the material\'s base UOM) required by this vendor for this material. Relationship-specific commercial term that varies by vendor-material combination.']
  preferred_rank varchar [note: 'Numeric ranking of this vendor\'s preference for sourcing this material (1 = primary/preferred source, 2 = secondary, etc.). Used by procurement to determine sourcing priority when multiple approved vendors exist for the same material.']
  qualification_date date [note: 'Date on which this vendor was approved to supply this specific material. Relationship-specific — a vendor may be qualified for different materials on different dates.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Approved Vendor List (AVL) contract between material_master and vendor. It captures the operational qualification and commercial terms governing each approved vendor-material sourcing relationship in agricultural procurement. Each record links one material to one approved vendor and carries attributes — qualification status, preferred rank, contracted price, lead time, and minimum order quantity — that exist only in the context of this specific vendor-material pairing and cannot reside on either the material master or the vendor master alone.. Existence Justification: In agricultural procurement, a single material (e.g., glyphosate herbicide, hybrid corn seed, urea fertilizer) is routinely sourced from multiple approved vendors at different contracted prices, lead times, and minimum order quantities — and each vendor supplies many different materials. The business actively manages an Approved Vendor List (AVL) per material, tracking qualification status, preferred ranking, contracted pricing, and lead times for each vendor-material combination. This is a well-recognized operational concept in agriculture procurement that procurement teams create, update, and retire as supply agreements change.'
}

Table inventory.lot_allocation {
  lot_allocation_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the lot_allocation association']
  account_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking this allocation record to the customer account receiving the committed commodity quantity.']
  commodity_lot_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking this allocation record to the specific commodity lot from which quantity is being committed.']
  allocated_quantity_bu decimal [note: 'The quantity of the commodity lot committed to this customer account under this allocation, expressed in bushels. This value belongs to the allocation relationship — not to the lot (which tracks total on-hand) nor to the account (which does not own inventory).']
  allocation_date date [note: 'The date on which this allocation was created and committed, recording when the business decision to assign this lot quantity to this account was made. Used for FIFO/FEFO rotation audit trails and forward contract settlement timing.']
  allocation_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of this lot-to-account allocation. Drives fulfillment workflow: PENDING (created, awaiting confirmation), CONFIRMED (customer accepted), SHIPPED (quantity dispatched), INVOICED (billing complete), CANCELLED (allocation voided), ON_HOLD (suspended pending quality or compliance review).']
  contract_reference varchar [note: 'The forward contract number, sales order number, or purchase agreement identifier governing this allocation. Links the allocation to the originating commercial agreement. May reference a SAP SD sales order or an external grain trading platform contract ID.']
  price_per_bu decimal [note: 'The negotiated or contracted price per bushel for this specific lot-account allocation. Price varies by deal, contract terms, and market conditions — it belongs to the allocation, not to the lot (which has no single price) nor to the account (which has no per-lot price).']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Contract between commodity_lot and account in the agricultural commodity trading process. It captures the operational commitment of a specific quantity from a commodity lot to a customer account, typically governed by a forward contract or sales order. Each record links one commodity_lot to one account with attributes — allocated quantity, price, status, and contract reference — that exist only in the context of this allocation relationship and cannot reside on either the lot or the account alone.. Existence Justification: In agricultural commodity trading, a single commodity lot is routinely split and allocated to multiple customer accounts (e.g., a 50,000 bu corn lot sold in portions to three food manufacturers under separate forward contracts), and a customer account simultaneously holds allocations across many commodity lots. The business actively manages these allocations as operational records — creating, updating, and cancelling them — with quantity, price, status, and contract reference data that belongs to neither the lot nor the account alone. This is a recognized operational concept in grain trading known as a \'Lot Allocation\' or \'Commodity Allocation\'.'
}

Table inventory.lot_fulfillment {
  lot_fulfillment_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the lot_fulfillment association']
  commodity_lot_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the commodity lot being allocated or fulfilled against this delivery order']
  delivery_order_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the delivery order that this commodity lot (or portion thereof) is fulfilling']
  lot_number varchar [note: 'Batch or lot tracking identifier assigned to the commodity in this delivery. Enables end-to-end traceability from farm origin through customer delivery for FSMA compliance and recall management. [Moved from delivery_order: The lot_number string on delivery_order is a denormalized reference that can only capture a single lot per delivery order. In the true M:N business reality, a delivery order is fulfilled by multiple lots. This field should be removed from delivery_order and replaced by the lot_fulfillment association, which properly links delivery_order to multiple commodity_lot records via commodity_lot_id (which carries lot_number as an attribute).]']
  lot_split_pct decimal [note: 'The percentage of the total commodity lot quantity allocated to this specific delivery order. Supports FIFO/FEFO rotation tracking and lot consumption reporting when a single lot is split across multiple delivery orders.']
  moisture_at_delivery decimal [note: 'The moisture content percentage of this commodity lot measured at the time of delivery for this specific delivery order.   quality_grade_at_delivery varchar [note: 'The USDA or contractually specified quality grade confirmed for this specific lot at the time of delivery. May differ from the lot\'s master grade if re-grading occurred at load-out. Belongs to the lot-delivery pairing, not to either entity alone, and is used for quality settlement and contract compliance.']
  quantity_allocated_bu decimal [note: 'The quantity of this commodity lot allocated to this specific delivery order, expressed in bushels.
