Cannot reside on commodity_lot (which tracks total on-hand) or delivery_order (which tracks total ordered quantity) alone.']
  quantity_delivered_bu decimal [note: 'The actual quantity of this commodity lot that was physically delivered against this delivery order, expressed in bushels. May differ from quantity_allocated_bu due to scale tickets, shrinkage, or load adjustments. Used for quality settlement and inventory depletion.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the fulfillment event between a commodity_lot and a delivery_order in the agricultural supply chain. It captures the operational allocation of a specific commodity lot (or portion thereof) to a specific delivery order, recording quantity allocated, quantity actually delivered, lot split percentage, and quality measurements (grade and moisture) confirmed at the time of delivery. Each record links one commodity_lot to one delivery_order and carries attributes that exist only in the context of this specific lot-to-delivery pairing, supporting FSMA Section 204 traceability, quality settlement, and FIFO/FEFO rotation compliance.. Existence Justification: In grain trading and agricultural supply chain operations, a single delivery order is routinely fulfilled by blending or splitting multiple commodity lots (e.g., combining two partial bins of corn to meet a 50,000 BU delivery order), and a single commodity lot can be allocated across multiple delivery orders over time (e.g., a large 100,000 BU lot split across three separate customer deliveries). The business actively manages this lot-to-delivery allocation as an operational record — tracking quantity allocated, quality at delivery, and moisture per lot-delivery combination — for FSMA Section 204 traceability, quality settlement, and regulatory compliance. This is a recognized operational concept in grain merchandising known as \'lot allocation\' or \'lot fulfillment\', with its own data (quantity_allocated_bu, moisture_at_delivery, quality_grade_at_delivery) that belongs to neither the lot nor the delivery order alone.'
}

Table inventory.lot_pesticide_exposure {
  lot_pesticide_exposure_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the lot_pesticide_exposure association']
  commodity_lot_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the commodity lot whose PHI compliance status is being determined by this pesticide application exposure record.']
  pesticide_use_record_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the pesticide use record (PUR) that generated this exposure event for the associated commodity lot.']
  active_ingredient_name varchar [note: 'The active ingredient (AI) of the pesticide product as it applies to this lot\'s exposure record. Captured at the association level to support MRL (Maximum Residue Limit) checks and export compliance queries per lot without requiring a join to the PUR. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.']
  application_date date [note: 'The date of the pesticide application as it pertains to this specific lot\'s PHI compliance calculation. Sourced from the detection phase relationship data. Denormalized here to support lot-level PHI window calculations without requiring a join back to the PUR.']
  application_rate decimal [note: 'The application rate of the pesticide product relevant to this lot\'s exposure. Captured at the association level to support residue estimation and MRL compliance checks per lot. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.']
  area_treated decimal [note: 'The portion of the total treated area that is attributable to this specific commodity lot. A single application may cover an entire field, but individual lots may represent sub-parcels or harvest windows within that field. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.']
  exposure_determination_method varchar [note: 'The method by which this lot was determined to be exposed to this pesticide application — e.g., via GIS field boundary overlap, manual agronomist assignment, or system-derived parcel matching. Required for audit trail and regulatory defensibility.']
  phi_clearance_date date [note: 'The earliest date on which this commodity lot may be harvested while remaining compliant with the PHI for this specific pesticide application. Calculated as application_date + phi_days from the associated PUR. This derived date belongs to the association because it is specific to the lot-application pairing.']
  phi_compliant_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the commodity lot\'s actual or projected harvest date satisfies the Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) requirement for this specific pesticide application. This flag belongs to the association because the same PUR may be PHI-compliant for one lot (harvested later) and non-compliant for another (harvested earlier).']
  phi_date date [note: 'The Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) date — the earliest date on which the commodity could have been legally harvested after the last pesticide or chemical application, per EPA label requirements. Lots harvested before this date may have MRL (Maximum Residue Limit) violations. Critical for food safety compliance and FSMA traceability. [Moved from commodity_lot: The phi_date on commodity_lot is a single scalar that cannot represent the PHI clearance dates from MULTIPLE pesticide applications. The true PHI clearance date is the MAXIMUM phi_clearance_date across all associated PURs for that lot. The lot-level phi_date should be a derived/computed field (max of association phi_clearance_dates), not a stored attribute on the lot itself. The per-application PHI clearance date belongs to the lot_pesticide_exposure association.]']
  record_status varchar [note: 'Lifecycle status of this lot-application exposure record. PENDING = awaiting compliance review; CONFIRMED = PHI compliance determination finalized; DISPUTED = under review due to data discrepancy; SUPERSEDED = replaced by a corrected record.']
  review_date date [note: 'Date on which this lot-application exposure linkage was reviewed and confirmed by a compliance officer. Part of the regulatory audit trail for PHI compliance sign-off.']
  reviewed_by varchar [note: 'Name or user ID of the compliance officer or agronomist who reviewed and confirmed this lot-application exposure linkage. Required for regulatory audit trail.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the PHI Compliance Linkage event between a commodity_lot and a pesticide_use_record. It captures the regulatory determination of whether a specific pesticide application affects a specific commodity lot\'s pre-harvest interval compliance status. Each record links one commodity_lot to one pesticide_use_record and carries the compliance attributes that exist only in the context of this specific lot-application pairing — including the PHI compliance outcome, the area of the lot affected, and the active ingredient exposure details. Required for FSMA Section 204 traceability, EPA pesticide use reporting, and pre-harvest clearance workflows.. Existence Justification: In agricultural operations, a single commodity lot (harvested from a field over a season) is subject to multiple pesticide applications, each generating its own PUR — and a single pesticide application event can affect multiple commodity lots harvested from the same field across different harvest windows. The business actively manages this relationship to determine PHI compliance status for each lot, which is a regulatory obligation under EPA and FSMA rules. This is not an analytical correlation — it is an operational compliance record that agronomists and compliance officers create, query, and audit as part of pre-harvest clearance workflows.'
}

  regulatory_agency varchar [note: 'The regulatory authority to which this finding must be reported, if regulatory_reportable_flag is True. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: USDA|FDA|FSIS|EPA|APHIS|OSHA|state_agency|none — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  regulatory_reportable_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this finding must be reported to a regulatory authority (USDA, FDA, FSIS, EPA, APHIS). When True, triggers mandatory regulatory notification workflows and documentation requirements under FSMA, FSIS directives, or EPA regulations.']
  repeat_finding_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this finding is a recurrence of a previously identified non-conformance at the same location or process. Repeat findings trigger escalated corrective action requirements under GFSI schemes and may impact certification grade.']
  response_due_date date [note: 'Required deadline by which a corrective action plan or response must be submitted for this finding.   risk_severity_rating varchar [note: 'Risk-based severity assessment of the finding\'s potential impact on food safety, product quality, regulatory compliance, or business continuity.   sap_qm_notification_number varchar [note: 'The SAP S/4HANA QM module notification number corresponding to this finding. Enables bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse silver layer record and the operational system of record for corrective action management and ERP integration.']
  standard_clause_reference varchar [note: 'The specific clause, control point, element, or requirement number within the applicable standard scheme against which this finding was raised (e.g., FSMA 21 CFR Part 117.135, GLOBALG.A.P. CB.7.1, SQF Element 2.4.3, BRC Clause 4.11.2, IFS Requirement 4.18.1). Essential for certification body reporting and corrective action traceability.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Audit timestamp when this finding record was last modified. Tracks changes to status, corrective action assignments, or evidence updates for compliance audit trail purposes.']
  verified_closed_date date [note: 'Actual date on which the finding was verified as effectively closed following corrective action implementation. Populated by the verifying auditor or quality manager. Used to calculate closure cycle time and assess corrective action effectiveness.']

  Note: 'Individual findings, observations, and deficiencies identified during quality inspections or formal audits (internal, second-party, third-party certification). Records parent event reference and type (inspection or audit), finding classification (critical, major, minor, observation, opportunity for improvement), applicable standard clause reference (FSMA 21 CFR Part 117, GLOBALG.A.P. control point, SQF Element, BRC Clause, IFS requirement), description of non-conformance or observation, objective evidence, risk severity rating, required response timeline, and disposition. Unified SSOT for ALL quality findings regardless of detection context — replaces separate audit finding tracking. Drives corrective action generation and certification status updates.'
}

  gfsi_scheme varchar [note: 'GFSI-benchmarked certification scheme under which this HACCP plan is audited (Safe Quality Food (SQF), British Retail Consortium (BRC), International Featured Standards (IFS), FSSC 22000, or GLOBALG.A.P.). Drives audit scope and documentation requirements.']
  hazard_analysis_summary varchar [note: 'Narrative summary of the hazard analysis conducted for this plan, documenting the methodology used to identify and evaluate biological, chemical, and physical hazards at each process step. Corresponds to Codex Alimentarius Principle 1.']
  intended_use varchar [note: 'Documented intended use and consumer population for the product covered by this plan, including whether the product is intended for vulnerable populations (e.g., infants, immunocompromised). Informs hazard severity assessment.']
  last_review_date date [note: 'Date of the most recent formal reassessment or revalidation of the HACCP plan, triggered by process changes, new hazard information, regulatory updates, or scheduled periodic review. Required by FDA FSMA and GFSI schemes.']
  monitoring_frequency varchar [note: 'Frequency at which the monitoring parameter is measured at the CCP (e.g., continuous, every batch, hourly, per shift). Defined in the HACCP plan and enforced during production operations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: continuous|every_batch|hourly|every_2_hours|daily|per_shift|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  monitoring_method varchar [note: 'Description of the procedure, instrument, or technique used to monitor the CCP parameter (e.g., \'Calibrated digital thermometer\', \'Inline pH meter\', \'Metal detector test piece challenge\'). Supports equipment calibration traceability.']
  monitoring_parameter varchar [note: 'The physical or chemical parameter measured at the CCP to verify the critical limit is being met (e.g., temperature in °C, pH, chlorine concentration in ppm, metal detector sensitivity in mm). Corresponds to Codex Alimentarius Principle 4. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: temperature|pH|chlorine_concentration|metal_detector_sensitivity|water_activity|time|pressure|flow_rate|turbidity|conductivity|other — promote to reference product]']
  next_review_date date [note: 'Date by which the next formal reassessment of the HACCP plan must be completed. Used for compliance calendar management and audit readiness tracking.']
  open_corrective_actions varchar [note: 'Count of corrective action records currently open and unresolved against this HACCP plan. Used for compliance dashboard monitoring and audit readiness assessment. Zero indicates full compliance.']
  physical_hazards_identified boolean [note: 'Indicates whether physical hazards (e.g., metal fragments, glass, bone, hard plastic, stones) were identified as significant hazards requiring a CCP such as metal detection or X-ray inspection in this HACCP plan.']
  plan_name varchar [note: 'Descriptive human-readable name of the HACCP plan, typically referencing the commodity, process line, or facility scope (e.g., \'Fresh-Cut Leafy Greens Processing — Facility A\').']
  plan_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique alphanumeric identifier for the HACCP plan, used in regulatory submissions, audit documentation, and cross-system references (e.g., SAP QM inspection lot linkage). Format: HACCP-{FACILITY_CODE}-{YEAR}-{SEQ}.']
  plan_scope varchar [note: 'Defines the operational scope of the HACCP plan — whether it covers an entire facility, a specific process line, a commodity category, or a specific finished product. Determines applicability during audits.']
  plan_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the HACCP plan. \'active\' indicates the plan is in operational use; \'under_review\' indicates a scheduled reassessment is in progress; \'suspended\' indicates temporary halt pending corrective action; \'superseded\' indicates replaced by a newer version.']
  plan_version varchar [note: 'Version number of the HACCP plan document, incremented upon each formal review or revision cycle. Supports document control and audit trail requirements (e.g., \'1.0\', \'2.3\').']
  prerequisite_programs varchar [note: 'List of prerequisite programs (PRPs) supporting this HACCP plan, such as Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), sanitation standard operating procedures (SSOPs), pest control, and allergen management programs. PRPs are foundational controls that underpin the HACCP system.']
  process_description varchar [note: 'Narrative description of the production or processing scope covered by this HACCP plan, including process flow steps from raw material receipt through finished product dispatch. Required by Codex Alimentarius Step 4 (process flow diagram description).']
  recordkeeping_requirements varchar [note: 'Description of the records that must be maintained to document HACCP plan implementation, including monitoring logs, corrective action records, verification records, and retention periods. Corresponds to Codex Alimentarius Principle 7.']
  regulatory_framework varchar [note: 'Primary regulatory or certification framework under which this HACCP plan was developed and is maintained (e.g., FDA FSMA Preventive Controls, FSIS HACCP, GFSI scheme such as SQF or BRC). Determines audit requirements and record retention obligations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA_FSMA|FSIS_HACCP|USDA_NOP|GLOBALG.A.P.|SQF|BRC|IFS|ISO_22000|Codex_Alimentarius|EU_852_2004|other — promote to reference product]']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to this HACCP plan record in the system. Used for change tracking, version control, and data synchronization with SAP QM module.']
  verification_procedure varchar [note: 'Documented activities used to confirm the HACCP plan is functioning effectively, including calibration schedules, record review, periodic product testing, and internal audits. Corresponds to Codex Alimentarius Principle 6.']

  Note: 'HACCP (Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points) plan master records with embedded CCP monitoring logs for each production process, commodity, or facility. Plan-level: defines process scope, hazard analysis summary, identified biological/chemical/physical hazards, critical control points (CCPs), critical limits, monitoring procedures, corrective action procedures, verification activities, and record-keeping requirements. CCP monitoring log detail: captures real-time or periodic measurements at each CCP including monitoring parameter (temperature, pH, chlorine concentration, metal detector sensitivity), measured value, critical limit, monitoring frequency, operator identity, timestamp, deviation flag, and immediate corrective action taken. Provides both the plan framework and continuous compliance evidence required by FDA FSMA Preventive Controls rule and GFSI scheme auditors (SQF, BRC, IFS).'
}

Table quality.quality_standard {
  quality_standard_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for quality_standard']

  applicable_product_categories varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of product categories or commodity groups to which this quality standard applies (e.g., fresh produce, dairy, meat and poultry, processed foods, animal feed, packaging materials). Defines the scope of products covered.']
  audit_frequency_months varchar [note: 'Required frequency for third-party audits or internal assessments against this quality standard, expressed in months (e.g., 12 for annual, 24 for biennial). Null if no periodic audit is required.']
  certification_body varchar [note: 'Name of the accredited organization that issues or governs this quality standard (e.g., SQFI, BRC Global Standards, IFS Management GmbH, GLOBALG.A.P. c/o FoodPLUS GmbH, NSF International, SGS, Bureau Veritas). Null for internal or non-certified standards.']
  certification_duration_months varchar [note: 'Validity period of certification issued under this quality standard, expressed in months (e.g., 12, 24, 36). After this period, recertification audit is required. Null for non-certification standards.']
  corrective_action_timeframe_days varchar [note: 'Maximum number of days allowed to implement corrective actions for non-conformances identified during audits or assessments under this quality standard. Timeframe varies by severity of finding (e.g., 30 days for major, 90 days for minor).']
  country_codes varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes where this quality standard is applicable or recognized (e.g., USA, CAN, MEX, DEU, GBR, CHN). Null for global standards applicable everywhere.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this quality standard record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.']
  critical_defect_threshold varchar [note: 'Maximum number of critical non-conformances allowed before automatic failure of audit or assessment. Critical defects are findings that pose immediate food safety risk or regulatory violation. Zero tolerance is common for many food safety standards.']
  documentation_requirements varchar [note: 'Description of mandatory documentation, records, and evidence that must be maintained to demonstrate compliance with this quality standard (e.g., HACCP plans, SOPs, training records, COA files, corrective action logs, supplier approvals).']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date when this version of the quality standard becomes enforceable or recommended for adoption. Organizations must comply with the standard from this date forward for new certifications or audits.']
  expiration_date date [note: 'Date when this version of the quality standard is superseded or retired. After this date, organizations must transition to the next version. Null for standards with indefinite validity.']
  geographic_scope varchar [note: 'Geographic applicability of the quality standard. Global standards apply worldwide (ISO, GFSI schemes), regional standards apply to multi-country regions (EU regulations), national standards apply to a single country (USDA, FDA), state standards apply to sub-national jurisdictions, and local standards apply to specific municipalities or districts.']
  gfsi_recognized_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this quality standard is benchmarked and recognized by the Global Food Safety Initiative (GFSI). GFSI recognition is a key requirement for many global retailers and food manufacturers. True if GFSI-recognized, false otherwise.']
  internal_owner_department varchar [note: 'Name of the internal department or business unit responsible for managing compliance with this quality standard (e.g., Quality Assurance, Food Safety, Regulatory Affairs, Operations). Used for accountability and audit coordination.']
  issuing_authority varchar [note: 'Regulatory or governing body that mandates or oversees the standard (e.g., USDA, FDA, FSIS, European Commission, Codex Alimentarius, state agriculture departments). Applicable for regulatory and industry standards.']
  last_reviewed_date date [note: 'Date when this quality standard was last reviewed by internal quality management team for continued applicability, accuracy, and alignment with business needs. Used to ensure master data currency and trigger periodic reviews.']
  last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this quality standard record was most recently modified. Used for audit trail, change tracking, and data freshness monitoring.']
  major_defect_threshold varchar [note: 'Maximum number of major non-conformances allowed before failure of audit or assessment. Major defects are significant deviations from standard requirements that could lead to food safety issues if not corrected.']
  minimum_score_required decimal(5,2) [note: 'Minimum audit score or compliance percentage required to achieve certification or pass assessment under this quality standard (e.g., 80.00 for 80% compliance). Null if the standard does not use numeric scoring.']
  next_review_date date [note: 'Scheduled date for the next periodic review of this quality standard record. Used to trigger proactive review workflows and ensure master data remains current with evolving regulatory and industry requirements.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional information, special considerations, implementation guidance, or historical context related to this quality standard. Used to capture nuances not covered by structured fields.']
  reference_document_url varchar [note: 'Web URL link to the official published standard document, guidance materials, or certification body website where the full standard text and requirements can be accessed.']
  regulatory_mandate_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether compliance with this quality standard is legally required by government regulation (e.g., FSMA Preventive Controls, HACCP for seafood and juice). True if mandated by law, false if voluntary or industry-driven.']
  scope_description varchar [note: 'Detailed description of what the quality standard covers, including applicable products, processes, facilities, and supply chain stages. Defines the boundaries of compliance requirements and audit scope.']
  standard_category varchar [note: 'Primary functional category of the quality standard. Food safety covers pathogen control and contamination prevention (HACCP, FSMA), quality management covers systematic quality assurance (ISO 9001, SQF), good agricultural practices cover on-farm production (GLOBALG.A.P.), good manufacturing practices cover processing facility operations (GMP, cGMP), hazard analysis covers risk assessment methodologies (HACCP principles), and traceability covers supply chain tracking (PTI, FSMA 204).']
  standard_code varchar [note: 'Unique business identifier code for the quality standard (e.g., SQF-2000, BRC-8, IFS-7, HACCP-001, GAP-V5). Used for external reference and certification documentation.']
  standard_name varchar [note: 'Full official name of the quality standard (e.g., Safe Quality Food Level 2, British Retail Consortium Global Standard for Food Safety, International Featured Standards Food).']
  standard_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the quality standard by its origin and enforcement mechanism. Certification standards are third-party verified (GFSI schemes), regulatory are government-mandated (FDA, USDA, FSIS), internal are company-defined, industry are sector-wide best practices, customer-specific are buyer requirements, and voluntary are optional compliance frameworks.']
  status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the quality standard. Active standards are in force and enforceable, superseded standards have been replaced by newer versions, draft standards are under development, under review standards are being evaluated for adoption, retired standards are no longer applicable, and suspended standards are temporarily not enforced.']
  supplier_approval_requirements varchar [note: 'Description of supplier qualification, approval, and monitoring requirements mandated by this quality standard (e.g., supplier audits, COA review, risk-based supplier verification, FSMA Foreign Supplier Verification Program requirements).']
  testing_protocol_requirements varchar [note: 'Description of mandatory testing, sampling, and analytical methods required by this quality standard (e.g., pathogen testing frequency, MRL testing protocols, environmental monitoring programs, finished product testing specifications).']
  traceability_requirements varchar [note: 'Description of traceability and supply chain tracking requirements mandated by this quality standard (e.g., one-up/one-back traceability, lot coding requirements, recall readiness, FSMA 204 Key Data Elements for high-risk foods).']
  training_requirements varchar [note: 'Description of mandatory training programs and competency requirements for personnel involved in activities covered by this quality standard (e.g., HACCP training for food safety team, GMP training for production staff, auditor qualification requirements).']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Version or edition number of the quality standard (e.g., 8.0, 7.1, V5.2). Quality standards are periodically revised to incorporate new science, regulatory changes, and industry best practices.']

  Note: 'Master reference table for quality_standard. Referenced by quality_standard_id.'
}

Table weather.station {
  station_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique system-generated surrogate identifier for the weather station master record. Primary key for all downstream observation, forecast, and derived weather product references.']
  employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the SAP SuccessFactors employee record of the technician or agronomist responsible for this station\'s maintenance, calibration scheduling, and data quality oversight.']
  farm_unit_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the farm or agricultural production unit with which this station is primarily associated. Enables linkage of meteorological observations to crop plans, irrigation events, and yield records within the Granular Farm Management and John Deere Operations Center systems.']
  field_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific field or land parcel most closely associated with this station. Supports field-level weather data attribution for planting windows, spray windows, and pest pressure prediction in Trimble Ag Software and Climate FieldView.']
  network_id varchar [note: 'Identifier assigned by the external data provider network (e.g., DTN network node ID, Climate FieldView station UUID, NOAA COOP network ID). Used for data feed reconciliation and provider-side traceability.']
  zone_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to weather.weather_zone. Business justification: A weather station belongs to one geographic weather zone; a zone contains many stations. This FK normalizes the zone membership of each station and enables zone-level aggregation of station data. weat']
  anemometer_height_m decimal(5,2) [note: 'Height above ground level in meters at which the wind speed sensor (anemometer) is mounted. Required for FAO-56 Penman-Monteith reference evapotranspiration (ET) calculations and wind speed standardization to the 2-meter reference height used in irrigation scheduling.']
  calibration_method varchar [note: 'Method used during the most recent calibration event. Determines the level of measurement traceability and acceptability for regulatory and insurance documentation. NIST-traceable calibration is required for USDA crop insurance documentation.']
  calibration_technician varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the technician or certified service provider who performed the most recent calibration. Required for audit trail and regulatory documentation under FSMA and USDA crop insurance standards.']
  calibration_tolerance_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Acceptable measurement tolerance threshold expressed as a percentage of full-scale reading, as defined in the station\'s calibration specification. Used to evaluate pass/fail status during calibration and set the out_of_tolerance_flag.']
  communication_protocol varchar [note: 'Data transmission protocol used by the station to relay observations to the central data platform. Determines data latency, reliability SLA, and applicable IoT integration configuration in the FMIS. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: cellular_4g|cellular_5g|lora_wan|wifi|satellite|rf_radio|ethernet — promote to reference product]']
  data_provider varchar [note: 'Organization or platform supplying meteorological data for this station. Determines data licensing, feed format, latency SLA, and applicable data quality standards. Key for WASDE and DTN market data integration traceability. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: dtn|climate_fieldview|on_farm_iot|trimble|granular|noaa|private — promote to reference product]']
  data_quality_rating varchar [note: 'Enterprise data quality tier assigned to this station based on calibration history, uptime percentage, sensor completeness, and data gap frequency. Gold-rated stations are used for regulatory and insurance submissions; Silver for operational decisions; Bronze for supplemental reference only.']
  data_transmission_interval_min varchar [note: 'Configured frequency in minutes at which the station transmits observation data to the central platform. Drives data freshness expectations for real-time irrigation scheduling, spray window alerts, and frost/freeze notifications.']
  decommission_date date [note: 'Calendar date on which the weather station was permanently taken out of service. Null for active stations. Used to bound the valid observation record window for historical analysis and regulatory documentation.']
  elevation_m decimal(8,2) [note: 'Station elevation above mean sea level in meters. Critical for barometric pressure correction, evapotranspiration (ET) calculations, frost/freeze risk modeling, and accurate temperature lapse-rate adjustments in crop protection and irrigation scheduling.']
  installation_date date [note: 'Calendar date on which the weather station was physically installed and commissioned at its current location. Defines the start of the station\'s valid observation record for historical data analysis and crop insurance documentation.']
  insurance_eligible_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this station meets USDA Risk Management Agency (RMA) requirements for use as an approved weather data source in crop insurance loss documentation. Requires current calibration, gold data quality rating, and WMO or NOAA network registration.']
  iot_device_serial varchar [note: 'Manufacturer serial number of the IoT sensor node hardware for on-farm stations. Used for warranty tracking, firmware update management, and hardware replacement traceability. Null for DTN reference and cooperative network stations.']
  last_calibration_date date [note: 'Date of the most recent completed calibration of the station\'s primary sensors. Critical for data quality assurance, regulatory documentation under FSMA, and crop insurance measurement accuracy attestation.']
  last_maintenance_date date [note: 'Date of the most recent preventive or corrective maintenance activity performed on the station. Used to schedule next maintenance in SAP PM and assess station reliability for data quality rating.']
  latitude decimal(10,7) [note: 'Geographic latitude of the station in decimal degrees (WGS84 datum), captured via GPS/RTK positioning. Used for GIS spatial analysis in Esri ArcGIS, field-to-station proximity matching, and precision agriculture variable rate application (VRA) zone assignment.']
  leaf_wetness_sensor_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this station is equipped with a leaf wetness sensor. Critical for spray window determination (REI compliance), fungal disease pressure modeling under IPM programs, and GLOBALG.A.P. crop protection documentation.']
  longitude decimal(10,7) [note: 'Geographic longitude of the station in decimal degrees (WGS84 datum), captured via GPS/RTK positioning. Used for GIS spatial analysis, field mapping in John Deere Operations Center, and spatial interpolation of weather data across farm units.']
  manufacturer varchar [note: 'Name of the hardware manufacturer of the weather station or IoT sensor node (e.g., Davis Instruments, Campbell Scientific, Onset HOBO, Pessl Instruments). Used for maintenance scheduling, parts procurement, and calibration procedure selection.']
  model_number varchar [note: 'Manufacturer model designation of the weather station hardware. Determines applicable calibration procedures, sensor specifications, and maintenance SOPs referenced in SAP PM.']
  next_calibration_date date [note: 'Scheduled date for the next calibration of the station\'s sensors. Used to trigger maintenance work orders in SAP PM and ensure continuous data quality compliance for regulatory and insurance documentation.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for operational notes, site-specific observations, known data anomalies, or special instructions relevant to this station\'s operation and data interpretation. Used by field agronomists and data quality teams.']
  operational_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the weather station. Drives data quality flags on all downstream observation records and determines whether the station is included in active irrigation scheduling, spray window, and GDD accumulation calculations.']
  out_of_tolerance_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the most recent calibration found one or more sensors outside the acceptable tolerance range. When True, downstream observation records from this station are flagged for data quality review and excluded from regulatory and insurance submissions until recalibration is completed.']
  power_source varchar [note: 'Primary power supply type for the weather station. Determines maintenance requirements, uptime risk profile, and applicable preventive maintenance schedule in SAP PM. Solar and battery stations require periodic battery health checks.']
  record_created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this weather station master record was first created in the enterprise data platform. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and Silver layer ingestion traceability.']
  record_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to this weather station master record. Used for change data capture (CDC) in the Databricks Silver layer pipeline and audit trail compliance.']
  sensor_inventory varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of sensor types installed on this station (e.g., \'temperature,humidity,precipitation,wind_speed,wind_direction,solar_radiation,soil_moisture,leaf_wetness\'). Defines which observation parameters are available from this station for ET, GDD, and IPM calculations.']
  soil_moisture_sensor_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this station includes in-ground soil moisture sensors. Enables direct soil water content measurement for irrigation scheduling decisions and supports NDVI-correlated crop stress analysis.']
  solar_radiation_sensor_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this station is equipped with a pyranometer or solar radiation sensor. Required for FAO-56 Penman-Monteith ET calculations; stations without this sensor must use estimated solar radiation from sunshine hours or cloud cover data.']
  station_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier for the station, used in field operations, DTN data feeds, Climate FieldView integrations, and regulatory/insurance documentation. Unique across the enterprise station network.']
  station_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable descriptive name for the weather station, typically referencing the associated farm unit, field block, or geographic landmark (e.g., \'North Creek Field Station - Block 4\'). Used in reporting, dashboards, and operator interfaces.']
  station_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the station by its physical deployment and data-provider category. Drives data ingestion pipeline routing and quality thresholds. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fixed_field|portable_iot|dtn_reference|climate_fieldview|cooperative|airport — promote to reference product if additional types emerge]']
  temperature_sensor_height_m decimal(5,2) [note: 'Height above ground level in meters at which the temperature and humidity sensors are mounted. Standard WMO siting requires 1.25–2.0 m. Deviations affect GDD accumulation accuracy and frost/freeze alert thresholds.']
  wmo_station_number varchar [note: 'Official WMO-assigned 5 or 6-digit station identifier for stations registered with the global meteorological network. Null for private on-farm IoT nodes not registered with WMO. Required for NOAA and DTN data feed cross-referencing.']

  Note: 'Master record for meteorological observation stations including fixed field stations, portable IoT sensor nodes, and DTN network reference points. Stores station identity, GPS/GIS coordinates, elevation, installation date, operational status, data provider (DTN, Climate FieldView, on-farm IoT), associated field or farm unit linkage, and complete sensor/instrument inventory with calibration history (sensor identifier, calibration date, method, pre/post calibration readings, acceptable tolerance range, calibration technician, next scheduled calibration date, out-of-tolerance flag). SSOT for station identity, instrument health, sensor calibration traceability, and data quality assurance referenced by all observation, forecast, and derived weather products. Supports regulatory and insurance documentation of measurement accuracy.'
}

Table weather.observation {
  observation_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique system-generated identifier for each meteorological observation record. Primary key for the weather observation time-series table in the Silver Layer lakehouse.']
  field_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the agricultural field or land parcel associated with this observation, enabling field-level weather correlation for irrigation scheduling, spray window determination, and crop insurance documentation.']
  station_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the weather station or IoT field sensor that captured this observation. Links to the station master record for location, calibration, and ownership metadata.']
  weather_station_id varchar [note: 'FK to weather.weather_station.weather_station_id — Every weather observation is captured at a specific station. Without this FK, weather data cannot be attributed to a location — breaking all spatial weather queries and field-level weather correlation']
  barometric_pressure_hpa decimal(7,2) [note: 'Atmospheric pressure measured during the observation interval, in hectopascals (hPa). Used for weather front detection, storm prediction, and calibration of altitude-adjusted ET calculations. Supports short-term weather forecasting for field operations planning.']
  created_at timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this observation record was first ingested and created in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Used for audit trail, data freshness monitoring, and SLA compliance tracking for weather data feeds.']
  data_source varchar [note: 'Identifies the originating system or feed that provided this observation record. Supports data lineage, quality weighting, and source reconciliation across IoT field sensors, DTN weather feeds, Climate FieldView integrations, and manual entries.']
  dew_point_c decimal(6,2) [note: 'Dew point temperature in degrees Celsius, representing the temperature at which air becomes saturated with moisture. Used for frost risk prediction, fungal disease pressure modeling (e.g., gray mold, downy mildew), and spray window determination under IPM frameworks.']
  et_mm decimal(7,3) [note: 'Reference evapotranspiration (ET₀) calculated for the observation interval using the FAO-56 Penman-Monteith method, in millimeters. SSOT for irrigation scheduling, water balance modeling, and crop water use estimation. Integrates with Climate FieldView and Granular Farm Management irrigation modules.']
  frost_alert boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether this observation triggered a frost or freeze alert condition (temperature at or below 0°C). Drives automated notifications for frost protection actions (e.g., wind machine activation, irrigation frost protection), crop insurance event documentation, and PHI compliance tracking.']
  gdd_base10_c decimal(7,2) [note: 'Growing Degree Day (GDD) accumulation for the observation interval using a base temperature of 10°C, calculated as max(0, (temp_max_c + temp_min_c)/2 - 10). Used for crop phenology tracking, pest emergence prediction, and harvest timing optimization. Standard base for corn and many broadacre crops.']
  interval varchar [note: 'Configured measurement interval for this observation record. Determines the temporal resolution of the time-series data. Supported intervals: 5-minute, 15-minute, hourly, and daily aggregations. Drives GDD and ET calculation granularity.']
  leaf_wetness_hours decimal(5,2) [note: 'Duration of leaf surface wetness during the observation interval, in hours. Critical input for fungal and bacterial disease pressure models under IPM frameworks (e.g., fire blight, late blight, botrytis). Drives spray timing recommendations and PHI (Pre-Harvest Interval) compliance tracking.']
  observation_status varchar [note: 'Quality lifecycle status of the observation record. Raw records are ingested as-is; validated records have passed QC checks; flagged records have anomalies under review; corrected records have been adjusted; rejected records are excluded from downstream calculations.']
  observation_type varchar [note: 'Classifies whether the record represents an instantaneous point reading, an interval average, a daily summary aggregation, or a forecast value ingested from DTN or WASDE feeds. Drives downstream processing logic for GDD and ET calculations.']
  observed_at timestamp [note: 'ISO 8601 timestamp of when the meteorological measurement was captured at the sensor or station. This is the principal real-world event time used for time-series analysis, GDD accumulation, ET computation, and crop insurance documentation. Stored in yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX format.']
  precipitation_mm decimal(8,2) [note: 'Total liquid precipitation (rainfall) accumulated during the observation interval, in millimeters. Core input for irrigation scheduling, water balance calculations, crop insurance loss documentation, and FSMA water quality compliance tracking.']
  qc_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes from the automated QC process or manual data reviewer describing the reason for a suspect, fail, or estimated quality flag. Supports audit trail requirements for crop insurance documentation and FSMA traceability.']
  quality_flag varchar [note: 'WMO-aligned quality control flag for the observation record. Pass = all values within expected range; Suspect = one or more values outside climatological bounds but not definitively erroneous; Fail = confirmed erroneous values; Missing = one or more required measurements absent; Estimated = gap-filled using interpolation or neighboring station data.']
  relative_humidity_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Relative humidity as a percentage (0–100%) measured during the observation interval. Critical input for spray window determination (REI compliance), fungal disease pressure modeling under IPM frameworks, and ET calculation via the Penman-Monteith method.']
  sensor_depth_cm decimal(5,1) [note: 'Depth below the soil surface at which soil temperature and soil moisture readings were captured, in centimeters. Required for multi-depth sensor arrays to correctly attribute readings to the appropriate soil horizon. Null for atmospheric measurements.']
  sensor_height_m decimal(4,1) [note: 'Height above ground level at which atmospheric measurements (temperature, humidity, wind) were captured, in meters. Standard WMO height is 2m for temperature/humidity and 10m for wind. Required for ET calculation height corrections and data quality validation.']
  snowfall_mm decimal(8,2) [note: 'Snowfall accumulation during the observation interval expressed as millimeters of water equivalent. Used for spring soil moisture forecasting, field access planning, and crop insurance documentation in winter crop regions.']
  soil_moisture_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Volumetric soil moisture content as a percentage of field capacity, measured at the sensor depth. Core input for irrigation scheduling decisions, drought stress monitoring, and VRA (Variable Rate Application) prescription generation. Integrates with John Deere Operations Center and Trimble Ag Software.']
  soil_temperature_c decimal(6,2) [note: 'Soil temperature measured at the sensor depth during the observation interval, in degrees Celsius. Used for planting window determination (germination threshold monitoring), soil microbial activity modeling, and fertilizer application timing optimization.']
  solar_radiation_wm2 decimal(8,2) [note: 'Incoming solar radiation (shortwave) measured during the observation interval, in watts per square meter (W/m²). Primary driver of ET (Evapotranspiration) calculations via the Penman-Monteith method and NDVI-based crop growth modeling. Also used for solar energy resource assessment on farm.']
  source_record_code varchar [note: 'Original record identifier from the upstream source system (e.g., DTN feed message ID, Climate FieldView observation UUID, John Deere Operations Center telemetry record ID). Enables end-to-end data lineage tracing from raw ingestion to Silver Layer.']
  spray_window_open boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether current meteorological conditions (wind speed, temperature, relative humidity, precipitation) meet the criteria for a safe and compliant pesticide or fertilizer application window. Derived from EPA label requirements and IPM BMP thresholds. Supports REI and PHI compliance.']
  temperature_avg_c decimal(6,2) [note: 'Mean air temperature for the observation interval, in degrees Celsius. Computed as (max + min) / 2 for daily intervals or as a true average for sub-daily intervals. Primary input for ET (Evapotranspiration) calculations and irrigation scheduling models.']
  temperature_max_c decimal(6,2) [note: 'Maximum air temperature recorded during the observation interval, in degrees Celsius. Used for GDD (Growing Degree Day) accumulation calculations, heat stress threshold monitoring, and crop insurance documentation. Paired with temperature_min_c for daily range analysis.']
  temperature_min_c decimal(6,2) [note: 'Minimum air temperature recorded during the observation interval, in degrees Celsius. Critical for frost/freeze alert generation, GDD base temperature calculations, chilling hour accumulation, and crop protection decision support.']
  updated_at timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this observation record was last modified in the Silver Layer, such as after QC correction, status change, or data enrichment. Supports audit trail and change data capture (CDC) for downstream consumers.']
  wind_direction_deg decimal(5,1) [note: 'Prevailing wind direction during the observation interval, expressed in meteorological degrees (0–360°, where 0/360 = North). Used for spray drift modeling, pesticide application compliance, and field-level wind exposure analysis.']
  wind_gust_ms decimal(6,2) [note: 'Maximum instantaneous wind gust speed recorded during the observation interval, in meters per second. Used for equipment safety alerts, spray application go/no-go decisions, and crop lodging risk assessment.']
  wind_speed_ms decimal(6,2) [note: 'Average wind speed during the observation interval, in meters per second. Used for spray window determination (drift risk assessment), ET calculation, and wind damage risk alerts. EPA pesticide label compliance requires wind speed checks before application.']

  Note: 'Time-series transactional record of actual meteorological measurements captured at a weather station or IoT field sensor. Stores instantaneous or interval readings for temperature (min/max/avg in °F/°C), precipitation (rainfall/snowfall in inches/mm), relative humidity (%), wind speed (mph) and direction, barometric pressure (inHg/hPa), solar radiation (W/m²), dew point, and leaf wetness duration (hours). Timestamped to ISO 8601 with configurable interval (5-min, 15-min, hourly, daily). SSOT for all raw weather measurements; feeds GDD calculation, ET computation, irrigation scheduling, spray window determination, and crop insurance documentation.'
}

Table weather.forecast {
  forecast_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique system-generated identifier for each meteorological forecast record in the agricultural weather domain.']
  field_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the agricultural field polygon for which this forecast is generated, enabling field-level planting window and spray window decisions. Sourced from Esri ArcGIS field mapping or Climate FieldView.']
  station_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the weather station or IoT field sensor from which this forecast is anchored or associated. Links to the weather station master record.']
  cloud_cover_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Forecast percentage of sky covered by clouds for the valid period. Influences solar radiation estimates used in ET evapotranspiration calculations and NDVI Normalized Difference Vegetation Index interpretation.']
  confidence_interval_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Quantitative confidence interval expressed as a percentage (e.g., 90 for a 90% confidence interval) associated with the forecast values. Supports probabilistic risk assessment for crop insurance documentation and WASDE-aligned seasonal outlooks.']
  confidence_level varchar [note: 'Qualitative confidence level assigned by the forecast provider indicating the reliability of this forecast record. High confidence forecasts are used for firm operational commitments; low confidence forecasts trigger contingency planning.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this forecast record was first ingested into the agricultural data lakehouse. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and Silver Layer processing compliance. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  dew_point_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Forecast dew point temperature in degrees Celsius for the valid period. Used in disease pressure models (e.g., fungal blight risk) and to assess condensation risk on crops and equipment.']
  elevation_m decimal(7,2) [note: 'Elevation of the forecast location above mean sea level in meters. Influences temperature lapse rate adjustments, frost risk calculations, and ET evapotranspiration estimates for high-altitude agricultural fields.']
  et_forecast_mm decimal(7,3) [note: 'Forecast reference evapotranspiration (ET) in millimeters for the valid period, calculated using the FAO Penman-Monteith method. Primary input for irrigation scheduling decisions and water resource management in Climate FieldView and Trimble Ag Software.']
  external_forecast_ref varchar [note: 'Externally assigned identifier or reference code from the source forecast provider (e.g., NOAA NWS product ID, DTN forecast package ID, Climate FieldView forecast run ID). Enables traceability back to the originating provider record for dispute resolution and data quality audits.']
  forecast_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the forecast record. Active forecasts are in use for operational decisions; superseded forecasts have been replaced by a newer issue; expired forecasts have passed their valid period; cancelled forecasts were withdrawn by the provider.']
  forecast_type varchar [note: 'Temporal resolution and horizon of the forecast record. Hourly forecasts support spray window scheduling; daily and 7-day support planting window decisions; seasonal forecasts align with WASDE outlooks and crop insurance documentation.']
  freeze_risk boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether forecast minimum temperature is at or below -2.2°C (28°F), triggering a hard freeze alert. Distinguishes from frost risk for crop damage severity classification and crop insurance loss event documentation.']
  frost_risk boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether forecast minimum temperature is at or below 0°C, triggering a frost alert. Supports frost protection decisions including irrigation-based frost protection, smudge pot activation, and harvest acceleration.']
  gdd_base_temp_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Base temperature in degrees Celsius used in the GDD growing degree day calculation for this forecast record. Varies by crop species (e.g., 10°C for corn, 4.4°C for wheat). Ensures GDD values are interpreted correctly for the target crop.']
  gdd_forecast decimal(7,2) [note: 'Forecast growing degree day accumulation for the valid period, calculated from forecast max and min temperatures relative to a crop-specific base temperature. Supports crop development stage prediction, pest emergence timing, and planting window optimization.']
  horizon_hours varchar [note: 'Number of hours from the issued timestamp to the end of the forecast valid period. Indicates how far into the future the forecast extends, supporting confidence assessment and operational planning lead time.']
  humidity_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Forecast relative humidity as a percentage for the valid period. Influences fungal disease pressure prediction, spray efficacy windows, and ET evapotranspiration calculations for irrigation scheduling.']
  issued_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the forecast was officially issued or published by the source provider. Used to determine forecast freshness and to sequence superseding forecast versions. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  latitude decimal(9,6) [note: 'Decimal latitude coordinate of the forecast location or field polygon centroid. Used for spatial alignment with GIS field maps and IoT sensor networks. Expressed in decimal degrees (WGS84).']
  longitude decimal(9,6) [note: 'Decimal longitude coordinate of the forecast location or field polygon centroid. Used for spatial alignment with GIS field maps and IoT sensor networks. Expressed in decimal degrees (WGS84).']
  model_version varchar [note: 'Version identifier of the numerical weather prediction model used to generate this forecast (e.g., GFS 16.3.0, NAM 4.1, ECMWF CY47R3). Enables traceability and reproducibility of forecast-driven agricultural decisions for audit and compliance purposes.']
  precip_amount_mm decimal(7,2) [note: 'Forecast total precipitation amount in millimeters for the valid period. Used for irrigation scheduling decisions, soil moisture modeling, and crop insurance documentation under USDA Risk Management Agency guidelines.']
  precip_probability_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Forecast probability of measurable precipitation occurring during the valid period, expressed as a percentage (0–100). Key input for spray window scheduling — high probability suppresses pesticide application recommendations per IPM Integrated Pest Management protocols.']
  precip_type varchar [note: 'Forecast type of precipitation expected during the valid period. Distinguishes rain from snow, hail, or freezing rain, which have different implications for field operations, equipment deployment, and crop damage risk assessment.']
  solar_radiation_mj_m2 decimal(7,3) [note: 'Forecast incoming solar radiation in megajoules per square meter for the valid period. Direct input to the FAO Penman-Monteith ET calculation and photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) models for crop growth simulation.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Originating data provider or system for this forecast record. Identifies whether the forecast was sourced from DTN Data Transmission Network, NOAA National Weather Service, Climate FieldView, custom IoT field sensors, or WASDE World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates seasonal outlook.']
  spray_window_open boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether forecast conditions (wind speed, precipitation probability, temperature, humidity) meet the criteria for a safe and effective pesticide or herbicide application window. Derived from EPA application guidelines and IPM Integrated Pest Management protocols.']
  temp_avg_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Forecast mean air temperature in degrees Celsius for the valid period. Used as the base input for GDD growing degree day accumulation calculations and pest pressure prediction models.']
  temp_max_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Forecast maximum air temperature in degrees Celsius for the valid period. Used in growing degree day (GDD) accumulation calculations, heat stress assessments, and crop development stage modeling.']
  temp_min_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Forecast minimum air temperature in degrees Celsius for the valid period. Critical for frost and freeze alert generation, PHI pre-harvest interval compliance, and cold stress risk assessment for crops.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this forecast record was last modified or refreshed in the data lakehouse, such as when a forecast is superseded or corrected by the provider. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  wind_direction_deg decimal(5,2) [note: 'Forecast prevailing wind direction in meteorological degrees (0–360, where 0/360 = North). Used in spray drift modeling to protect adjacent fields, buffer zones, and sensitive areas per EPA and GLOBALG.A.P. requirements.']
  wind_gust_kmh decimal(6,2) [note: 'Forecast maximum wind gust speed in kilometers per hour for the valid period. Used to assess equipment safety thresholds for aerial application and tall crop operations.']
  wind_speed_kmh decimal(6,2) [note: 'Forecast average wind speed in kilometers per hour for the valid period. Critical for spray window determination — wind speeds above threshold trigger spray application restrictions per EPA and REI Restricted Entry Interval guidelines.']
  valid_from timestamp [note: 'Start of the period for which this forecast is valid. For hourly forecasts this is the start of the forecast hour; for daily forecasts it is the start of the forecast day. Used to align forecast data with field operation scheduling windows.']
  valid_to timestamp [note: 'End of the period for which this forecast is valid. Defines the forecast window boundary for planting, spraying, and irrigation scheduling decisions.']

  Note: 'Meteorological forecast record sourced from DTN, NOAA NWS, or Climate FieldView for a specific geographic location or field polygon. Captures forecast horizon (hourly, daily, 7-day, seasonal), predicted temperature range, precipitation probability and amount, wind speed/direction, humidity, ET forecast, and confidence interval. Supports planting window decisions, spray window scheduling, and WASDE-aligned seasonal outlooks.'
}

Table weather.growing_degree_day {
  growing_degree_day_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for growing_degree_day']
  climate_normal_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to weather.climate_normal. Link']

  growing_season_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the growing season during which GDD accumulation is recorded. Aligns with crop planning and seasonal crop management cycles.']
  planting_event_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to crop.planting_event. Business justification: GDD accumulation is anchored to the actual planting date from the planting event.
