Agronomic yield forecasting and harvest scheduling req']
  station_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the weather station or IoT field sensor providing the temperature data used to calculate daily GDD values.']
  accumulation_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the GDD accumulation record for this crop and field. \'active\' indicates ongoing accumulation; \'paused\' indicates temporary suspension (e.g., dormancy period); \'terminated\' indicates season ended by frost or crop failure; \'completed\' indicates crop reached maturity.']
  base_temperature_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Crop-specific minimum threshold temperature in degrees Celsius below which crop development does not occur. For corn this is typically 10°C (50°F); for wheat 0°C (32°F). Used as the lower bound in GDD calculation.']
  calculation_method varchar [note: 'The mathematical method used to calculate daily GDD values. \'standard\' uses simple average of min/max temperature minus base; \'modified\' applies upper threshold cap; \'baskerville_emin\' uses sine curve interpolation for more accurate results.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this GDD accumulation record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and Silver layer processing tracking.']
  crop_type varchar [note: 'The type of crop for which GDD accumulation is being tracked (e.g., corn, soybeans, wheat, cotton). Determines the applicable base and upper threshold temperatures. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: corn|soybeans|wheat|cotton|sorghum|sunflower|barley|canola|rice|alfalfa — promote to reference product]']
  cumulative_gdd decimal(8,2) [note: 'Running total of heat units accumulated from the planting date or season start date through the record date. Used to predict crop development stage and estimate time to maturity.']
  current_growth_stage varchar [note: 'Estimated crop development stage derived from cumulative GDD accumulation (e.g., VE, V6, VT, R1, R6 for corn; VC, V1, R1, R7, R8 for soybeans). Used for agronomic decision-making, spray window compliance, and PHI tracking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: VE|V1|V2|V3|V4|V5|V6|VT|R1|R2|R3|R4|R5|R6|R7|R8 — promote to reference product]']
  daily_gdd decimal(6,2) [note: 'Heat units accumulated on the record date, calculated as the average of adjusted min/max temperatures minus the base temperature. Negative values are set to zero. Expressed in degree-days (°C-days or °F-days per calculation method).']
  data_quality_flag varchar [note: 'Quality control indicator for the temperature observations used in GDD calculation. \'good\' indicates validated sensor data; \'estimated\' indicates gap-filled or interpolated values; \'suspect\' indicates values outside expected range pending review; \'missing\' indicates no data available; \'corrected\' indicates post-processing adjustment applied.']
  data_source varchar [note: 'Origin of the temperature data used to calculate the daily GDD value. Indicates whether data came from a physical weather station, IoT field sensor, DTN commercial weather feed, Climate FieldView platform, manual entry, or spatial interpolation.']
  forecast_gdd_30day decimal(8,2) [note: 'Projected GDD accumulation over the next 30 calendar days based on extended weather forecast data. Used for medium-term harvest planning, logistics coordination, and crop insurance monitoring.']
  forecast_gdd_7day decimal(7,2) [note: 'Projected GDD accumulation over the next 7 calendar days based on weather forecast data from DTN or Climate FieldView. Used for short-term irrigation scheduling, spray window planning, and harvest timing decisions.']
  frost_event_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a frost or freeze event occurred on the record date (minimum temperature at or below 0°C / 32°F). Critical for crop damage assessment, insurance claims, and replanting decisions.']
  gdd_deviation decimal(7,2) [note: 'Difference between the current cumulative GDD and the historical average cumulative GDD for the same date and location. Positive values indicate above-normal heat accumulation; negative values indicate below-normal accumulation. Critical for crop insurance documentation and yield forecasting.']
  gdd_percentile_rank decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentile rank of the current cumulative GDD relative to the historical distribution for the same crop, location, and calendar date. A value of 90 means the current season is warmer than 90% of historical seasons. Supports climate risk assessment and crop insurance documentation.']
  gdd_to_emergence decimal(7,2) [note: 'Crop-specific cumulative GDD milestone required to reach the emergence (VE) growth stage. Used to predict emergence date and validate actual emergence observations against heat unit accumulation.']
  gdd_to_maturity decimal(7,2) [note: 'Crop-specific cumulative GDD milestone required to reach physiological maturity (black layer for corn, R8 for soybeans). Used for harvest timing decisions, crop insurance documentation, and logistics planning.']
  gdd_to_silking decimal(7,2) [note: 'Crop-specific cumulative GDD milestone required to reach the silking (R1) or equivalent flowering growth stage. Critical for pollination timing, spray window management, and PHI compliance planning.']
  historical_avg_gdd decimal(8,2) [note: 'Long-term historical average cumulative GDD for the same crop, field location, and calendar date, typically based on a 30-year climate normal. Used as the baseline for deviation analysis and climate risk assessment.']
  killing_frost_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a killing frost event occurred on the record date (minimum temperature at or below -2.2°C / 28°F for a sustained period). A killing frost terminates the growing season and stops GDD accumulation. Triggers crop insurance documentation requirements.']
  phi_compliance_stage_reached boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the crop has reached the growth stage at which Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) restrictions for applied agrochemicals become active, as determined by cumulative GDD. Critical for food safety compliance and EPA/FDA regulatory adherence.']
  predicted_maturity_date date [note: 'Estimated calendar date when the crop will reach physiological maturity based on current cumulative GDD and historical or forecast temperature trends. Supports harvest scheduling and supply chain planning.']
  record_date date [note: 'Calendar date for which the daily Growing Degree Day (GDD) value is calculated. Represents the specific day of temperature observation.']
  season_start_date date [note: 'The date from which cumulative GDD accumulation begins for this crop and field. Typically the planting date or a standardized calendar date (e.g., January 1 for winter crops). Defines the accumulation window.']
  spray_window_open boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the current crop growth stage (as determined by cumulative GDD) is within an approved spray application window for pesticides or fungicides. Derived from GDD-based growth stage and PHI/REI compliance rules.']
  temperature_avg_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Mean daily air temperature in degrees Celsius, calculated as the average of the minimum and maximum temperatures for the record date. Intermediate value used in standard GDD calculation.']
  temperature_max_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Observed maximum air temperature in degrees Celsius recorded at the weather station or field sensor for the record date. Used as the upper bound in daily GDD calculation.']
  temperature_min_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Observed minimum air temperature in degrees Celsius recorded at the weather station or field sensor for the record date. Used as the lower bound in daily GDD calculation.']
  temperature_unit varchar [note: 'Unit of measure used for all temperature values and GDD calculations in this record. \'celsius\' for metric (°C-days); \'fahrenheit\' for imperial (°F-days). Ensures consistent interpretation across systems and regions.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this GDD accumulation record was last modified, such as when temperature data was corrected, quality flags were updated, or forecast values were refreshed.']
  upper_threshold_temperature_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Crop-specific maximum temperature ceiling in degrees Celsius above which additional heat does not accelerate crop development. For corn this is typically 30°C (86°F). Temperatures above this are capped at this value in modified GDD calculations.']

  Note: 'Growing Degree Day (GDD) accumulation record tracking heat unit accumulation for a specific crop, field, and growing season. Stores daily GDD calculated from min/max temperature against crop-specific base and upper threshold temperatures, cumulative GDD to date, target GDD milestones (emergence, silking, maturity), and deviation from historical norms. Critical for crop development stage prediction, PHI compliance, and harvest timing decisions.'
}

Table weather.evapotranspiration {
  evapotranspiration_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for evapotranspiration']
  field_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the agricultural field or irrigation zone for which this ET calculation was performed. Links to the field master record in the land and soil domain.']
  growing_season_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the growing season during which this ET calculation applies, enabling seasonal water balance tracking and crop coefficient (Kc) stage alignment.']
  station_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the weather station or IoT field sensor that provided the meteorological inputs used in this ET calculation. May be a physical station or a virtual grid-point from DTN weather feeds.']
  calculation_date date [note: 'The calendar date for which this evapotranspiration calculation was computed. Represents the real-world observation or forecast date, not the record creation date. Used for daily water balance tracking and irrigation scheduling.']
  calculation_method varchar [note: 'The scientific method used to compute reference evapotranspiration (ETo). Penman-Monteith (FAO-56) is the USDA and FAO standard; Hargreaves is used when solar radiation data is unavailable. Drives traceability and comparability of ET values.']
  calculation_status varchar [note: 'Lifecycle status of this ET calculation record. \'computed\' indicates automated calculation; \'validated\' indicates agronomist review; \'superseded\' indicates a newer recalculation replaced this record; \'error\' indicates a failed computation requiring review.']
  calculation_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Precise timestamp when this ET calculation record was computed or ingested into the system. Supports audit trail and distinguishes multiple intraday recalculations for the same date.']
  crop_coefficient decimal(5,3) [note: 'Dimensionless crop coefficient (Kc) applied to reference ET to derive crop-specific ET. Value varies by crop growth stage (initial, mid-season, late-season) per FAO-56 tables. Sourced from crop plan or agronomist input.']
  crop_et_mm decimal(8,3) [note: 'Crop evapotranspiration (ETc) in millimetres, calculated as ETo × Kc. Represents the actual water demand of the specific crop at its current growth stage. Primary input to irrigation scheduling and water balance calculations.']
  crop_growth_stage varchar [note: 'The phenological growth stage of the crop at the time of this ET calculation, used to select the appropriate crop coefficient (Kc) from FAO-56 tables. Stage progression drives changes in water demand throughout the season.']
  cumulative_et_season_mm decimal(10,3) [note: 'Running cumulative crop ET (ETc) in millimetres from the start of the growing season to the calculation date. Used for seasonal water budget tracking, crop insurance documentation, and water use compliance reporting.']
  cumulative_irrigation_season_mm decimal(10,3) [note: 'Running cumulative irrigation water applied in millimetres from the start of the growing season to the calculation date. Compared against cumulative ET to assess irrigation efficiency and water use compliance.']
  data_quality_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Numeric quality score (0–100) reflecting the completeness and reliability of the weather input data used in this ET calculation. Lower scores indicate missing inputs (e.g., estimated solar radiation, gap-filled humidity) that reduce confidence in the ET result.']
  data_source_type varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the weather inputs used in this ET calculation were derived from observed station data, weather forecast models, spatially interpolated grid data, or satellite-derived estimates. Affects confidence in irrigation recommendations.']
  effective_precipitation_mm decimal(8,3) [note: 'The portion of total precipitation credited toward meeting crop ET demand after accounting for runoff, deep percolation, and interception losses. Calculated per USDA SCS method. Reduces the net irrigation requirement.']
  et_deficit_mm decimal(8,3) [note: 'Daily ET deficit in millimetres, calculated as ETc minus effective precipitation. Represents the net water demand that must be met by irrigation for the calculation date. Negative values indicate precipitation surplus.']
  frost_risk_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether minimum temperature conditions on the calculation date meet or fall below the frost threshold for the crop type. Triggers frost/freeze alerts in irrigation scheduling systems and supports crop insurance documentation.']
  irrigation_method varchar [note: 'The irrigation delivery method applicable to this field and ET recommendation. Determines application efficiency factors and scheduling logic. Drip and subsurface drip have higher application efficiency than flood or sprinkler systems.']
  max_temperature_c decimal(6,2) [note: 'Maximum daily air temperature in degrees Celsius used as a weather input to the ET calculation. Required by both Penman-Monteith and Hargreaves methods. Sourced from weather station or DTN feed.']
  mean_temperature_c decimal(6,2) [note: 'Mean daily air temperature in degrees Celsius, calculated as the average of maximum and minimum temperatures. Used in Hargreaves ET method and growing degree day (GDD) accumulation calculations.']
  min_temperature_c decimal(6,2) [note: 'Minimum daily air temperature in degrees Celsius used as a weather input to the ET calculation. Required by both Penman-Monteith and Hargreaves methods. Also used for frost risk assessment.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text agronomist or system notes associated with this ET calculation record, capturing manual overrides, data quality observations, or irrigation scheduling decisions that deviate from the automated recommendation.']
  precipitation_mm decimal(8,3) [note: 'Total precipitation (rainfall) recorded or forecast for the calculation date in millimetres. Used as a credit against crop ET demand in the daily water balance calculation.']
  recommended_irrigation_acre_in decimal(8,3) [note: 'Weather-driven irrigation recommendation expressed in acre-inches per acre, derived from the ET deficit and soil water deficit. Primary output consumed by John Deere Operations Center and Trimble Ag VRA for irrigation scheduling and variable rate application prescriptions.']
  recommended_irrigation_mm decimal(8,3) [note: 'Weather-driven irrigation recommendation expressed in millimetres, the SI unit equivalent of the acre-inch recommendation. Used for international reporting, water resource compliance, and integration with metric-based irrigation controllers.']
  reference_et_mm decimal(8,3) [note: 'Reference evapotranspiration (ETo) in millimetres for the calculation date, representing the ET demand of a standardised reference crop (short grass or alfalfa). The foundational output of the Penman-Monteith or Hargreaves equation. Used as the basis for crop-specific ET adjustment.']
  relative_humidity_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Mean daily relative humidity as a percentage, used in the Penman-Monteith ET calculation to determine vapour pressure deficit. High humidity reduces ET demand; low humidity increases it.']
  scheduled_irrigation_date date [note: 'The recommended calendar date on which irrigation should be applied based on the ET-driven water balance calculation. Populated when weather-driven scheduling is active. Null when no irrigation is currently recommended.']
  scheduled_irrigation_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Precise scheduled start date and time for the recommended irrigation event, used when automated irrigation controllers require time-of-day scheduling. Null when only date-level scheduling is active.']
  soil_moisture_target_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Target soil moisture level as a percentage of field capacity for this field and crop stage. Used as the trigger threshold for irrigation scheduling. Typically set between 50–70% of available water capacity depending on crop stress tolerance.']
  soil_water_deficit_mm decimal(8,3) [note: 'Cumulative soil water deficit in millimetres representing the difference between field capacity and current soil moisture content. Positive values indicate irrigation need. Updated daily using the FAO-56 water balance model.']
  solar_radiation_mj_m2 decimal(8,3) [note: 'Daily incoming solar radiation in megajoules per square metre (MJ/m²), a primary driver of ET demand in the Penman-Monteith equation. Sourced from weather station pyranometer or estimated from sunshine hours and cloud cover.']
  spray_window_suitable boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether weather conditions on the calculation date are suitable for pesticide or fertilizer spray application, based on wind speed, temperature, humidity, and precipitation thresholds. Supports Integrated Pest Management (IPM) and EPA/REI compliance.']
  vapour_pressure_deficit_kpa decimal(6,3) [note: 'Vapour pressure deficit (VPD) in kilopascals, representing the difference between saturated and actual vapour pressure. A key intermediate variable in the Penman-Monteith ET calculation and an indicator of atmospheric drying demand on crops.']
  water_stress_index decimal(5,3) [note: 'Dimensionless water stress coefficient (Ks) ranging from 0 to 1, representing the degree of crop water stress due to soil moisture deficit. A value of 1 indicates no stress; values below 1 indicate stress-adjusted ET. Used in FAO-56 dual crop coefficient approach.']
  wind_speed_ms decimal(6,2) [note: 'Mean daily wind speed at 2-metre height in metres per second, a required input to the Penman-Monteith ET equation. Higher wind speeds increase ET demand by enhancing vapour transport from the crop canopy.']

  Note: 'Evapotranspiration (ET) calculation and weather-driven water balance record for a field or irrigation zone. Computed using the Penman-Monteith or Hargreaves method from observed or forecast weather inputs. Stores reference ET (ETo), crop ET (ETc) adjusted by crop coefficient (Kc), soil water deficit, ET deficit, soil moisture target, precipitation credit applied, recommended irrigation volume (acre-inches), irrigation method suitability (drip, pivot, flood), and scheduled irrigation date/time when weather-driven scheduling is active. SSOT for weather-derived water balance calculations and ET-based irrigation recommendations that feed irrigation scheduling systems (John Deere Operations Center, Trimble Ag VRA) and water resource management compliance reporting.'
}

Determines appropriate protective measures.']
  gdd_impact_estimate decimal(7,2) [note: 'Estimated reduction in Growing Degree Day (GDD) accumulation attributable to the frost event. GDD accumulation drives crop phenology and maturity timing; frost-induced GDD loss affects harvest scheduling and yield forecasting in Climate FieldView.']

  irrigation_frost_protection boolean [note: 'Indicates whether overhead irrigation frost protection has been recommended or activated for this alert. Irrigation frost protection uses latent heat of freezing water to protect crops; relevant to irrigation scheduling systems.']
  issued_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the frost alert was officially issued by the source system or meteorological authority. This is the principal real-world event time for the alert, distinct from the record creation audit timestamp.']
  latitude decimal(9,6) [note: 'Geographic latitude coordinate (decimal degrees, WGS84) of the alert centroid or affected field center. Supports GIS-based spatial analysis and precision agriculture mapping in Esri ArcGIS.']
  longitude decimal(9,6) [note: 'Geographic longitude coordinate (decimal degrees, WGS84) of the alert centroid or affected field center. Supports GIS-based spatial analysis and precision agriculture mapping in Esri ArcGIS.']
  nws_event_code varchar [note: 'External reference identifier assigned by the National Weather Service (NWS) to the corresponding official frost or freeze advisory, watch, or warning. Enables cross-referencing with NWS public alert records for regulatory and insurance documentation.']
  observed_low_temp_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Actual recorded minimum air temperature in degrees Celsius as measured by the weather station or IoT sensor during the frost event. Populated post-event; used for insurance loss documentation and model validation.']
  recommended_action varchar [note: 'Primary recommended protective action for the affected field or zone based on alert severity and crop vulnerability. Examples include frost cloth application, overhead irrigation frost protection, wind machine activation, smudge pot deployment, or harvest acceleration. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: frost_cloth|overhead_irrigation|wind_machine|smudge_pot|harvest_acceleration|no_action|monitor — promote to reference product]']
  relative_humidity_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Forecast or observed relative humidity percentage at the time of the frost event. Low humidity combined with low temperatures increases frost severity; used in dew point and frost point calculations.']
  sky_condition varchar [note: 'Forecast or observed sky cover condition at the time of the frost event. Clear skies promote radiative cooling and increase frost severity; overcast conditions reduce frost risk by trapping longwave radiation.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Audit timestamp recording when the frost alert record was last modified, such as when status changes, forecast updates are received, or protective action outcomes are recorded.']
  wind_speed_ms decimal(6,2) [note: 'Forecast or observed wind speed in meters per second at the time of the frost event. Low wind speeds (calm conditions) increase radiation frost risk; used in frost type classification (radiation vs. advection frost).']

  Note: 'Frost and freeze event alert record generated when forecast or observed temperatures fall below crop-specific critical thresholds. Captures alert type (advisory/watch/warning), predicted low temperature, frost probability, affected field or geographic zone, crop vulnerability rating, recommended protective actions (frost cloth, irrigation frost protection), and alert source (DTN, NWS). Supports crop protection decision-making and insurance loss documentation.'
}

  data_source varchar [note: 'Identifies the originating data source system for this precipitation event record. Used for data lineage tracking, quality weighting, and source reconciliation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: iot_sensor|dtn_feed|climate_fieldview|manual_entry|noaa_api|nws_api — promote to reference product]']
  event_end_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the precipitation or severe weather event concluded at the recorded location. Used to calculate event duration and determine trafficability and re-entry windows. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  event_reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric identifier for this precipitation event, used for cross-referencing with USDA disaster reports, insurance claim documentation, and DTN weather feed records. Format: EVT-YYYYMMDD-NNNN.']
  event_start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the precipitation or severe weather event began at the recorded location. Principal real-world event time used for spray window invalidation, irrigation scheduling, and insurance claim trigger documentation. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  event_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the precipitation event record. \'active\' indicates the event is ongoing; \'completed\' indicates the event has ended and data is finalized; \'cancelled\' indicates a false alarm or data retraction; \'under_review\' indicates the record is pending quality validation.']
  external_event_ref varchar [note: 'External system identifier for this event as assigned by the source system (e.g., DTN event ID, NWS storm report number, Climate FieldView event key). Used for cross-system reconciliation and audit traceability.']
  hail_density_stones_sqft decimal(8,2) [note: 'Estimated number of hail stones per square foot observed during the event. Combined with hail stone size to determine crop damage severity and insurance claim trigger eligibility. Null when precip_type is not hail or mixed.']
  hail_stone_size_in decimal(5,2) [note: 'Maximum observed hail stone diameter in inches during the event. Used to assess structural damage risk to crops, equipment, and infrastructure. Null when precip_type is not hail or mixed.']
  insurance_claim_trigger boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this precipitation event meets the threshold criteria to trigger a crop insurance claim under the applicable USDA RMA policy. True initiates the insurance claim documentation workflow and notifies the risk management team.']
  irrigation_adjustment_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this precipitation event requires adjustment to the active irrigation schedule. True triggers review of ET (Evapotranspiration) balance and irrigation prescription update in the FMIS (Farm Management Information System).']
  latitude decimal(9,6) [note: 'Geographic latitude coordinate (WGS84 decimal degrees) of the primary observation point for this precipitation event. Used for spatial analysis, GIS mapping, and cross-referencing with field boundaries in Esri ArcGIS.']
  longitude decimal(9,6) [note: 'Geographic longitude coordinate (WGS84 decimal degrees) of the primary observation point for this precipitation event. Used for spatial analysis, GIS mapping, and cross-referencing with field boundaries in Esri ArcGIS.']
  precip_intensity_peak_mm_hr decimal(6,2) [note: 'Maximum instantaneous precipitation rate in millimeters per hour recorded during the event. High peak intensity values indicate elevated runoff risk, soil erosion potential, and spray drift invalidation conditions.']
  precip_total_mm decimal(8,2) [note: 'Total accumulated precipitation depth in millimeters recorded during the event. Primary quantitative outcome used for irrigation scheduling adjustments, runoff estimation, soil saturation assessment, and USDA disaster reporting thresholds.']
  precip_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the form of precipitation observed during the event. Determines downstream impact on crop damage assessment, trafficability, and equipment operation windows.']
  runoff_estimate_mm decimal(8,2) [note: 'Estimated surface water runoff depth in millimeters generated by this precipitation event, calculated using USDA NRCS curve number methodology.   soil_saturation_index decimal(5,2) [note: 'Dimensionless index (0.00–1.00) representing estimated soil water saturation level following this precipitation event.   spray_drift_risk_level varchar [note: 'Categorical assessment of spray drift risk based on wind speed, wind direction, and precipitation conditions during the event.   spray_window_invalidated boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this precipitation event has invalidated one or more planned spray application windows. True triggers re-scheduling of pesticide or fertilizer applications and PHI (Pre-Harvest Interval) recalculation.']
  storm_track_path varchar [note: 'GIS-encoded storm track path as a WKT (Well-Known Text) LineString representing the movement trajectory of the storm system across the geographic area. Used for spatial analysis of multi-field impact assessment in Esri ArcGIS.']
  storm_type varchar [note: 'Meteorological classification of the storm system producing the precipitation event. Convective storms are associated with thunderstorms and rapid intensity; frontal storms are associated with weather front passages; orographic storms result from terrain-forced uplift. Used for pest pressure prediction and crop insurance documentation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: convective|frontal|orographic|tropical|extratropical|monsoonal — promote to reference product]']
  structural_damage_risk boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the combination of wind gust speed, hail size, and precipitation intensity during this event poses a risk of structural damage to farm buildings, grain storage, irrigation infrastructure, or equipment. True triggers facility inspection workflow.']
  trafficability_restricted boolean [note: 'Indicates whether field trafficability is restricted following this precipitation event due to soil saturation or standing water conditions. True prevents heavy equipment entry and triggers field access hold in the John Deere Operations Center fleet management workflow.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this precipitation event record was last modified. Used for change tracking, data quality monitoring, and incremental data pipeline processing. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  usda_disaster_reportable boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this precipitation event qualifies for USDA disaster program reporting under FSA emergency programs. True triggers submission to the USDA Farm Service Agency disaster reporting workflow.']
  wind_direction_deg decimal(5,1) [note: 'Prevailing wind direction in degrees from true north (0–360) during the event. Used for spray drift risk assessment, storm track path analysis, and field-level impact modeling.']
  wind_gust_peak_mph decimal(6,2) [note: 'Maximum instantaneous wind gust speed in miles per hour recorded during the event. Used to assess crop lodging risk, spray drift risk, structural damage risk, and Beaufort scale classification.']
  wind_speed_sustained_mph decimal(6,2) [note: 'Average sustained wind speed in miles per hour over the event duration. Used alongside peak gust for Beaufort classification, spray window assessment, and crop lodging risk evaluation.']

  Note: 'Discrete severe weather event record capturing precipitation, hail, and high-wind episodes at field or station level. Stores event start/end timestamps, total precipitation amount, peak intensity, storm type (convective, frontal, orographic), hail stone size (inches) and density (stones/sq ft), peak wind gust speed (mph), sustained wind speed, wind direction, Beaufort scale classification, crop lodging risk flag, spray drift risk level, structural damage risk indicator, runoff estimate, soil saturation index, estimated crop damage severity (none/light/moderate/severe), affected acreage, storm track path, and insurance claim trigger flag. SSOT for all field-level severe weather event documentation including precipitation, hail, and wind damage. Used for irrigation adjustments, trafficability assessment, spray window invalidation, crop insurance documentation, USDA disaster reporting, and FSIS compliance.'
}

  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this spray window record was last modified. Tracks recalculations triggered by updated forecast data or manual overrides. Supports audit trail and data quality monitoring.']
  wind_direction_deg decimal(5,2) [note: 'Prevailing wind direction in degrees (0–360, meteorological convention) during the spray window. Used to assess drift trajectory relative to sensitive areas, water bodies, and neighbouring fields.']
  wind_speed_max_kmh decimal(5,2) [note: 'Maximum observed or forecast wind speed in kilometres per hour during the spray window period. Exceeding label-specified maximum wind speed thresholds triggers window closure to prevent off-target drift.']
  wind_speed_min_kmh decimal(5,2) [note: 'Minimum observed or forecast wind speed in kilometres per hour during the spray window period. Used to assess drift risk and label compliance; most pesticide labels require a minimum wind speed to ensure adequate air movement.']
  window_duration_min varchar [note: 'Calculated duration of the spray window in minutes, derived from window_start and window_end. Stored for operational scheduling and equipment dispatch planning without requiring runtime calculation.']
  window_end timestamp [note: 'The datetime marking the close of the meteorologically permissible application window. Spray operations must cease by this time to remain within label-compliant and regulatory-compliant conditions.']

[ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pesticide|herbicide|fungicide|insecticide|fertilizer|growth_regulator|adjuvant|micronutrient — promote to reference product]']

  enso_phase varchar [note: 'Current El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) phase influencing the climate risk assessment. ENSO phase is a primary driver of seasonal precipitation and temperature anomalies affecting agricultural production.']
  estimated_yield_impact_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Estimated percentage reduction in crop yield attributable to the assessed climate risk event, based on historical loss data and agronomic models. Supports crop insurance underwriting and enterprise risk management.']
  et_deficit_mm decimal(8,2) [note: 'Estimated Evapotranspiration (ET) deficit in millimeters for the assessment zone and period, representing the gap between crop water demand and available supply. Supports irrigation scheduling and drought risk assessment.']
  frost_risk_days varchar [note: 'Number of days within the assessment window with a forecast or historical probability of frost occurrence. Applicable when risk_type is late_frost; supports planting window decisions and crop insurance documentation.']
  gdd_deviation decimal(7,2) [note: 'Deviation of accumulated Growing Degree Days (GDD) from the historical average for the assessment period. Supports planting window decisions, crop maturity forecasting, and pest pressure prediction.']
  hail_risk_index decimal(5,2) [note: 'Composite index score quantifying hail risk for the assessment zone and period, derived from historical hail frequency and storm climatology data. Applicable when risk_type is hail; supports crop insurance underwriting.']
  historical_frequency_years decimal(5,2) [note: 'Average recurrence interval in years for this risk type at this geographic zone, derived from historical climate records. Supports long-term capital planning and crop insurance actuarial analysis.']
  indicator_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known business identifier code for this climate risk indicator record, used for cross-system reference in FMIS, Granular Farm Management, and crop insurance underwriting workflows.']
  insurance_relevant boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this climate risk indicator is relevant for crop insurance claim documentation or underwriting purposes under USDA Risk Management Agency programs.']
  latitude decimal(9,6) [note: 'Geographic latitude in decimal degrees of the centroid of the assessed geographic zone or farm unit. Supports GIS spatial analysis in Esri ArcGIS and precision agriculture workflows.']
  longitude decimal(9,6) [note: 'Geographic longitude in decimal degrees of the centroid of the assessed geographic zone or farm unit. Supports GIS spatial analysis in Esri ArcGIS and precision agriculture workflows.']
  model_version varchar [note: 'Version identifier of the climate risk assessment model or algorithm used to generate this indicator record. Supports reproducibility, model governance, and AI/ML lineage tracking.']
  occurrence_probability_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Estimated probability (0.00–100.00%) that the assessed climate risk event will occur within the valid assessment window. Used in crop insurance underwriting and actuarial modeling.']
  precip_anomaly_pct decimal(6,2) [note: 'Percentage deviation of observed or forecast precipitation from the long-term historical average for the assessment period and zone. Positive values indicate excess; negative values indicate deficit. Supports flood and drought risk quantification.']
  recommended_action varchar [note: 'Free-text description of the recommended agronomic or capital investment action to mitigate or adapt to the assessed climate risk. Supports Best Management Practices (BMP) documentation and SOP compliance.']
  risk_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional context, qualifications, or observations related to this climate risk indicator record. Supports analyst commentary and audit documentation.']
  risk_severity_index decimal(5,2) [note: 'Quantitative index score representing the severity of the assessed climate risk, typically on a normalized scale (e.g., 0.00–100.00). Drives prioritization in enterprise risk management and capital planning for climate adaptation.']
  risk_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of this climate risk indicator record, indicating whether the risk is actively being monitored, elevated to alert level, resolved, or archived for historical reference.']
  risk_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the primary climate risk event type being assessed. Drives crop insurance underwriting, enterprise risk management, and capital planning for climate adaptation investments.']
  temp_anomaly_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Deviation of observed or forecast temperature in degrees Celsius from the long-term historical average for the assessment period and zone. Supports heat stress and late frost risk quantification.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this climate risk indicator record was last modified in the Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer. Supports change tracking, data quality monitoring, and audit trail requirements.']
  wasde_outlook_alignment varchar [note: 'Alignment of this climate risk assessment with the USDA World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates (WASDE) seasonal outlook for precipitation or temperature. Supports enterprise risk management and long-range planning.']
  wind_risk_index decimal(5,2) [note: 'Composite index score quantifying excessive wind risk for the assessment zone and period. Applicable when risk_type is excessive_wind; supports crop insurance underwriting and spray window planning.']
  valid_from date [note: 'Start date of the period for which this climate risk indicator is considered valid and applicable. Defines the seasonal or long-range assessment window.']
  valid_to date [note: 'End date of the period for which this climate risk indicator is considered valid. Nullable for open-ended long-range assessments. Supports crop insurance policy period alignment.']

  Note: 'Seasonal and long-range climate risk assessment record for a geographic zone or farm unit. Captures risk type (drought, flood, heat stress, late frost, hail, excessive wind), risk severity index, probability of occurrence, affected crop types, historical frequency, ENSO phase influence, and WASDE seasonal outlook alignment. Supports crop insurance underwriting, enterprise risk management, and long-term capital planning for climate adaptation investments.'
}

Table weather.drought_index {
  drought_index_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each drought index monitoring record in the silver layer lakehouse.']
  climate_normal_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to weather.climate_normal. Business justification: Drought indices (SPI, PDSI, CMI) are calculated by comparing actual precipitation and temperature against long-term climate normals. drought_index has precip_normal_mm — this is a denormalized value f']
  field_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the agricultural field or management zone for which this drought index record applies. Supports field-level irrigation scheduling and crop insurance documentation.']
  station_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the weather station or IoT field sensor that provided the meteorological observations underpinning this drought index calculation.']
  zone_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to weather.weather_zone. Business justification: Drought monitoring indices are tracked at the geographic zone level (USDA drought monitor uses zone-based reporting). drought_index has geographic_zone_code (STRING) which is a denormalized reference ']
  affected_area_ha decimal(12,2) [note: 'Total land area in hectares affected by the drought condition represented in this record. Used for crop insurance claim quantification, USDA disaster designation documentation, and irrigation resource planning.']
  cmi_value decimal(8,4) [note: 'Crop Moisture Index value measuring short-term moisture conditions critical to crop development. Negative values indicate moisture stress affecting crop growth. Published weekly by USDA and used to assess in-season crop moisture adequacy for irrigation scheduling.']
  consecutive_dry_days varchar [note: 'Number of consecutive days with precipitation below the dry-day threshold (typically < 1 mm/day). A key indicator of agricultural drought onset and persistence. Used to trigger irrigation scheduling recommendations and crop insurance claim documentation.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this drought index record was first created in the silver layer lakehouse. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and compliance documentation requirements.']
  data_source varchar [note: 'Originating data source system or feed for this drought index record. DTN = DTN Weather Data Network; NOAA = National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration; USDA_NASS = USDA National Agricultural Statistics Service; CLIMATE_FIELDVIEW = Climate FieldView platform; IOT_SENSOR = IoT field sensor network; USDM = US Drought Monitor; MANUAL = manually entered record. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: DTN|NOAA|USDA_NASS|CLIMATE_FIELDVIEW|IOT_SENSOR|USDM|MANUAL — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  drought_category varchar [note: 'US Drought Monitor (USDM) drought category classification: None = No drought; D0 = Abnormally Dry; D1 = Moderate Drought; D2 = Severe Drought; D3 = Extreme Drought; D4 = Exceptional Drought. Used for USDA disaster designation documentation and federal crop insurance eligibility.']
  drought_status varchar [note: 'Current operational status of the drought condition for this record. Indicates whether drought conditions are active, trending toward improvement or deterioration, or have been resolved. Drives alert notifications and irrigation scheduling decisions.']
  estimated_yield_loss_pct decimal(6,2) [note: 'Estimated percentage reduction in crop yield attributable to drought stress conditions represented by this index record. Used for crop insurance claim documentation, USDA disaster designation support, and financial loss estimation in Granular Farm Management.']
  et_actual_mm decimal(10,2) [note: 'Actual evapotranspiration in millimeters for the index period, representing the combined water loss from soil evaporation and plant transpiration. Used in soil moisture deficit calculations and drought severity assessments. Sourced from IoT field sensors or DTN weather feeds.']
  index_date date [note: 'Calendar date for which this drought index record is valid. Represents the observation or reporting date used for drought severity assessment and USDA disaster designation documentation.']
  index_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the drought index methodology used for this record. PDSI = Palmer Drought Severity Index; SPI = Standardized Precipitation Index; CMI = Crop Moisture Index; NDVI_STRESS = Normalized Difference Vegetation Index-derived vegetation stress; SPEI = Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index; EDDI = Evaporative Demand Drought Index.']
  index_value decimal(10,4) [note: 'Computed numeric value of the drought index for the specified index_type. For PDSI, ranges approximately -10 (extreme drought) to +10 (extreme wet). For SPI, standardized z-score. For CMI, inches of moisture deficit or surplus. Feeds irrigation scheduling algorithms and crop insurance claim triggers.']
  insurance_claim_relevant boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this drought index record meets the threshold criteria to support a crop insurance claim under USDA Risk Management Agency (RMA) policies. True = record qualifies as supporting evidence for an insurance claim filing.']
  irrigation_deficit_mm decimal(10,2) [note: 'Recommended irrigation application amount in millimeters to address the current soil moisture deficit. Computed from the soil moisture deficit adjusted for irrigation efficiency. Used to generate variable rate application (VRA) prescriptions.']
  irrigation_recommended boolean [note: 'Indicates whether irrigation is recommended based on the current drought index values and soil moisture deficit. True = irrigation action recommended. Drives automated irrigation scheduling workflows in Trimble Ag Software and John Deere Operations Center.']
  latitude decimal(9,6) [note: 'Geographic latitude in decimal degrees (WGS84) of the centroid or representative point for this drought index record. Supports spatial analysis in Esri ArcGIS and integration with USDM drought polygon overlays.']
  longitude decimal(9,6) [note: 'Geographic longitude in decimal degrees (WGS84) of the centroid or representative point for this drought index record. Supports spatial analysis in Esri ArcGIS and integration with USDM drought polygon overlays.']
  ndvi_stress_index decimal(8,4) [note: 'NDVI-derived vegetation stress indicator computed from satellite or drone imagery. Values range from -1 to +1; lower values indicate greater vegetation stress due to moisture deficit. Integrates with Climate FieldView and Esri ArcGIS for spatial drought impact mapping.']
  pdsi_value decimal(8,4) [note: 'Palmer Drought Severity Index value for this record period. Ranges from approximately -10 (extreme drought) to +10 (extreme wet conditions). Negative values indicate moisture deficit. Used for USDA disaster designation and crop insurance documentation.']
  precip_actual_mm decimal(10,2) [note: 'Observed precipitation in millimeters accumulated over the index period. Used as the primary input for SPI and CMI calculations and for comparison against normal precipitation to quantify drought severity.']
  precip_departure_pct decimal(8,2) [note: 'Percentage departure of actual precipitation from the climatological normal for the index period. Negative values indicate below-normal precipitation contributing to drought conditions. Key metric for USDA disaster designation documentation.']
  quality_flag varchar [note: 'Quality control flag indicating the reliability and completeness of the drought index data in this record. Good = passed all QC checks; Suspect = potential data quality issue requiring review; Missing = one or more input values absent; Estimated = value gap-filled or interpolated; Corrected = value was adjusted post-QC.']
  soil_moisture_deficit_mm decimal(10,2) [note: 'Estimated soil moisture deficit in millimeters representing the amount of water needed to bring soil to field capacity. Derived from water balance calculations incorporating precipitation, evapotranspiration (ET), and runoff. Directly drives variable rate irrigation prescriptions.']
  source_record_code varchar [note: 'External identifier or reference number from the originating source system (e.g., USDM polygon ID, DTN record ID, Climate FieldView observation ID). Supports data lineage traceability and reconciliation with upstream systems.']
  spi_time_scale_months varchar [note: 'Accumulation period in months over which the SPI value was calculated (e.g., 1, 3, 6, 12, 24 months). Short time scales reflect agricultural drought; longer scales reflect hydrological drought. Required for correct interpretation of the SPI value.']
  spi_value decimal(8,4) [note: 'Standardized Precipitation Index value representing precipitation deficit or surplus as a standardized z-score relative to the historical distribution. Negative values indicate below-normal precipitation. Computed for the SPI time scale specified in spi_time_scale_months.']
  spray_window_open boolean [note: 'Indicates whether current drought and weather conditions support an open spray application window for pesticide or fertilizer application. Drought conditions may affect spray efficacy and drift risk. Integrates with IPM protocols and EPA REI compliance.']
  temp_avg_c decimal(6,2) [note: 'Mean air temperature in degrees Celsius for the index period. Elevated temperatures accelerate evapotranspiration and exacerbate drought conditions. Used in PDSI and SPEI calculations and for heat stress assessment in conjunction with drought monitoring.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this drought index record was last modified in the silver layer lakehouse. Used for incremental data processing, change detection, and audit trail maintenance.']
  usda_disaster_designation boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the geographic area covered by this drought index record has received or is being considered for a USDA Secretarial Disaster Designation. True = disaster designation active or pending. Enables eligibility tracking for USDA emergency loan programs and FSA assistance.']

  Note: 'Drought monitoring index record tracking soil moisture deficit and drought severity for a field or geographic region. Stores Palmer Drought Severity Index (PDSI), Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI), Crop Moisture Index (CMI), NDVI-derived vegetation stress indicator, drought category (D0–D4 per USDM), and consecutive dry days count. Feeds irrigation scheduling, crop insurance claims, and USDA disaster designation documentation.'
}

Table weather.soil_temperature {
  soil_temperature_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for soil_temperature']

  station_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the weather station or IoT field sensor node that captured this soil temperature reading. Links to the station master record.']
  zone_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to weather.weather_zone. Business justification: Soil temperature readings are associated with geographic zones for regional agronomic analysis. soil_temperature has geographic_zone_code (STRING) which is a denormalized reference to weather_zone.zon']
  ambient_air_temp_c decimal(6,2) [note: 'Concurrent ambient air temperature in degrees Celsius recorded at the same station at the time of the soil temperature reading. Provides context for soil-air temperature differential analysis and frost risk assessment.']

Affects data trust level for agronomic decisions.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this soil temperature reading record was first ingested into the silver layer lakehouse. Audit trail field for data governance and lineage tracking. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  crop_type varchar [note: 'The crop species or type associated with this soil temperature reading context (e.g., corn, soybeans, wheat, cotton). Used to apply crop-specific germination thresholds, GDD base temperatures, and planting window criteria. Null if the field has no active crop assignment.']
  data_source varchar [note: 'Originating system or method that produced this soil temperature reading. Supports data lineage, source reconciliation, and trust-level differentiation between automated sensor feeds and manual entries. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: IoT_field_sensor|weather_station_probe|DTN_feed|manual_entry|Climate_FieldView|Trimble_Ag|FMIS|other — promote to reference product]']
  depth_cm decimal(6,2) [note: 'Depth below soil surface at which the temperature measurement was taken, expressed in centimetres. Standard agricultural depths include 5 cm (2-inch), 10 cm (4-inch), 15 cm (6-inch), and 30 cm (12-inch). Critical for seed germination prediction and soil biological activity assessment.']
  depth_inches decimal(6,2) [note: 'Depth below soil surface at which the temperature measurement was taken, expressed in inches (US customary). Common agricultural reference depths: 2-inch, 4-inch, 6-inch, 12-inch. Stored alongside cm value to support both US and metric reporting.']

  elevation_m decimal(8,2) [note: 'Elevation above mean sea level of the sensor location in metres. Influences soil temperature patterns and microclimate conditions. Used for topographic correction in spatial interpolation models.']
  frost_risk_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this soil temperature reading falls at or below the frost threshold (typically 0°C / 32°F at the relevant depth), triggering frost risk conditions. Used for frost alert generation, crop protection decisions, and crop insurance documentation.']

  gdd_contribution decimal(6,2) [note: 'Growing Degree Day (GDD) contribution calculated from this soil temperature reading relative to the configured base temperature. Supports cumulative GDD accumulation tracking for crop development stage prediction and planting window determination.']
  insurance_relevant boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this soil temperature reading is relevant for crop insurance documentation purposes (e.g., frost damage claims, planting date verification). When True, the record is retained in the insurance evidence dataset.']
  last_calibration_date date [note: 'Date on which the soil temperature sensor was most recently calibrated. Used to assess reading reliability and trigger maintenance workflows when calibration intervals are exceeded.']
  latitude decimal(9,6) [note: 'Geographic latitude coordinate of the soil temperature sensor location in decimal degrees (WGS84). Supports GIS-based spatial analysis, precision agriculture mapping, and integration with Esri ArcGIS.']
  longitude decimal(9,6) [note: 'Geographic longitude coordinate of the soil temperature sensor location in decimal degrees (WGS84). Supports GIS-based spatial analysis, precision agriculture mapping, and integration with Esri ArcGIS.']
  measurement_interval_min varchar [note: 'Configured interval in minutes between successive soil temperature readings from this sensor. Common values: 15, 30, 60 minutes. Used to identify gaps in the time series and validate reading frequency against sensor configuration.']
  next_calibration_date date [note: 'Scheduled date for the next sensor calibration. Supports preventive maintenance scheduling and ensures data quality compliance for crop insurance documentation and regulatory reporting.']
  planting_window_suitable boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the soil temperature at this reading meets the minimum threshold for planting the associated crop type. Derived from crop-specific germination temperature requirements. Supports planting window determination and field operations scheduling.']
  qc_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes added by automated QC processes or data stewards explaining quality flags, anomalies, or manual corrections applied to this reading. Supports audit trail and data governance review.']
  quality_flag varchar [note: 'Automated quality control flag applied during silver layer processing. PASS = no issues detected; RANGE_FAIL = value outside physically plausible range; SPIKE = sudden implausible change; FROZEN = sensor reporting constant value; DRIFT = gradual sensor degradation detected; MANUAL_OVERRIDE = value corrected by data steward.']
  reading_date date [note: 'Calendar date of the soil temperature reading (yyyy-MM-dd). Used for daily aggregation, GDD accumulation calculations, and planting window reporting without requiring timestamp precision.']
  reading_status varchar [note: 'Quality status of the soil temperature reading indicating whether the value is usable for agronomic decisions. \'valid\' = passed all QC checks; \'suspect\' = flagged for review; \'invalid\' = failed QC; \'missing\' = no data received; \'estimated\' = gap-filled or interpolated value.']
  reading_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The exact date and time (UTC) when the soil temperature measurement was recorded by the sensor or probe. Principal event timestamp for this observation. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  sensor_type varchar [note: 'Technology type of the soil temperature sensor. Determines measurement accuracy characteristics and calibration requirements. Common types: thermistor (most common in agricultural IoT), thermocouple, RTD (Resistance Temperature Detector), infrared, fiber optic.']
  soil_moisture_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Volumetric soil moisture content (%) captured as a co-reading from multi-parameter sensors at the same depth and timestamp. Contextualises soil temperature readings for irrigation scheduling and germination prediction. Null when sensor does not support moisture measurement.']
  soil_type_code varchar [note: 'USDA soil texture classification code for the measurement location (e.g., SaL = Sandy Loam, SiCL = Silty Clay Loam). Soil type affects thermal conductivity and temperature dynamics. Supports soil-adjusted agronomic modelling.']
  source_record_code varchar [note: 'Original record identifier from the upstream source system (e.g., Climate FieldView reading UUID, DTN feed record ID, John Deere Operations Center telemetry ID). Supports data lineage tracing and deduplication in the silver layer.']
  temperature_c decimal(6,2) [note: 'Measured soil temperature in degrees Celsius at the recorded depth. Principal quantitative measurement for this record. Used for GDD accumulation, seed germination thresholds, and soil biological activity assessment.']
  temperature_f decimal(6,2) [note: 'Measured soil temperature in degrees Fahrenheit at the recorded depth. Stored alongside Celsius value to support US agronomic reporting, crop insurance documentation, and FMIS integrations that operate in Fahrenheit.']

Critical for planting window determination, seed germination prediction, and soil biological activity assessment.'

[ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Af|Am|Aw|BSh|BSk|BWh|BWk|Cfa|Cfb|Cfc|Csa|Csb|Dfa|Dfb|Dfc|ET|EF — promote to reference product]']

  data_source varchar [note: 'Primary source system or data feed from which the underlying 30-year observations were aggregated to produce this normal. Supports data lineage and quality auditing.   frost_free_days_normal decimal(5,1) [note: '30-year average number of frost-free days in the growing season (between last spring frost and first autumn frost). Determines viable crop maturity window for variety selection.']

  humidity_normal_pct decimal(5,2) [note: '30-year average relative humidity percentage for the applicable month or season. Used for disease pressure modelling, spray window suitability, and ET calculations.']
  latitude decimal(9,6) [note: 'WGS-84 latitude of the weather station or zone centroid in decimal degrees. Used for GIS spatial analysis in Esri ArcGIS and for ET calculations requiring solar angle.']
  longitude decimal(9,6) [note: 'WGS-84 longitude of the weather station or zone centroid in decimal degrees. Used for GIS spatial analysis and solar radiation calculations.']
  month_number varchar [note: 'Calendar month (1=January through 12=December) to which this normal record applies. Null for seasonal or annual normal_type records.']
  noaa_climate_division varchar [note: 'NOAA-assigned climate division code (state + division number, e.g., \'IL01\') used to aggregate station data to regional climate normals. Supports WASDE regional yield estimation and USDA crop reporting district alignment.']
  normal_period_end_year varchar [note: 'The last calendar year of the 30-year baseline period used to compute this climate normal (e.g., 2020 for the 1991-2020 WMO normal period).']
  normal_period_start_year varchar [note: 'The first calendar year of the 30-year baseline period used to compute this climate normal (e.g., 1991 for the 1991-2020 WMO normal period).']
  normal_status varchar [note: 'Lifecycle status of this climate normal record. Active records are used for operational decisions; superseded records are retained for historical comparison and crop insurance documentation.']
  normal_type varchar [note: 'Temporal granularity of this climate normal record — monthly (one record per calendar month), seasonal (DJF/MAM/JJA/SON), or annual (full-year aggregate).']
  precip_days_normal decimal(5,1) [note: '30-year average number of days with measurable precipitation (≥0.25 mm) for the applicable month or season. Used for spray window planning and field operation scheduling.']
  precip_normal_mm decimal(8,2) [note: '30-year average total precipitation in millimetres for the applicable month or season. Baseline for irrigation scheduling, water resource planning, and crop insurance actuarial calculations.']
  published_date date [note: 'Date on which this climate normal record was officially published or made available for operational use. Used for version control and regulatory audit trails under FSMA and crop insurance documentation requirements.']
  quality_flag varchar [note: 'Quality control status of the climate normal record indicating whether the underlying 30-year observation series passed automated QC checks, was estimated via interpolation, or contains missing data gaps.']
  season_code varchar [note: 'WMO meteorological season code: DJF (December-January-February / Winter), MAM (March-April-May / Spring), JJA (June-July-August / Summer), SON (September-October-November / Autumn). Null for monthly or annual normal_type records.']
  snowfall_normal_mm decimal(7,2) [note: '30-year average total snowfall expressed as water equivalent in millimetres for the applicable month or season. Relevant for soil moisture recharge estimation and spring planting window forecasting.']
  solar_radiation_normal_mj_m2 decimal(7,2) [note: '30-year average incoming solar radiation in megajoules per square metre per day for the applicable month or season. Required input for FAO-56 Penman-Monteith ET calculations and NDVI baseline modelling.']
  temp_max_c decimal(5,2) [note: '30-year average of daily maximum temperatures in degrees Celsius for the applicable month or season. Used for heat stress thresholds and GDD upper-cap calculations.']
  temp_mean_c decimal(5,2) [note: '30-year average mean daily temperature in degrees Celsius for the applicable month or season. Core input for GDD accumulation norms and WASDE yield estimation.']
  temp_min_c decimal(5,2) [note: '30-year average of daily minimum temperatures in degrees Celsius for the applicable month or season. Critical for frost risk assessment and crop variety selection.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to this climate normal record in the data lakehouse. Tracks revisions from reprocessing, QC corrections, or source data updates.']
  wind_speed_normal_ms decimal(5,2) [note: '30-year average wind speed in metres per second at 2-metre height for the applicable month or season. Used in ET calculations, spray window assessments, and pesticide drift risk modelling per EPA REI guidelines.']
  wmo_station_number varchar [note: 'Official WMO 5- or 6-digit station identifier assigned by the World Meteorological Organization. Enables cross-referencing with NOAA NCEI, DTN, and international climate databases for data lineage and audit.']
  years_of_record varchar [note: 'Actual number of years of valid observational data used to compute this normal (may be less than 30 if data gaps exist). Values below 25 indicate reduced statistical confidence per WMO guidelines.']

  Note: 'Long-term climate normal record representing 30-year statistical baselines (WMO standard) for a weather zone or station. Stores monthly and seasonal averages for temperature (min/max/mean), precipitation, ET, frost dates (average first/last), GDD accumulation norms, and extreme event frequencies. Used as baseline for anomaly detection, crop variety selection, and WASDE yield estimation inputs.'
}

  longitude decimal(9,6) [note: 'Geographic longitude coordinate of the alert centroid or point of origin in decimal degrees (WGS84). Used in conjunction with latitude for GIS spatial analysis, field boundary intersection, and precision agriculture alert targeting.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional operational notes, observations, or context related to this weather alert.   nws_event_code varchar [note: 'The official National Weather Service (NWS) event identifier for this alert, used for cross-referencing with NWS public alert feeds, NOAA databases, and regulatory documentation. Enables traceability to the authoritative government weather alert record.']
  recommended_action varchar [note: 'Prescribed protective action recommended in response to this weather alert, such as deploy frost cloth, activate irrigation frost protection, delay spray application, evacuate field workers, or secure equipment. Sourced from FMIS decision support rules or NWS/DTN advisory guidance.']
  relative_humidity_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Forecast or observed relative humidity percentage at the time of alert issuance. Used in frost risk assessment (high humidity increases frost severity), spray window determination, and disease pressure prediction for Integrated Pest Management (IPM).']
  severity varchar [note: 'Severity tier of the weather alert following NWS standard classification. Advisory indicates conditions that may cause inconvenience; Watch indicates conditions are favorable for a hazard; Warning indicates a hazard is imminent or occurring; Emergency indicates an extreme, life-threatening event.']
  spray_window_open boolean [note: 'Indicates whether pesticide or fertilizer spray application is permissible during the alert period based on wind speed, temperature, humidity, and precipitation conditions. False indicates spray operations should be suspended per EPA application restrictions and Good Agricultural Practices (GAP).']
  start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The datetime when the hazardous weather conditions described in the alert are expected to begin or have begun. Used for scheduling protective actions such as frost cloth deployment, irrigation frost protection activation, and spray window closure.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Audit timestamp recording when this weather alert record was last modified in the data product. Tracks alert updates such as severity upgrades, zone expansions, or cancellations. Supports data lineage and FSMA compliance audit trails.']
  wind_speed_ms decimal(6,2) [note: 'Forecast or observed wind speed in metres per second at the time of alert issuance. Relevant for high wind alerts, spray window assessment, frost risk modification (wind reduces radiation frost risk), and wildfire smoke dispersion modeling.']

  Note: 'Official weather alert, warning, and frost/freeze advisory record issued by NWS, DTN, or internal farm management systems for a weather zone or field. Stores alert type (tornado, severe thunderstorm, flash flood, heat advisory, winter storm, high wind, frost/freeze advisory, wildfire smoke), alert severity (advisory/watch/warning/emergency), issuance and expiration datetime, affected geographic zone, predicted low temperature for frost events, frost probability, crop-specific vulnerability rating, recommended protective actions (including frost cloth, irrigation frost protection), alert source, and acknowledgment status. SSOT for all weather alert types including frost/freeze events, consolidating all alert lifecycle management in a single product.'
}

Table weather.sensor_calibration {
  sensor_calibration_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each sensor calibration record in the weather domain. Primary key for the sensor_calibration data product.']

Linking calibration records to the fixed asset enables maintenance cost capitalization vs expensing decisio']

  station_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the weather station at which the sensor is installed. Supports traceability of calibration records to a specific field location.']

  calibration_location varchar [note: 'Indicates where the calibration was physically performed. \'field_in_situ\' means the sensor was calibrated at its installed location; \'laboratory\' means it was removed and bench-tested; \'manufacturer_depot\' means returned to the OEM.']
  calibration_method varchar [note: 'The procedure or technique used to perform the calibration. \'field_comparison\' compares against a co-located reference sensor; \'laboratory_bench\' involves removal and bench testing; \'reference_standard\' uses a NIST-traceable reference instrument.']

  calibration_result varchar [note: 'Overall outcome of the calibration procedure. \'pass\' indicates sensor is within tolerance without adjustment; \'pass_with_adjustment\' indicates within tolerance after correction; \'fail\' indicates sensor could not be brought within tolerance and must be decommissioned or replaced.']
  calibration_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the calibration record. \'failed\' indicates the sensor did not meet tolerance after calibration and requires corrective action. \'overdue\' indicates the scheduled calibration date has passed without completion.']
  calibration_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Precise date and time at which the calibration procedure was executed, including timezone offset. Supports audit trail and regulatory documentation requirements.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this calibration record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and regulatory documentation requirements.']
  data_quality_impact_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the pre-calibration drift was significant enough to have materially impacted the quality of historical weather observations recorded since the last calibration. True triggers a data quality review and potential retroactive correction of affected records.']
  insurance_documentation_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this calibration record is required as supporting documentation for a crop insurance claim. When True, the record must be retained per USDA Risk Management Agency documentation requirements.']
  measurement_unit varchar [note: 'The unit of measure applicable to the pre-calibration, post-calibration, and reference standard readings. Ensures dimensional consistency across sensor types (e.g., °C for temperature, %RH for humidity, mm for precipitation). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: °C|%RH|mm|m/s|deg|m³/m³|W/m²|hPa|hours — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  next_calibration_date date [note: 'The date by which the next calibration of this sensor must be completed. Drives preventive maintenance scheduling, compliance monitoring, and automated overdue alerts. Calculated based on calibration interval policy.']
  out_of_tolerance_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the sensor reading remained outside the acceptable tolerance range after calibration adjustment. True triggers a corrective action workflow, sensor quarantine, and data quality review for affected historical observations. Critical for regulatory and insurance documentation.']
  post_calibration_error decimal(10,4) [note: 'Calculated difference between the post-calibration sensor reading and the reference standard reading. Confirms whether the calibration adjustment brought the sensor within acceptable tolerance.']
  post_calibration_reading decimal(10,4) [note: 'The sensor measurement value recorded immediately after the calibration adjustment was applied. Compared against the reference standard to confirm the sensor is within acceptable tolerance.']
  pre_calibration_error decimal(10,4) [note: 'Calculated difference between the pre-calibration sensor reading and the reference standard reading. Quantifies sensor drift prior to adjustment. Used for data quality assessment of historical weather observations.']
  pre_calibration_reading decimal(10,4) [note: 'The raw sensor measurement value recorded immediately before the calibration adjustment was applied. Used to quantify drift and assess data quality for historical observations.']
  reference_standard_reading decimal(10,4) [note: 'The measurement value recorded by the certified reference standard instrument at the time of calibration. Serves as the ground truth against which pre- and post-calibration readings are compared.']
  sensor_manufacturer varchar [note: 'Name of the manufacturer of the sensor instrument. Used for vendor management, warranty claims, and equipment lifecycle tracking.']
  sensor_model varchar [note: 'Model designation of the sensor instrument as specified by the manufacturer. Supports calibration procedure selection and spare parts management.']
  sensor_serial_number varchar [note: 'Manufacturer-assigned serial number of the sensor instrument. Used for equipment traceability, warranty management, and regulatory documentation. Aligns with SAP PM Equipment master serial number.']
  sensor_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the IoT field sensor or weather station instrument being calibrated. Determines applicable calibration standards, tolerance ranges, and measurement units. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: temperature|humidity|precipitation|wind_speed|wind_direction|soil_moisture|soil_temperature|solar_radiation|barometric_pressure|leaf_wetness — promote to reference product]']
  technician_certification_number varchar [note: 'Professional certification or qualification number of the calibration technician. Validates that the individual performing calibration meets required competency standards per ISO/IEC 17025.']
  technician_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the technician who performed the calibration. Retained for regulatory documentation and audit purposes where a named individual must be identified on calibration certificates.']
  tolerance_lower_limit decimal(10,4) [note: 'The minimum acceptable deviation from the reference standard reading. If the post-calibration reading falls below this limit, the sensor is flagged as out-of-tolerance and requires corrective action.']
  tolerance_upper_limit decimal(10,4) [note: 'The maximum acceptable deviation from the reference standard reading. If the post-calibration reading exceeds this limit, the sensor is flagged as out-of-tolerance and requires corrective action.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this calibration record was last modified. Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.']
  work_order_number varchar [note: 'SAP Plant Maintenance (PM) work order number associated with this calibration event. Provides traceability to the maintenance planning and cost tracking system.']

  Note: 'Calibration and maintenance record for IoT field weather sensors and weather station instruments. Stores sensor identifier, calibration date, calibration method, pre/post calibration readings, acceptable tolerance range, calibration technician, next scheduled calibration date, and out-of-tolerance flag. Ensures data quality and traceability for regulatory and insurance documentation purposes.'
}

  notes varchar [note: 'Additional notes, comments, or observations recorded by adjusters, underwriters, or agents during the claim lifecycle.']
  payment_date date [note: 'The date on which the claim payout was issued to the policyholder.']
  reinsurance_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this claim is subject to reinsurance arrangements. True if reinsurance applies, False otherwise.']
  reported_date date [note: 'The date on which the claim was first reported to the insurance carrier or agent.']
  supporting_documentation varchar [note: 'References to supporting documents submitted with the claim (e.g., photos, weather reports, yield records, receipts). Stored as file paths or document identifiers.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this claim record was last modified in the system. Follows format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  yield_loss_percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'The percentage of expected crop yield lost due to the insured event. Measured as a percentage (0-100).']

  Note: 'Master reference table for insurance_claim. Referenced by claim_id.'
}

Table weather.sensor {
  sensor_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for sensor']
  field_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the agricultural field or plot where the sensor is installed, linking sensor data to specific crop management zones.']
  parent_sensor_id varchar [note: 'Self-referencing FK on sensor (parent_sensor_id)']
  weather_station_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the weather station or field location where this sensor is deployed, enabling grouping of sensors by site.']
  accuracy_rating decimal(5,2) [note: 'Manufacturer-specified accuracy rating of the sensor expressed as a percentage or tolerance value, indicating the precision of measurements.']
  calibration_interval_days varchar [note: 'Number of days between required calibration services as specified by manufacturer recommendations or internal quality standards.']
  communication_protocol varchar [note: 'Network protocol or technology used by the sensor to transmit data to collection systems or gateways.']

  elevation_meters decimal(8,2) [note: 'Height above sea level in meters at which the sensor is installed, important for atmospheric pressure and temperature adjustments.']
  firmware_version varchar [note: 'Version number of the firmware software running on the sensor device, important for compatibility and security updates.']
  health_status varchar [note: 'Assessment of the sensors technical health based on diagnostic checks, data quality metrics, and performance indicators.']
