  organic_certified_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this product is certified organic under the USDA National Organic Program (NOP). True = NOP-certified organic product. Drives labeling requirements, premium pricing, and supply chain segregation from conventional products.']
  packaging_type varchar [note: 'Type of packaging used for this product at the sellable unit level (e.g., bulk, bag, box, crate, pallet, drum). Drives warehouse storage configuration, shipping requirements, and labeling compliance. Aligned with SAP MM packaging data and Manhattan Associates WMS container types. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: bulk|bag|box|crate|pallet|drum|tote|carton|bottle|pouch — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  plu_code varchar [note: '4- or 5-digit Price Look-Up (PLU) code assigned to fresh produce and bulk agricultural commodities for retail checkout identification. Managed by the International Federation for Produce Standards (IFPS).']
  product_category varchar [note: 'Second-level product hierarchy classification (e.g., Grains & Oilseeds, Fresh Produce, Dairy, Poultry, Beef, Pork, Fiber Crops, Horticultural Products, Seeds, Fertilizers). Used for reporting, pricing, and supply chain segmentation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: grains_oilseeds|fresh_produce|dairy|poultry|beef|pork|fiber_crops|horticultural|seeds|fertilizers — promote to reference product]']
  product_line varchar [note: 'Named product line or portfolio grouping to which this product belongs (e.g., Organic Harvest Line, Premium Grain Series, Non-GMO Select). Supports marketing segmentation, pricing strategy, and customer account management.']
  product_name varchar [note: 'The full commercial or trade name of the agricultural product as it appears on labeling, sales orders, and customer-facing documents. Aligned with SAP MM material description field.']
  product_subcategory varchar [note: 'Third-level product hierarchy classification providing granular segmentation within a product category (e.g., within Grains: Corn, Wheat, Soybeans, Rice; within Fresh Produce: Leafy Greens, Root Vegetables, Citrus). Supports detailed analytics and procurement planning.']
  product_type varchar [note: 'High-level classification of the agricultural product type distinguishing between raw commodities (grains, produce, fiber), processed goods, seed/input products, livestock-derived items (meat, dairy, eggs), value-added products, and agricultural inputs (fertilizers, chemicals). Drives linkage to type-specific detail tables.']
  shelf_life_days varchar [note: 'Maximum shelf life of the product in days from the date of production or harvest under standard storage conditions. Used for inventory rotation (FEFO - First Expired First Out), expiry date calculation, and food safety compliance per FSMA requirements.']
  sku varchar [note: 'Internal Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) code uniquely identifying a specific product variant for inventory tracking, order management, and warehouse operations. Corresponds to SAP MM material number used in WMS and ERP transactions.']
  standard_cost decimal(18,4) [note: 'Standard cost per base unit of measure used for inventory valuation, variance analysis, and COGS (Cost of Goods Sold) calculation. Set during annual cost roll-up in SAP CO module. Confidential as it reflects internal pricing strategy and margin structure.']
  storage_temp_max_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Maximum permitted storage temperature in degrees Celsius for maintaining product quality and safety. Exceeding this threshold triggers quarantine hold procedures in the WMS and quality management system.']
  storage_temp_min_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Minimum required storage temperature in degrees Celsius for maintaining product quality and safety. Used by Manhattan Associates WMS for cold chain storage zone assignment and temperature monitoring compliance.']
  unit_of_measure varchar [note: 'Base unit of measure (UOM) for this product used in inventory management, purchasing, and sales transactions. Aligned with SAP MM base unit of measure (MEINS). Common agricultural units include BU (Bushel), CWT (Hundredweight), MT (Metric Ton), KG (Kilogram), LB (Pound). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: KG|LB|MT|BU|CWT|EA|CS|BAG|TON|L|GAL — 11 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  upc varchar [note: '12-digit Universal Product Code (UPC) barcode identifier used for retail point-of-sale scanning, consumer packaging, and retail distribution. Required for products sold through retail channels.']
  usda_commodity_code varchar [note: 'Official USDA commodity classification code used for federal reporting, subsidy programs, crop insurance, and WASDE (World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates) alignment. Maps to USDA Agricultural Marketing Service commodity codes.']
  valuation_class varchar [note: 'SAP MM valuation class code that determines the G/L (General Ledger) account assignment for inventory postings. Controls how inventory value is recorded in financial accounting (FI module) and cost accounting (CO module). Critical for COGS (Cost of Goods Sold) and inventory valuation reporting.']

  Note: 'Central master catalog and SSOT for all sellable, transferable, and internally consumed agricultural products. Every product in the enterprise — whether a raw commodity packaged for sale, a processed good, a seed variety, a livestock-derived item, or an agricultural input — has exactly one product_master record. Captures SKU, PLU, UPC, GTIN codes, product hierarchy classification, brand, product line, net weight, packaging type, shelf life, storage requirements (temperature range, humidity, light sensitivity), and product lifecycle status (active, discontinued, seasonal). Distinguishes between conventional, organic (NOP-certified), and non-GMO product lines. Type-specific detail is held in linked detail tables (seed_variety, livestock_product, processed_good, input_product). Aligned with SAP S/4HANA Material Master (MM module).'
}

True = COOL labeling required on all products in this node; False = COOL not required. Drives labeling compliance workflows and retail packaging requirements.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this product hierarchy node record was first created in the system. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and Silver Layer ingestion tracking. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']

  effective_to_date date [note: 'Date after which this product hierarchy node is no longer valid for new product assignments. Null indicates an open-ended, currently active node. Supports hierarchy versioning and ensures products are not assigned to expired classification nodes.']

  gmo_classification varchar [note: 'Indicates the Genetically Modified Organism (GMO) status applicable to products in this hierarchy node. Values: GMO (contains genetically modified material), Non-GMO (no GMO material, not certified), GMO-Free Certified (third-party verified non-GMO), Not Applicable (e.g., agrochemicals). Required for COOL labeling, USDA BE (Bioengineered) disclosure, and export documentation.']
  gpc_brick_code varchar [note: 'GS1 Global Product Classification (GPC) Brick-level code for this hierarchy node. Enables standardized product categorization for retail trading partners, EDI transactions, and global supply chain interoperability. Particularly relevant for produce, dairy, and packaged goods nodes.']
  grading_standard_code varchar [note: 'USDA Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) grading standard code applicable to products in this hierarchy node (e.g., US No. 1, US Grade A, USDA Choice). Governs quality grading, inspection requirements, and grade-based pricing. Used in SAP QM quality inspection and COA documentation.']
  haccp_applicable_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP) plans are required for products in this hierarchy node. True = HACCP plan mandatory (e.g., meat, poultry, juice, seafood); False = HACCP not required. Drives food safety program assignment and FSIS/FDA audit requirements.']
  hazmat_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether products in this hierarchy node are classified as hazardous materials requiring special handling, storage, and transportation documentation (e.g., certain agrochemicals, fertilizers). True = HAZMAT classification applies; False = standard handling. Drives SDS (Safety Data Sheet) requirements and DOT/EPA compliance.']
  hierarchy_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this hierarchy node. Corresponds to the SAP S/4HANA PRODH (Product Hierarchy) field used in SD pricing and MM material classification. Used for cross-system integration with SAP, Oracle NetSuite, and Granular Farm Management.']
  hierarchy_description varchar [note: 'Detailed business description of this hierarchy node, including the scope of products it encompasses, applicable production methods, and any relevant regulatory or quality notes. Used in training materials, data catalogs, and business user documentation.']
  hierarchy_level varchar [note: 'Numeric depth of this node within the hierarchy tree.   hierarchy_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable name of this hierarchy node (e.g., \'Grains & Oilseeds\', \'Fresh Produce\', \'Dairy Products\', \'Crop Inputs - Seed\'). Used in reporting, category management, and retail planogram structures.']
  hierarchy_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of this product hierarchy node.   organic_eligible_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether products classified under this hierarchy node are eligible for USDA National Organic Program (NOP) organic certification.   phi_required_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) tracking is required for products in this hierarchy node. True = PHI compliance mandatory (food/feed crops subject to pesticide application); False = PHI not applicable. Drives crop protection event tracking and harvest scheduling compliance.']
  plu_category_code varchar [note: 'International Federation for Produce Standards (IFPS) Price Look-Up (PLU) category code for fresh produce hierarchy nodes.   pricing_uom varchar [note: 'Unit of measure used for pricing and invoicing products in this hierarchy node. May differ from reporting UOM (e.g., corn priced per BU but reported in MT). Drives SAP S/4HANA SD condition record pricing and Oracle NetSuite invoice generation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: BU|CWT|MT|LB|KG|TON|DOZ|EA|GAL|L — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  product_line_type varchar [note: 'High-level classification of the product line represented by this hierarchy node. Distinguishes between Crop Commodity (grains, produce, fiber), Livestock Product (meat, dairy, eggs), Processed Good, Seed Input, Value-Added, and Agrochemical product lines. Drives business rules, compliance requirements, and reporting segmentation.']
  reporting_uom varchar [note: 'Primary unit of measure used for volume and yield reporting for products in this hierarchy node. Aligned with USDA NASS and WASDE reporting conventions. BU = Bushel, CWT = Hundredweight, MT = Metric Ton, LB = Pound, KG = Kilogram, TON = Short Ton, DOZ = Dozen, EA = Each, GAL = Gallon, L = Liter.   retail_category_code varchar [note: 'Internal retail category management code used for merchandising, planogram assignment, and retail buyer reporting.   sap_material_group varchar [note: 'SAP S/4HANA Material Group (MATKL field) associated with this hierarchy node.   usda_commodity_code varchar [note: 'Official USDA commodity classification code assigned to this hierarchy node.   Note: 'Defines the multi-level classification hierarchy for all agricultural products — from enterprise product division down through category, sub-category, product family, and individual SKU.   seed_treatment_active_ingredient varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of active ingredients (AI) in the seed treatment formulation (e.g., \'clothianidin, metalaxyl, fludioxonil\'). Required for MRL compliance, EPA registration cross-reference, and FSMA produce safety rule documentation.']

  trait_package varchar [note: 'Descriptive label of the bundled biotechnology or conventionally bred trait stack applied to this variety (e.g., \'RoundupReady2Xtend + Bollgard3\', \'Enlist E3\', \'LibertyLink GT27\').   variety_code varchar [note: 'Internally assigned alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the seed variety in ERP and FMIS systems (e.g., SAP S/4HANA material master number or Trimble Ag Software variety code). Used as the business key for cross-system integration and SKU linkage.']

  product_name varchar [note: 'The registered commercial or trade name of the agricultural input product as it appears on the EPA label or manufacturer documentation (e.g., \'Roundup PowerMAX\', \'Urea 46-0-0\', \'Rhizobium inoculant\').']

Active = currently approved and available for procurement/application; Discontinued = no longer available; Pending Registration = awaiting EPA or regulatory approval; Suspended = temporarily withdrawn; Under Review = regulatory re-evaluation in progress.']
  registrant_name varchar [note: 'The name of the company or entity holding the EPA registration for this pesticide product, as listed in the EPA Pesticide Registration database. The registrant is legally responsible for label compliance and product efficacy claims.']
  registration_expiry_date date [note: 'The date on which the EPA registration for this pesticide product expires or is subject to re-registration review. Products with expired registrations cannot be legally sold or applied. Triggers procurement and compliance alerts in the FMIS.']
  resistance_group varchar [note: 'The resistance management group designation (e.g., IRAC Group 4A, FRAC Group 11, HRAC Group 2) used for rotation planning under Integrated Pest Management (IPM) programs to prevent or delay development of resistance in target pest populations.']
  restricted_entry_interval_hours decimal(5,1) [note: 'The minimum number of hours that workers must wait before entering a treated field after application of this pesticide product, as specified on the EPA-registered label. Mandatory for OSHA Worker Protection Standard (WPS) compliance and farm safety programs.']
  restricted_use_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this product is classified as a Restricted Use Pesticide (RUP) by the EPA, requiring purchase and application only by certified pesticide applicators or persons under their direct supervision. True = RUP; False = General Use.']
  sds_reference varchar [note: 'The document reference number or URL pointing to the current Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for this input product, as required under OSHA Hazard Communication Standard (HazCom 2012) and GHS. The SDS must be accessible to all workers handling the product.']
  shelf_life_months varchar [note: 'The manufacturer-specified shelf life of this input product in months from the date of manufacture, under recommended storage conditions. Used for inventory rotation (FIFO), expiry date management in the WMS, and procurement planning.']
  signal_word varchar [note: 'The EPA-mandated signal word appearing on the pesticide product label indicating the acute toxicity hazard level to humans: DANGER (Toxicity Category I - most toxic), WARNING (Category II), CAUTION (Category III), NONE (Category IV - least toxic). Required for SDS documentation and worker safety training.']
  storage_temperature_max_c decimal(5,1) [note: 'The maximum storage temperature in degrees Celsius for this input product as specified by the manufacturer or SDS. Defines upper thermal limit for warehouse storage zone assignment and cold chain compliance monitoring.']
  storage_temperature_min_c decimal(5,1) [note: 'The minimum storage temperature in degrees Celsius for this input product as specified by the manufacturer or SDS. Used to define cold chain and warehouse storage zone requirements in the WMS and to prevent product degradation or hazardous conditions.']
  un_number varchar [note: 'The four-digit UN number (e.g., UN1993, UN2902) assigned by the United Nations Committee of Experts on the Transport of Dangerous Goods for this hazardous input product. Required on shipping labels, placards, and Bill of Lading (BOL) for DOT-regulated transport.']

  Note: 'Master catalog of all agricultural input products procured and applied in farm operations — fertilizers (NPK formulations, micronutrients, lime), crop protection chemicals (herbicides, fungicides, insecticides, nematicides), adjuvants, soil amendments, biological inoculants, and seed treatments. Captures active ingredient (AI), EPA registration number, SDS reference, MRL thresholds (linked to mrl_threshold), PHI (Pre-Harvest Interval), REI (Restricted Entry Interval), restricted use pesticide (RUP) flag, signal word, formulation type, application rate range, and organic-approved status (OMRI listing). Aligned with EPA FIFRA registration and USDA NOP compliance requirements. Links to product_master for SKU/procurement identity.'
}

Determines which products and operations are covered under this certificate.']
  certification_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the organic certification. Active: certificate is valid and in good standing. Suspended: temporarily halted pending investigation or corrective action. Revoked: permanently cancelled due to violation. Pending: application submitted, awaiting certifying agent approval. Expired: past expiration date without renewal. Withdrawn: voluntarily relinquished by the operation.']

COOL mandates disclosure of the country of origin for covered commodities at retail, and organic products must meet both NOP and COOL labeling requirements.']
  country_of_origin varchar [note: 'Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code indicating the country where the certified organic product was produced or primarily grown. Required for COOL compliance and international organic equivalency agreements.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this organic certification record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail, data lineage tracking, and compliance record-keeping in the Databricks Silver Layer.']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date on which the organic certification becomes legally valid and binding. Marks the start of the certified period during which organic labeling claims and premium pricing are authorized.']

  expiration_date date [note: 'The date on which the organic certification expires and must be renewed to maintain organic status. Organic certificates are typically issued on an annual basis. Expiration triggers renewal workflow and may affect organic premium pricing eligibility.']
  fsma_compliant_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the certified organic operation is also compliant with applicable Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) rules, including the Produce Safety Rule and Preventive Controls for Human Food. Organic certification does not automatically confer FSMA compliance.']
  globalg_ap_certified_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the operation holds concurrent GLOBALG.A.P. (Global Good Agricultural Practices) certification in addition to USDA NOP organic certification. GLOBALG.A.P. certification is often required by major retail buyers and export markets.']
  gmo_free_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the certified operation and its products are verified as free from Genetically Modified Organisms (GMOs). USDA NOP prohibits the use of excluded methods including genetic engineering; this flag confirms GMO-free status as part of organic compliance.']
  international_equivalency_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this certification is recognized under an international organic equivalency arrangement (e.g., USDA-EU Organic Equivalency Agreement, USDA-Canada Organic Equivalency Arrangement). Enables certified organic products to be sold as organic in partner countries without additional certification.']
  last_inspection_date date [note: 'Date of the most recent on-site inspection conducted by the certifying agent at the certified operation. Annual on-site inspections are required under USDA NOP to verify compliance with organic standards.']
  last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this organic certification record was most recently modified. Tracks changes to certification status, renewal events, suspension/revocation actions, and document updates for audit and compliance purposes.']
  next_inspection_date date [note: 'Scheduled date for the next on-site inspection by the certifying agent. Used for compliance planning and operational readiness to ensure the operation is prepared for the annual NOP inspection.']
  nop_system_plan_reference varchar [note: 'Document reference number or identifier for the Organic System Plan (OSP) submitted to and approved by the certifying agent. The OSP is the foundational compliance document describing all practices, materials, and monitoring activities for the certified operation.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional remarks, conditions, or special provisions associated with this organic certification record. May include certifying agent conditions, corrective action requirements, or operational notes relevant to compliance management.']
  operation_name varchar [note: 'The legal name of the certified organic operation (farm, ranch, or handling facility) as it appears on the organic certificate. This is the entity name recognized by the certifying agent and USDA NOP for compliance purposes.']
  operation_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the certified organic operation type. Producer: farms and ranches growing organic crops or raising organic livestock. Handler: facilities processing or packaging organic products. Broker: entities buying and selling organic products. Importer: entities importing certified organic products. Distributor: entities distributing certified organic products.']
  organic_label_type varchar [note: 'The USDA NOP-defined organic labeling category authorized for products under this certification. 100_percent_organic: all ingredients are certified organic. Organic: at least 95% certified organic ingredients. Made_with_organic: 70-95% certified organic ingredients. Organic_ingredients: less than 70% organic, may list specific organic ingredients. Determines permissible label claims and USDA Organic Seal usage.']
  premium_pricing_eligible_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether products covered by this certification are currently eligible for organic premium pricing in sales and distribution channels. Eligibility requires active certification status and valid organic label type authorization.']
  renewal_due_date date [note: 'The deadline by which the annual renewal application and supporting documentation must be submitted to the certifying agent to maintain uninterrupted organic certification status.']
  revocation_date date [note: 'The date on which the organic certification was permanently revoked by the certifying agent. Populated only when certification_status is \'revoked\'. Revocation is the most severe enforcement action and prohibits the operation from making organic claims.']
  revocation_reason varchar [note: 'Narrative description of the reason for permanent revocation of the organic certification. Documents the specific violation or fraudulent activity that resulted in the certifying agent revoking the certificate.']
  suspension_date date [note: 'The date on which the organic certification was suspended by the certifying agent. Populated only when certification_status is \'suspended\'. Suspension may result from non-compliance findings, use of prohibited substances, or failure to submit required documentation.']
  suspension_reason varchar [note: 'Narrative description of the reason for suspension of the organic certification. Documents the specific non-compliance finding or violation that triggered the suspension action by the certifying agent.']
  transition_complete_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the mandatory 36-month organic transition period has been completed for the land or operation covered by this certification. True indicates the operation has fulfilled the transition requirement and is eligible for full organic certification.']
  transition_start_date date [note: 'The date on which the operation began the mandatory 36-month transition period required before land can be certified organic under USDA NOP. During transition, no prohibited substances may be applied to the land.']

  Note: 'Tracks USDA National Organic Program (NOP) organic certification records for products, product lines, and production operations. Captures certifying agent name, certificate number, certification scope (crops, livestock, handling/processing), certification effective date, expiration date, annual renewal status, allowed materials list, and any suspension or revocation events. Links products to their certified organic status and supports COOL and organic labeling compliance. Required for organic premium pricing and retail organic claims.'
}

Table product.grading_standard {

[ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: US No. 1|US No. 2|US No. 3|US Extra Fancy|USDA Prime|USDA Choice|USDA Select|US Grade A|US Grade B|US Grade C — promote to reference product]']

  inspection_frequency varchar [note: 'Required frequency of grading inspections for commodities subject to this standard (e.g., per lot, per shipment, per batch, periodic, continuous). Drives quality inspection scheduling in SAP QM and Manhattan WMS workflows.']
  last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this grading standard record was most recently modified. Used for change tracking, data synchronization with SAP QM, and regulatory audit trail maintenance.']
  moisture_content_max_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Maximum allowable moisture content (%) for a commodity to qualify for this grade designation. A critical grading criterion for grains and oilseeds per GIPSA standards. Exceeding this threshold results in grade reduction or rejection.']
  mrl_threshold_ppm decimal(10,4) [note: 'Maximum Residue Limit (MRL) threshold in parts per million (ppm) for pesticide or chemical residues applicable to this grading standard. Compliance with MRL is required for grade certification and export eligibility per EPA and Codex Alimentarius standards.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional remarks, special conditions, or clarifications related to this grading standard (e.g., seasonal applicability, regional exceptions, special handling requirements). Used by quality and compliance teams.']
  organic_eligible_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this grading standard is applicable to USDA National Organic Program (NOP) certified organic products. When True, the standard supports organic product line quality certification and COA generation.']
  publication_date date [note: 'Date on which this grading standard was officially published in the Federal Register or by the administering agency. Distinct from the effective date; used for regulatory audit trails and compliance documentation.']
  regulation_citation varchar [note: 'Official regulatory citation for the grading standard, including CFR title, part, and section (e.g., \'7 CFR Part 26\', \'7 CFR Part 868\', \'9 CFR Part 319\'). Required for COA generation and FSMA compliance documentation.']
  serious_defects_max_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Maximum allowable percentage of serious defects (e.g., heat-damaged kernels, mold, insect damage) permitted for this grade. Serious defects are a distinct sub-category of total defects with stricter tolerance limits per GIPSA standards.']
  size_requirement varchar [note: 'Size specification or size range required for this grade designation (e.g., minimum diameter in mm, weight per unit, count per carton). Applies to produce, eggs, and livestock products per USDA AMS grading standards.']
  standard_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the grading standard (e.g., \'USDA-GR1-CORN\', \'AMS-EF-APPLE\'). Used as the business key for cross-system reference and COA generation.']
  standard_document_url varchar [note: 'URL link to the official published grading standard document on the administering agency\'s website (e.g., USDA AMS, GIPSA). Provides direct access to the authoritative source document for quality inspectors and compliance teams.']
  standard_name varchar [note: 'Full descriptive name of the grading standard as published by the administering agency (e.g., \'United States Standards for Grades of Corn\', \'USDA Extra Fancy Grade for Apples\'). Used in COA documentation and quality inspection workflows.']
  standard_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the grading standard. \'active\' indicates the standard is currently in force; \'superseded\' indicates replaced by a newer version; \'withdrawn\' indicates no longer applicable; \'draft\' or \'pending\' indicates under review or awaiting official publication.']
  superseded_by_code varchar [note: 'Standard code of the newer grading standard that replaces this record when status is \'superseded\'. Enables forward navigation in the version chain for compliance and historical reporting.']
  test_weight_min_lbs_bu decimal(5,2) [note: 'Minimum test weight in pounds per bushel (lbs/bu) required for a grain or oilseed commodity to qualify for this grade. Test weight is a key GIPSA grading factor reflecting grain density and quality.']
  total_defects_max_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Maximum allowable percentage of total defects (damaged kernels, heat damage, broken kernels, etc.) permitted for this grade designation. Applies to grain, oilseed, and produce grading per GIPSA and AMS standards.']
  usda_commodity_code varchar [note: 'Official USDA commodity code associated with this grading standard, enabling alignment with USDA AMS, GIPSA, and WASDE reporting systems. Used for regulatory reporting and supply chain traceability.']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Version or revision number of the grading standard as published by the administering agency (e.g., \'1.0\', \'2023\', \'3\'). Supports audit trails and historical compliance verification.']

  Note: 'Reference catalog of all applicable grading standards and grade specifications for agricultural commodities and products. Captures USDA grade designation (e.g., US No. 1, US Extra Fancy, USDA Prime), commodity type, grading criteria (moisture content, test weight, foreign material tolerance, defect limits), applicable regulation citation, effective date, and administering agency (AMS, FSIS, GIPSA). Supports quality inspection workflows and COA generation. Aligned with USDA AMS and GIPSA official grade standards.'
}

Table product.mrl_threshold {
  mrl_threshold_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique system-generated identifier for each MRL threshold record in the regulatory reference catalog. Primary key for this table.']
  active_ingredient_cas_number varchar [note: 'CAS Registry Number uniquely identifying the pesticide active ingredient chemical substance. Enables unambiguous cross-referencing across regulatory databases and SDS documentation.']
  active_ingredient_name varchar [note: 'Common or IUPAC chemical name of the pesticide active ingredient (AI) for which the MRL is established. Used to cross-reference against agrochemical product labels and COA verification.']
  analytical_method_reference varchar [note: 'Reference to the validated analytical method (e.g., AOAC, EN, EPA method number) used for laboratory detection and quantification of the residue to verify compliance with this MRL. Supports COA and laboratory accreditation alignment.']
  application_method varchar [note: 'Method of pesticide application for which this MRL tolerance is established (e.g., foliar spray, soil application, seed treatment, post-harvest treatment, fumigation). Affects residue behavior and PHI calculation.']
  codex_reference_number varchar [note: 'Official Codex Alimentarius MRL reference number (CXL number) for this tolerance, enabling direct cross-reference to the Codex MRL database. Used for international trade documentation and export COA verification.']
  commodity_code varchar [note: 'Standardized commodity classification code from USDA or Codex Alimentarius commodity classification system. Used for regulatory reporting, export documentation, and WASDE alignment.']
  commodity_group varchar [note: 'Broader commodity group classification under which the specific commodity falls (e.g., cereal grains, fruiting vegetables, root and tuber vegetables, meat and poultry). Supports group tolerance application per EPA and Codex rules.']
  commodity_name varchar [note: 'Name of the agricultural commodity or commodity group to which the MRL applies (e.g., wheat grain, fresh tomatoes, beef muscle). Aligned with USDA commodity codes and Codex commodity classifications.']
  commodity_part varchar [note: 'Specific part of the commodity to which the MRL applies (e.g., whole commodity, edible portion only, peel, grain, muscle tissue, fat, liver, milk, eggs). Relevant for processed commodity tolerances and animal product MRLs. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: whole_commodity|edible_portion|peel|seed|grain|muscle|fat|liver|kidney|milk|eggs — 11 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this MRL threshold record was first created in the system. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and Silver layer ingestion tracking per Databricks Lakehouse governance standards.']
  data_source varchar [note: 'Originating regulatory database or system from which this MRL record was sourced (e.g., EPA Office of Pesticide Programs tolerance database, Codex MRL database, EU Pesticides database). Supports data lineage and refresh cycle management.']
  default_mrl_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this MRL is a default/general tolerance applied in the absence of a specific established tolerance (e.g., Codex default of 0.01 ppm, EU default of 0.01 ppm under Regulation EC 396/2005). True = default MRL applies; False = specific established tolerance.']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date on which this MRL tolerance became legally effective and enforceable by the regulatory jurisdiction. Used to determine applicability for current crop season compliance and PHI scheduling.']
  epa_registration_number varchar [note: 'EPA pesticide registration number associated with the active ingredient or product formulation. Links MRL tolerance to the registered pesticide product for PHI compliance and export documentation.']
  exemption_reason varchar [note: 'Regulatory justification for a tolerance exemption, applicable when tolerance_type is \'exemption\'. Describes why the active ingredient is exempt from MRL requirements (e.g., naturally occurring substance, minimal risk, biochemical pesticide). Null for non-exemption tolerance types.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'Date on which this MRL tolerance expires or is scheduled for revocation. Null for indefinite tolerances. Critical for time-limited emergency exemptions (Section 18) and temporary import tolerances.']
  federal_register_citation varchar [note: 'U.S. Federal Register citation (volume, page number, and date) for the EPA final rule establishing or amending this tolerance. Provides regulatory traceability for audit and legal compliance purposes.']
  gmo_applicability_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this MRL tolerance specifically applies to or was established in the context of GMO crop varieties (e.g., herbicide-tolerant GMO crops with higher herbicide residue tolerances). True = GMO-specific tolerance; False = applies to conventional and GMO equally.']
  import_tolerance_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this MRL was established specifically as an import tolerance to facilitate trade for commodities treated with a pesticide not registered domestically. True = import tolerance; False = domestic tolerance. Relevant for FOB/CIF export documentation.']
  jurisdiction_country_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code for the importing or regulating country associated with this MRL. Used for export eligibility checks and Country of Origin Labeling (COOL) compliance. Null for multi-country jurisdictions (e.g., EU, Codex).']
  last_reviewed_date date [note: 'Date on which this MRL record was last reviewed and confirmed against the authoritative regulatory source database. Supports data quality management and ensures currency of compliance reference data.']
  last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this MRL threshold record was most recently modified. Used for incremental data refresh, change detection, and regulatory data currency validation in the Databricks Silver layer.']
  limit_of_quantification_ppm decimal(10,6) [note: 'Lowest concentration of the active ingredient residue that can be reliably quantified by the validated analytical method. Used to determine whether a non-detect result constitutes MRL compliance, particularly for default MRL tolerances.']
  mode_of_action_code varchar [note: 'IRAC (Insecticide Resistance Action Committee), FRAC (Fungicide Resistance Action Committee), or HRAC (Herbicide Resistance Action Committee) mode of action classification code for the active ingredient. Supports IPM resistance management planning.']
  mrl_value_ppm decimal(10,4) [note: 'The established maximum residue limit expressed in parts per million (ppm, equivalent to mg/kg) for the active ingredient on the specified commodity. Core compliance threshold used for COA verification, pre-harvest interval enforcement, and export eligibility determination.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional regulatory notes, conditions, or qualifications associated with this MRL tolerance (e.g., specific use restrictions, footnotes from regulatory publications, pending review status, or special conditions for application).']
  organic_approved_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the active ingredient is approved for use in certified organic production under USDA National Organic Program (NOP) standards. True = approved for organic use; False = not approved. Supports organic product line compliance and NOP certification maintenance.']
  phi_days varchar [note: 'Minimum number of days required between the last pesticide application and harvest to ensure residues do not exceed the MRL at time of harvest. Critical for crop protection scheduling and FSMA compliance. Sourced from EPA label requirements.']
  processing_factor decimal(8,4) [note: 'Ratio of residue concentration in the processed commodity to residue concentration in the raw agricultural commodity (RAC). Used to calculate MRL compliance for processed food products derived from the raw commodity. Values >1 indicate concentration; values <1 indicate reduction.']
  regulatory_jurisdiction varchar [note: 'The regulatory authority or jurisdiction that established this MRL (e.g., US_EPA for United States Environmental Protection Agency, EU for European Union Regulation EC 396/2005, CODEX for Codex Alimentarius Commission). Critical for export documentation and multi-market compliance. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: US_EPA|EU|CODEX|CANADA|JAPAN|AUSTRALIA|CHINA|BRAZIL|MEXICO|KOREA|INDIA|TAIWAN — promote to reference product]']
  residue_definition varchar [note: 'Regulatory definition of what constitutes the measurable residue for enforcement purposes, including parent compound and relevant metabolites or degradation products. Critical for laboratory COA analysis method alignment.']
  revocation_date date [note: 'Date on which a previously established MRL tolerance was formally revoked or cancelled by the regulatory authority. Null for active tolerances. Supports historical compliance audit trails and COA re-verification.']
  source_record_reference varchar [note: 'Native record identifier from the originating regulatory database (e.g., EPA tolerance petition number, Codex CXL reference, EU database entry ID). Enables traceability back to the authoritative source system for audit and refresh purposes.']
  tolerance_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the MRL tolerance record: \'active\' for currently enforceable tolerances, \'revoked\' for cancelled tolerances, \'expired\' for time-limited tolerances past their expiry date, \'pending\' for proposed tolerances under regulatory review, \'suspended\' for temporarily suspended tolerances.']
  tolerance_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the MRL tolerance type: \'established\' for standard EPA/Codex tolerances, \'exemption\' for active ingredients exempt from tolerance requirements, \'import_tolerance\' for tolerances set specifically for imported commodities, \'emergency_exemption\' for Section 18 emergency use tolerances, \'group_tolerance\' for tolerances covering a commodity group.']

  Note: 'Reference table of Maximum Residue Limits (MRL) for pesticide active ingredients (AI) on specific agricultural commodities by regulatory jurisdiction. Captures active ingredient name, EPA registration number, commodity or commodity group, MRL value (ppm), regulatory jurisdiction (US EPA, EU, Codex Alimentarius, importing country), effective date, and tolerance type (established, exemption, import tolerance). Critical for pre-harvest interval (PHI) compliance, export documentation, and COA verification. Sourced from EPA and Codex Alimentarius databases.'
}

Captures bundle name, bundle type (fixed, configurable), bundle pricing method (sum of components, discounted package, flat rate), minimum order quantity, availability period, and target customer segment. Includes component-level detail: individual component products (FK to product_master), quantity per bundle, unit of measure, substitution allowed flag, component-level pricing contribution, and component sequence/priority. Supports decomposition of bundle orders into individual product fulfillment lines and component-level inventory reservation. Enables value-added selling programs, input supply dealer agreements, and crop input financing packages.'
}

Table product.bundle_component {
  bundle_component_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each bundle component association record within the agricultural product catalog. Primary key for this entity.']
  bundle_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the parent bundle product (e.g., a seed+fertilizer+crop protection kit, or a livestock feed package) that contains this component. Links to the product catalog master record for the bundle.']
  master_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the individual component product (e.g., a specific seed variety, agrochemical, fertilizer, or feed ingredient) that is included within the parent bundle. Links to the product catalog master record for the component.']
  primary_bundle_substitute_product_master_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the approved substitute product that may replace this component when substitution_allowed_flag is True and the primary component is unavailable. Enables pre-approved substitution workflows in warehouse fulfillment and order management.']
  coa_required_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a Certificate of Analysis (COA) must accompany this component when fulfilling bundle orders. Applicable for seed lots, agrochemicals, and food-grade agricultural inputs requiring quality documentation per GFSI, SQF, or BRC standards.']
  component_quantity decimal(18,6) [note: 'The quantity of this component product included in one unit of the parent bundle. Supports fractional quantities for bulk commodities (e.g., 2.5 kg of seed per bundle, 0.5 L of agrochemical per kit). Used for inventory reservation and fulfillment decomposition.']
  component_sequence varchar [note: 'Numeric ordering position of this component within the bundle, used for display sequencing, picking order in warehouse fulfillment, and structured bill-of-materials presentation. Aligns with SAP BOM item number sequencing.']
  component_sku varchar [note: 'The Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) code for this component as it appears within the bundle context. May differ from the standalone product SKU when the component is packaged or sized differently for bundle inclusion (e.g., a smaller pack size of seed included in a starter kit bundle).']
  component_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of this bundle component association: active (currently included in bundle), inactive (temporarily excluded), discontinued (permanently removed from bundle), or pending_approval (awaiting quality or regulatory review before activation).']
  component_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the component\'s role within the bundle: primary (core required component), optional (customer-selectable add-on), promotional (included for marketing purposes), sample (trial quantity), or freebie (complimentary item). Drives fulfillment logic and revenue recognition treatment.']
  component_uom varchar [note: 'Unit of measure for the component quantity within the bundle (e.g., KG for kilograms, BU for bushels, L for liters, EA for each). Aligns with USDA commodity measurement standards and SAP base unit of measure configuration. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: KG|LB|MT|CWT|BU|L|ML|EA|BAG|TON|OZ|GAL — promote to reference product]']
  component_volume_l decimal(18,6) [note: 'The volume of this component in liters as included in the bundle, used for packaging dimension calculations, storage space planning, and container load optimization. Particularly relevant for liquid agrochemicals, fertilizer solutions, and liquid feed supplements.']
  component_weight_kg decimal(18,6) [note: 'The gross weight of this component in kilograms as included in the bundle, used for total bundle weight calculation, freight cost estimation, shipping label generation, and logistics planning. Aligns with SAP material master weight data.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this bundle component association record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for audit trail, data lineage, and SOX financial reporting controls.']
  effective_end_date date [note: 'The date after which this component is no longer valid within the bundle. Null indicates an open-ended association with no planned expiry. Used for seasonal bundle management, promotional period control, and regulatory compliance (e.g., MRL threshold changes requiring bundle reformulation).']
  effective_start_date date [note: 'The date from which this component is valid and active within the bundle. Supports seasonal agricultural product bundles (e.g., spring planting kits) and time-bound promotional bundles. Aligns with SAP validity period configuration.']
  fulfillment_split_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this component may be fulfilled separately from other bundle components (True) or must be shipped together with all other components in a single shipment (False). Supports split-shipment scenarios for agricultural bundles where seed and agrochemicals may ship from different warehouses.']
  gmo_status varchar [note: 'Indicates the GMO status of this component within the bundle: gmo (contains genetically modified organisms), non_gmo (does not contain GMOs but not certified), gmo_free_certified (third-party certified non-GMO), or not_applicable (for non-biological components). Required for COOL labeling and USDA reporting.']
  hazmat_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this component is classified as a hazardous material requiring special handling, storage, and shipping documentation (e.g., certain agrochemicals, pesticides, or fertilizers). Triggers HAZMAT compliance workflows in logistics and warehouse operations.']
  inventory_reservation_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether inventory for this component should be reserved at the component level upon bundle order placement (True) or managed at the bundle level only (False). Drives Manhattan Associates WMS inventory reservation logic for component-level stock allocation.']
  last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this bundle component association record was most recently modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change tracking, data synchronization with SAP S/4HANA and Oracle NetSuite, and audit compliance.']
  lead_time_days varchar [note: 'The procurement or production lead time in days for this component, used for bundle availability planning and supply chain scheduling. Critical for seasonal agricultural inputs where seed, fertilizer, and crop protection products must be available before planting windows.']
  mandatory_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this component is mandatory for the bundle to be valid and fulfillable. True = component must be present for bundle fulfillment; False = component is optional and may be excluded. Distinct from substitution_allowed_flag which governs product swaps rather than component inclusion.']
  max_quantity decimal(18,6) [note: 'The maximum quantity of this component that may be included in the bundle, applicable for variable-quantity bundles. Enforces upper limits for regulatory compliance (e.g., maximum agrochemical quantity per bundle per EPA/MRL restrictions) and inventory allocation controls.']
  min_quantity decimal(18,6) [note: 'The minimum quantity of this component that must be included in the bundle, applicable for variable-quantity bundles where customers may select quantities within a defined range (e.g., minimum 1 bag of seed per bundle). Used in order validation and fulfillment planning.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional operational notes, special handling instructions, or agronomic guidance specific to this component within the bundle context (e.g., \'Apply within 48 hours of seed treatment\', \'Store separately from fertilizer\', \'Requires cold chain handling\'). Not for regulatory documentation.']
  organic_certified_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this specific component within the bundle is certified organic under the USDA National Organic Program (NOP). Critical for maintaining bundle-level organic certification integrity — all mandatory components must be organic-certified for the bundle to carry an organic label.']
  pricing_contribution_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'The monetary value attributed to this component within the overall bundle price, representing the component\'s share of the bundle\'s total selling price. Used for revenue allocation, cost-of-goods-sold (COGS) decomposition, and component-level profitability analysis.']
  pricing_contribution_currency varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the component pricing contribution amount (e.g., USD, EUR, CAD). Supports multi-currency agricultural commodity trading and international supply chain operations.']
  pricing_contribution_pct decimal(7,4) [note: 'The percentage of the total bundle price attributable to this component, expressed as a decimal percentage (e.g., 35.50 for 35.5%). Used alongside the absolute pricing contribution amount for proportional revenue recognition and margin analysis per component.']
  quantity_variable_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the component quantity within the bundle is fixed (False) or variable/customer-selectable (True) within the min/max quantity bounds. Supports configurable agricultural input bundles where farmers select quantities based on acreage or herd size.']
  regulatory_approval_required_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this component requires specific regulatory approval or certification before it can be included in a bundle for sale (e.g., EPA-registered pesticides, USDA-approved seed varieties, FDA-regulated food additives). Triggers compliance review workflows.']
  sort_order varchar [note: 'The display sort order for this component in customer-facing product catalogs, sales order entry screens, and bundle configuration interfaces. Distinct from component_sequence which governs fulfillment/picking order; sort_order governs presentation layer ordering.']
  storage_compatibility_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the storage compatibility class of this component, used to ensure incompatible components within a bundle are not co-located in warehouse storage (e.g., separating oxidizers from flammables, or keeping seed away from agrochemicals). Aligns with EPA and OSHA storage segregation requirements.']
  substitution_allowed_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this component may be substituted with an alternative product during order fulfillment when the primary component is out of stock or unavailable. True = substitution permitted; False = component is mandatory and cannot be substituted. Supports Manhattan Associates WMS substitution logic.']

  Note: 'Association table capturing the individual component products within each product bundle, including component product reference, quantity per bundle, unit of measure, substitution allowed flag, and component-level pricing contribution. Enables decomposition of bundle orders into individual product fulfillment lines and supports component-level inventory reservation. Carries its own business data (quantity, pricing contribution) beyond the simple M:N relationship.'
}

Table product.substitution_rule {
  substitution_rule_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique system-generated identifier for the product substitution rule record. Primary key for the substitution_rule data product in the SAP S/4HANA MM material substitution configuration context.']
  facility_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the SAP S/4HANA plant (production facility, grain elevator, processing plant, or distribution center) where this substitution rule is applicable. Null indicates the rule applies enterprise-wide across all plants.']
  master_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the primary agricultural product or commodity (e.g., grain, produce, livestock product, seed input) that is subject to substitution when unavailable or constrained. Links to product.product_master.']
  primary_substitution_substitute_product_master_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the approved substitute agricultural product or commodity that can replace the primary product in order fulfillment, procurement, or feed formulation scenarios. Links to product.product_master.']
  sales_organization_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the SAP S/4HANA sales organization for which this substitution rule is valid in order fulfillment scenarios. Null indicates applicability across all sales organizations.']
  approval_authority varchar [note: 'Name or role of the business authority (e.g., Procurement Manager, Quality Assurance Director, Feed Nutritionist) who approved this substitution rule. Supports audit trail and regulatory compliance documentation.']
  approval_date date [note: 'Date on which the substitution rule was formally approved by the designated approval authority. Required for regulatory audit trails under FSMA and GLOBALG.A.P. compliance frameworks.']
  auto_substitution_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the system (SAP S/4HANA MM) may automatically apply this substitution rule without manual intervention when the trigger condition is met. False requires a planner or procurement officer to manually confirm the substitution.']
  coa_required_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a Certificate of Analysis (COA) must accompany the substitute product shipment to validate quality equivalency with the primary product. Supports GFSI, SQF, and BRC compliance requirements.']
  cool_country_of_origin varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code indicating the country of origin of the substitute product for COOL (Country of Origin Labeling) compliance. May differ from the primary product\'s origin and must be disclosed to customers and on product labels.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this substitution rule record was first created in the system. Provides audit trail for data governance and regulatory compliance documentation.']
  customer_acceptance_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether explicit customer approval must be obtained before applying this substitution in a sales order fulfillment context. True requires customer confirmation; False allows automatic substitution. Relevant for COOL and customer contract compliance.']
  customer_group_restriction varchar [note: 'Identifies a specific customer segment or customer group (e.g., food manufacturers, retail chains, export accounts) for which this substitution rule is restricted. Null means the rule applies to all customers. Aligns with Salesforce CRM customer segmentation.']
  effective_date date [note: 'Calendar date from which this substitution rule becomes valid and may be applied in order fulfillment, procurement, or feed formulation. Aligns with SAP S/4HANA MM validity start date for material substitution.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'Calendar date after which this substitution rule is no longer valid. Null indicates an open-ended rule with no planned expiration. Used to manage seasonal and emergency substitution windows.']
  fsma_traceability_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this substitution triggers additional traceability documentation requirements under the FDA Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) Food Traceability Rule (Section 204). True requires lot-level tracking and Key Data Elements (KDEs) to be captured.']
  gap_compliant_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the substitution maintains compliance with Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) standards for both the primary and substitute products. Required for GLOBALG.A.P. certification maintenance and USDA GAP audit readiness.']
  grade_equivalency_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the substitute product meets the same USDA grading standard as the primary product (True = grade-equivalent substitution). Used in quality assurance workflows and COA documentation to confirm substitution does not downgrade product quality.']
  last_review_date date [note: 'Date on which this substitution rule was most recently reviewed and confirmed by the approval authority. Used to trigger review reminders and compliance audit checks.']
  last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this substitution rule record was most recently modified. Supports change management, audit trail, and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.']
  max_substitution_qty decimal(18,4) [note: 'Maximum quantity of the substitute product (in the defined unit of measure) that may be applied under this rule per order or procurement event. Prevents over-substitution and supports supply chain planning constraints.']
  mrl_compliant_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the substitute product meets the same Maximum Residue Limit (MRL) thresholds as the primary product for pesticide and agrochemical residues. Required for food safety compliance under FDA, EPA, and Codex Alimentarius standards.']
  non_gmo_equivalency_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the substitute product maintains the same non-GMO (Genetically Modified Organism) status as the primary product. Critical for non-GMO product lines and customer labeling commitments under USDA BE (Bioengineered) disclosure rules.']
  organic_equivalency_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the substitute product maintains the same organic certification status as the primary product under USDA National Organic Program (NOP). True means both products are NOP-certified organic; False means organic status differs and substitution may affect labeling.']
  price_differential_pct decimal(8,4) [note: 'Percentage difference in standard cost between the substitute product and the primary product (positive = substitute is more expensive, negative = substitute is cheaper). Used in procurement cost impact analysis and COGS (Cost of Goods Sold) variance reporting.']
  priority_rank varchar [note: 'Numeric ranking (1 = highest priority) used to sequence multiple approved substitutes for the same primary product. Determines which substitute is selected first when multiple substitution rules are active simultaneously in SAP S/4HANA MM.']
  quantity_conversion_factor decimal(18,6) [note: 'Numeric multiplier applied to the primary product quantity to determine the equivalent substitute quantity (e.g., 1.05 means 5% more substitute is needed per unit of primary). Accounts for grade equivalency differences in weight, volume, or nutritional value.']
  regulatory_restriction_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this substitution is subject to regulatory restrictions (e.g., USDA, FDA, EPA, APHIS import/export controls, or state-level agricultural regulations) that limit when or where the substitute product may be used.']
  review_frequency_days varchar [note: 'Number of days between mandatory periodic reviews of this substitution rule to confirm continued validity, regulatory compliance, and business relevance. Supports governance and GLOBALG.A.P. continuous improvement requirements.']
  rule_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this substitution rule, used in SAP S/4HANA MM material substitution configuration and cross-referenced in procurement and order fulfillment workflows.']
  rule_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the substitution rule governing whether it may be applied in fulfillment or procurement operations. Active rules are eligible for automatic or manual substitution; suspended rules require review before use.']
  substitution_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text business justification describing why this substitution rule was established (e.g., \'Corn No. 2 Yellow substituted for Corn No. 1 Yellow during Q4 harvest shortfall; grade equivalency confirmed by QA\'). Supports audit documentation and supply chain resilience planning.']
  substitution_scope varchar [note: 'Business process context in which this substitution rule is applicable: order_fulfillment (sales order dispatch), procurement (purchase order sourcing), feed_formulation (livestock nutrition ingredient swap), or all (unrestricted across all processes).']
  substitution_type varchar [note: 'Categorical classification of the substitution relationship: equivalent_grade (same quality tier, different lot/source), approved_alternative (customer or regulatory pre-approved swap), emergency (supply disruption-driven), seasonal (crop availability-driven), feed_formulation (ingredient swap in livestock nutrition plans). Drives workflow routing in SAP S/4HANA MM.']
  supply_constraint_trigger varchar [note: 'Business condition that activates this substitution rule: stock_shortage (inventory below reorder point), seasonal_unavailability (crop not in season), quality_hold (primary product under quarantine), supplier_disruption (vendor supply failure), price_threshold (cost exceeds approved ceiling). Drives automated substitution logic in SAP S/4HANA MM.']
  unit_of_measure varchar [note: 'Standard unit of measure applicable to the quantity conversion factor for this substitution rule. Uses agricultural industry standard units: BU (Bushel), MT (Metric Ton), CWT (Hundredweight), KG, LB, L (Litre), GAL (Gallon), EA (Each). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: BU|MT|CWT|KG|LB|L|GAL|EA — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']

  Note: 'Defines approved product substitution and equivalency rules specifying which products can replace another in order fulfillment, procurement, or formulation scenarios due to supply constraints, grade equivalency, seasonal unavailability, or customer-approved alternatives. Captures primary product, substitute product, substitution type (equivalent grade, approved alternative, emergency, seasonal), approval authority, customer acceptance required flag, effective date range, and priority ranking when multiple substitutes exist. Supports supply chain resilience, order fulfillment flexibility, and feed formulation ingredient substitution. Aligned with SAP S/4HANA MM material substitution configuration.'
}

  export_restriction_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this product is subject to export restrictions from the domestic market to the specified jurisdiction. True when export is restricted or prohibited; False when export is permitted. Critical for export compliance and trade documentation.']

Table product.seed_supply_agreement {
  seed_supply_agreement_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the seed_supply_agreement association']
  seed_variety_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the seed variety being supplied under this agreement']
  vendor_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the vendor authorized to supply the seed variety under this agreement']
  agreement_end_date date [note: 'Date on which this vendor-variety supply agreement expires or is terminated. Null if the agreement is open-ended or currently active without a fixed end date.']
  agreement_start_date date [note: 'Date on which this vendor-variety supply agreement becomes effective. Required for tracking agreement history and seasonal renewals.']
  certification_status varchar [note: 'Current certification or authorization status of this supply agreement (e.g., ACTIVE, PENDING_REVIEW, SUSPENDED, EXPIRED). Tracks the lifecycle state of the vendor\'s authorization to supply this specific variety.']
  contracted_volume decimal [note: 'Total quantity of this seed variety the vendor is contracted to supply under this agreement for the specified season and region. Belongs to the agreement, not to the variety catalog or vendor master.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the price_per_unit in this supply agreement. May differ from the vendor\'s default invoicing currency for cross-border regional agreements.']
  exclusivity_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this vendor holds an exclusive supply right for this seed variety within the specified supply_region and supply_season. An exclusive agreement prevents other vendors from being authorized for the same variety-region-season combination.']
  price_per_unit decimal [note: 'Agreed contracted price per unit of seed (e.g., per bag, per cwt) for this vendor-variety combination in this season. Price varies by vendor, variety, and season and belongs to the agreement, not to either master record.']
  supply_region varchar [note: 'Geographic region or territory within which the vendor is authorized to supply this seed variety under this agreement (e.g., state code, USDA zone, or named sales territory).']
  supply_season varchar [note: 'The growing or crop year season for which this supply agreement is active (e.g., \'2024_SPRING\', \'2024_FALL\'). Agreements are typically renewed or renegotiated each season.']
  volume_uom varchar [note: 'Unit of measure for contracted_volume (e.g., BAG, CWT, LB, UNIT). Seed volume UOM varies by crop species and packaging convention.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Contract between seed_variety and vendor. It captures the formal supply arrangement under which a specific vendor is authorized to supply a specific seed variety for a given growing season and region. Each record links one seed_variety to one vendor with attributes — pricing, contracted volume, supply region, exclusivity, and certification status — that exist only in the context of this vendor-variety supply relationship and cannot be attributed to either the seed variety catalog or the vendor master alone.. Existence Justification: In agricultural seed procurement, a seed variety can be supplied by multiple vendors (seed companies, licensed distributors, regional dealers), and a single vendor typically supplies many seed varieties across their product portfolio. The business actively manages these supply relationships as formal agreements — tracking contracted volumes, pricing, supply regions, and growing seasons — making this a genuine operational M:N relationship, not an analytical correlation. Agriculture businesses explicitly manage \'which vendors are authorized to supply which varieties, under what terms\' as a named procurement concept (Seed Supply Agreement).'
}

Table product.crop_label_registration {

Drives crop-specific application compliance and MRL tracking. Sourced from the EPA-registered label. [Moved from agrochemical_product: This STRING field is a denormalized, comma-separated list of commodity crops for which the agrochemical is registered. It encodes the M:N relationship in a non-relational way. The proper model is to decompose this into individual crop_label_registration records, one per agrochemical-commodity pairing, each carrying the crop-specific application parameters.   pre_harvest_interval_days varchar [note: 'The minimum number of days that must elapse between the last application of this agrochemical and harvest of this specific commodity crop. PHI is crop-specific and belongs to the registration pairing, not to the agrochemical product alone.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the formal EPA Crop Label Registration (Contract) between agrochemical_product and commodity. It captures the regulatory approval of a specific agrochemical product for use on a specific commodity crop, including the label-defined application parameters that are unique to each agrochemical-commodity pairing. Each record links one agrochemical_product to one commodity and carries the application rate, pre-harvest interval, seasonal application limits, and approved method that govern compliant use under FSMA, EPA, and GLOBALG.A.P. requirements.. Existence Justification: In agricultural operations, the EPA formally registers specific pesticide-crop combinations, meaning a single agrochemical product is approved for use on multiple commodity crops, and a single commodity crop has multiple agrochemical products registered for use on it. This regulatory approval — known as a crop label registration or crop use registration — carries its own data (application rate, PHI days, seasonal application limits, application method) that belongs to neither the agrochemical product nor the commodity alone, but to the specific pairing. The business actively manages these registrations for FSMA, EPA, and GLOBALG.A.P. compliance, making this a genuine operational M:N relationship.'
}

Table product.agrochemical_practice_compatibility {
  agrochemical_practice_compatibility_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the agrochemical_practice_compatibility association']
  agrochemical_product_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the agrochemical product whose compatibility with a regenerative practice is being defined']
  regenerative_practice_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the regenerative practice for which the agrochemical compatibility rule applies']
  applicable_crop_type varchar [note: 'The specific crop type or commodity group for which this compatibility rule applies. A single agrochemical-practice pairing may have different rules depending on the crop context, making this a relationship-level attribute.']
  compatibility_status varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the agrochemical product is compatible, conditionally compatible, restricted, or prohibited for use in the context of the linked regenerative practice. This status cannot reside on either parent entity alone as it is specific to the pairing.']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date on which this compatibility rule became operationally effective. Required to track rule changes over time as EPA label revisions or carbon program updates alter compatibility status.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'The date on which this compatibility rule expires or is superseded. Supports temporal versioning of compatibility rules as regulations and program requirements evolve.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text agronomist notes or compliance annotations specific to this agrochemical-practice pairing, capturing nuances not expressible in structured fields.']
  restriction_type varchar [note: 'Specifies the nature of the restriction or condition governing use of the agrochemical product within the regenerative practice context (e.g., timing window restriction, buffer zone requirement, full prohibition). Belongs to the relationship as the same chemical may have different restriction types under different practices.']
  rule_source varchar [note: 'The authoritative source document or program that mandates or defines this compatibility rule (e.g., EPA label section, carbon program protocol version, GLOBALG.A.P. IFA checklist point). Supports audit and compliance traceability.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Compatibility Contract between agrochemical_product and regenerative_practice. It captures the operational compatibility and restriction rules that govern whether and how a specific agrochemical product may be used in the context of a specific regenerative agriculture practice. Each record links one agrochemical_product to one regenerative_practice with attributes — compatibility status, restriction type, applicable crop type, and effective date — that exist only in the context of this pairing and are actively managed by agronomists and compliance teams to satisfy EPA label requirements, carbon program rules, and GLOBALG.A.P. standards.. Existence Justification: In regenerative agriculture programs, agrochemical products and regenerative practices have explicit compatibility and restriction relationships that are actively managed by agronomists and compliance teams. A single regenerative practice (e.g., pollinator habitat establishment, cover cropping) restricts or conditionally permits multiple agrochemical products, while a single agrochemical product (e.g., a broad-spectrum herbicide) may be restricted or conditionally compatible with multiple regenerative practices. This relationship is operationally managed — agronomists create, update, and retire these compatibility rules as label registrations change, new practices are adopted, or carbon program requirements evolve.'
}

Table product.commodity_broker_authorization {
  commodity_broker_authorization_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the commodity_broker_authorization association']

Overrides the broker master\'s standard commission_rate_pct when a commodity-specific rate has been negotiated. Belongs to the authorization, not to either master entity, because the same broker may have different rates for corn vs. soybeans.']
  commodity_specializations varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of agricultural commodity types the broker is authorized and experienced to transact (e.g., corn, soybeans, wheat, cattle, hogs, fresh produce). Used for opportunity matching and compliance with USDA commodity-specific licensing requirements. [Moved from broker: This is a denormalized multi-value string field encoding the M:N broker-commodity relationship directly on the broker master record. Once the commodity_broker_authorization association is in place, each authorized commodity is represented as a proper row in the association table. The commodity_specializations field should be deprecated and removed from the broker master to eliminate the data integrity risk of a free-text multi-value field diverging from the structured authorization records.]']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date on which this broker-commodity authorization becomes legally effective and the broker is permitted to facilitate sales of this commodity.   exclusivity_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this broker holds exclusive rights to facilitate sales of this specific commodity within their geographic territory.   expiry_date date [note: 'Date on which this broker-commodity authorization expires or is terminated. Null indicates an open-ended authorization. Enables the enterprise to manage time-limited commodity authorizations independently of the broker\'s overall contract dates.']
  volume_target_mt decimal [note: 'Agreed annual commodity volume target in Metric Tons that the broker is expected to facilitate for this specific commodity under this authorization. Distinct from broker.annual_volume_target_mt which is an aggregate across all commodities. Belongs to the authorization because targets are negotiated per commodity.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the formal Commodity Brokerage Authorization contract between a commodity and a broker. It captures the specific terms under which a broker is authorized to facilitate sales of a particular agricultural commodity on behalf of the enterprise. Each record links one commodity to one broker and carries the commodity-specific commission rate, volume target, exclusivity arrangement, and authorization period — attributes that exist only in the context of this specific broker-commodity pairing and cannot reside on either the commodity or broker master record alone.. Existence Justification: In agricultural commodity brokerage, a broker specializes in and is authorized to sell multiple commodities (e.g., corn, soybeans, wheat), and each commodity is facilitated by multiple brokers across different territories and channels. This is an operationally managed relationship: the enterprise actively creates, maintains, and terminates broker-commodity authorization agreements that carry their own terms — commodity-specific commission rates, volume targets, exclusivity arrangements, and effective dates. The denormalized `commodity_specializations` field on the broker record is direct evidence that this M:N reality exists and is currently modeled incorrectly as a multi-value string.'
}

  agreement_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known, human-readable identifier for the pricing agreement as assigned by SAP S/4HANA SD or Salesforce CRM. Used in customer communications, contract references, and audit trails (e.g., PA-2024-00123).']
  agreement_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the pricing agreement. \'draft\' = under preparation; \'pending_approval\' = submitted for authorization; \'active\' = currently in force; \'suspended\' = temporarily halted; \'expired\' = past effective end date; \'terminated\' = cancelled before expiry.']
  agreement_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the pricing strategy governing this agreement. \'spot\' = current market price at time of transaction; \'forward\' = fixed price for future delivery; \'futures_linked\' = price tied to exchange futures contract (e.g., CBOT); \'contract\' = negotiated fixed-term contract price; \'index_based\' = price derived from a market index such as DTN or WASDE. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: BU|MT|CWT|LB|KG|TON|BBL|DOZ — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']

  bid_price decimal(18,6) [note: 'The price at which a buyer is willing to purchase the commodity per unit of measure on the price date. Used by sales teams for pricing validation, quote floor setting, and basis calculation. Expressed in the currency and unit of measure specified in this record.']

  price_source varchar [note: 'The originating data source or market feed from which this price record was obtained.   price_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the price observation indicating the commercial pricing mechanism. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: cash|futures|basis|fob|cif|forward|settlement — promote to reference product]']

  unit_of_measure varchar [note: 'The unit of measure in which the price is expressed.   updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this market price record was last modified or updated in the silver layer lakehouse (e.g., price correction, status change, source data revision). Used for change tracking, data quality monitoring, and audit compliance.']
  volume varchar [note: 'Total number of contracts or units traded for this commodity on the price date. Indicates market liquidity and trading activity. Used by sales and procurement teams to assess market depth and execution feasibility for large volume transactions.']
